chapters.title: Chapter 301: The Woman Who Once Loved a Hero Returns!
paragraphs: As the teams finally formed, the two sides stood apart from each other, with the Infernal Choir and the traitors gathered together on one side while everyone else assembled on the opposite side of the arena.
A feminine voice suddenly came from the Infernal Choir’s side.
"Lord Peiro."
The moment those words were spoken, everyone’s attention shifted toward the source of the voice.
It belonged to the leader of the Infernal Choir group, a woman who had reached the High B-rank.
Although her voice had been difficult to distinguish earlier, there was no mistaking it now.
It was unmistakably feminine, and she had directly addressed the blue spirit standing nearby.
’Peiro?’
Luke’s gaze shifted toward the blue spirit, who was now looking down at the leader of the Infernal Choir with a seemingly indifferent expression.
"What?"
At Peiro’s response, the woman slowly reached up and removed the upper portion of her robe, which had been concealing her face.
The fabric slid away.
And the moment her face was completely revealed, the atmosphere around them seemed to change.
Everyone’s expression turned to astonishment.
"So beautiful."
The words escaped from almost everyone’s mouth, including several of the Sunborn warriors. Even the representatives of Empyrean Academy stared at her in surprise, while the Elves were no different.
As for Luke—
’What the hell?’
He couldn’t help staring at her.
’How can anyone be this beautiful?’
Rather than being attracted to her beauty, Luke was simply stunned by it. He had seen beautiful women, but even among them, this woman stood out immediately.
Her hair was emerald green, but the lower portions gradually shifted into a deep purple, resembling poisonous venom.
Her eyes were equally unusual.
They were narrow and pointed like those of a serpent, with green pupils surrounded by bright purple irises that seemed to shimmer like distant starlight.
Her facial features were almost flawless, from the delicate shape of her face to her perfectly defined jawline and the red lips that completed her appearance.
Luke continued staring for a little too long, unconsciously comparing her beauty with that of every woman he had encountered.
After considering it carefully, he could only reach one conclusion.
She was definitely below the Saintess of Light in beauty.
However, she was still a level above Theia.
Unfortunately, Luke had forgotten one very important fact while making that comparison.
He wasn’t alone.
A chilling voice suddenly came from beside him, carrying enough jealousy to make it sound as though the person speaking was already imagining what his blood would taste like.
"She is beautiful?"
There was a brief pause.
"Right, darling?"
Luke froze.
Only then did he remember that Selene was standing beside him.
Because of the sudden reveal, he had completely forgotten about his surroundings and had stared at Brynessa for far too long.
So he slowly turned toward Selene.
She was smiling.
Her fangs, however, were already showing.
’She really wants to drink my blood.’
With this, omnious thought, Luke immediately put on a dignified expression.
"How could that be?"
He reached out, gently cupped Selene’s face, and looked directly into her eyes before speaking in a sincere and affectionate tone.
"For me, you’re the most beautiful woman in the world."
Selene’s smile remained.
In fact, it became slightly more satisfied.
She raised her hand and lightly, almost playfully, patted his cheek.
"Good. At least your eyes aren’t rotten like everyone else’s."
Luke quietly sighed in relief.
’That was close.’
Around them, however, the expressions of several representatives twitched.
They could clearly tell that Selene was mocking them.
Meanwhile, Alia, who would normally have been jealous upon seeing Luke and Selene behaving so affectionately, didn’t pay much attention to the couple this time.
Her focus remained entirely on Brynessa.
There was something familiar about that face.
Alia narrowed her eyes slightly as she searched through her memories, trying to determine where she had seen those features before.
Then, a memory suddenly surfaced.
"Her Highness... Brynessa?"
And those words left her mouth next moment.
So everyone who had been staring at Brynessa earlier, froze.
Their eyes widened.
Even Selene, Isaria, and Estelle showed surprise.
Only Luke remained completely clueless.
’What happened?’
He looked around, wondering why everyone had suddenly reacted so strongly.
Brynessa, who had been the one to call out to Peiro earlier, also raised an eyebrow in surprise when she heard her name.
However, the surprise lasted only briefly.
Her expression soon returned to normal, and she continued speaking to the blue spirit as though nothing had happened.
"Lord Peiro, I would like to use the last Champion Privilege to start the final round."
Her voice remained calm.
Then she announced the name of the privilege she intended to activate.
"WAR OF THE CHOSEN."
The moment those words echoed through the arena, the expressions of everyone on the opposing side changed.
Their eyes narrowed.
This was extremely disadvantageous for them.
Brynessa was a High B-rank, while the warriors on their side were only Early B-ranks.
Their original plan had been straightforward.
They would use their numerical advantage and overall quality to win the first two rounds. Even if they lost the third round, they would still secure victory overall.
But now everything had changed.
’Damn it.’
Estelle clenched her fist.
She could clearly see what Brynessa was trying to accomplish.
The woman wasn’t treating this as some ordinary competition anymore.
She was determined to kill them.
And that was exactly what made the situation so dangerous.
Meanwhile, Luke was still trying to understand what was going on, so he quietly asked Selene about Brynessa.
Selene had finally recovered from the shock of recognizing her and began explaining the story behind the Snake Princess.
She told Luke about how Brynessa had once fallen in love with a hero.
But that hero had rejected her.
Worse, he had mocked her for her feelings and eventually gone so far as to spread her private images, humiliating her in front of others.
Unable to endure what had happened to her, Brynessa had eventually taken her own life.
Luke listened silently as Selene explained the story.
"But now she is here."
Selene’s words eventually came to an end.
Luke’s expression changed slightly as he connected the story to something he had heard before in Stormveil County.
He remembered the conversation surrounding the real Snake Dance.
"So she’s that person?"
The words escaped his mouth after he finished thinking about her story.
He had once felt pity for the Snake Princess when he heard what had happened to her.
But seeing the same person alive and standing in front of him now, only to discover that she had become one of the villains opposing them, gave the story an entirely different feeling.
’What happened to her after that?’
The question immediately entered Luke’s mind.
One possibility came to him.
Perhaps she had made a deal with a demon, offering her soul in exchange for strength so that she could eventually take revenge on the hero who had destroyed her life.
’Maybe I’m thinking too much.’
Luke shook his head.
There was no point in making assumptions without knowing what had actually happened.
He turned his attention back toward Brynessa and Peiro.
"Hmm."
Peiro rubbed his chin thoughtfully for a few seconds before finally nodding.
"Okay. Since he has given you his emblem, you are fully eligible to activate his privilege."
The moment those words were spoken, everyone was suddenly teleported away.
The surroundings blurred for an instant before both sides reappeared in the spectator seats.
The two groups were seated on opposite sides, separated by the arena below them.
The arena itself stretched for roughly one hundred kilometers in diameter, yet the distance didn’t make it difficult for anyone to watch the battle.
Somehow, their vision had been enhanced by the Heaven’s Crucible.
Whenever they looked toward the opposite side, the figures sitting there appeared clearly, despite the enormous distance between them.
The same applied to the arena.
They could focus their vision on any particular section and zoom in, allowing them to observe the battle without missing the details.
"Nice feature."
Luke looked around with genuine appreciation.
The Heaven’s Crucible had clearly been designed with spectators in mind.
"You seem fine."
Selene’s voice came from beside him.
There was clear surprise in her tone.
After all, almost everyone else was worried about the upcoming fight, particularly because Brynessa was a High B-rank.
Luke, however, appeared completely relaxed.
He wasn’t nervous.
He simply sat there with the same relaxed smile on his face.
’Did he already give up?’
Selene studied his expression.
Then another thought occurred to her.
’Does he not know that after crossing early B-rank, beings can use Essentification?’
If Luke heard that thought, he would probably finally understand the strange transformation he had witnessed earlier in Marrec’s hands and legs.
Selene, however, didn’t know that.
’Maybe it’s better that he doesn’t know.’
She looked at him again before silently making up her mind.
’I will protect him.’
The thought strengthened her resolve.
"Huh?"
Luke noticed her expression and turned toward her.
She was looking at him with an unusually protective expression.
"What happened?"
He reached out and gently caressed her cheek.
Selene shook her head with a small smile.
"Nothing."
Before Luke could say anything else, movement appeared in the center of the arena.
Peiro materialized there, his figure clearly visible to everyone because of the enhanced vision provided by the Heaven’s Crucible.
He looked around at both sides before finally speaking in a loud voice that carried across the entire arena.
"Since the third round has been brought forward using Champion Privilege, the privilege side will not receive the buff options."
The Infernal Choir’s expressions remained unchanged.
They had clearly expected this.
Luke and the others, however, reacted differently.
Their expressions brightened slightly.
This restriction was actually beneficial to them.
If Brynessa wasn’t allowed to choose one of the available buffs, then at least one advantage had been removed from her side.
But Peiro wasn’t finished.
"Also, the Perfect State option, which restores all lost energy, health, and missing body parts after the battle, will be removed from this War of the Chosen round from both sides."
"What?!"
The moment those words ended, the expressions of everyone who had been feeling relieved immediately changed.
The situation had become far more dangerous.
Without the Perfect State restoration, every injury sustained during the battle would matter.
Every loss of energy would matter.
And if someone received an injury severe enough, they could no longer rely on the Heaven’s Crucible to restore them afterward.
That meant they would have to fight much more strategically and carefully.
More importantly, if they couldn’t surrender in time, they could actually die.
The representatives of Empyrean Academy, however, reacted differently.
Their expressions brightened.
Several of them looked toward Brynessa, who remained completely unbothered by the announcement.
"With this, we can tire her out."
Marius spoke with an excited expression.
The others nodded.
That was their plan.
They didn’t necessarily need to defeat Brynessa immediately.
If they could force her to fight repeatedly and gradually drain her energy, they might eventually create an opportunity to defeat her.
As the discussion continued among the representatives, Peiro finally raised his voice once again.
The arena gradually fell silent.
"The War of the Chosen has started."
His gaze moved toward both sides.
"Send your first warrior!"

chapters.title: Chapter 302: A Living Arena and a Vengeful Snake Princess
paragraphs: The moment those words were spoken, a brief silence settled over both groups as the fighters on either side looked toward each other, each waiting to see who would make the first move.

From Luke’s side, the representatives of Empyrean Academy didn’t move, apparently choosing to wait and see what the Infernal Choir would do first. Seeing this, Estelle finally decided to send one of her kingdom warriors into the arena.
"Bring victory to us."
She looked toward the warrior standing before her.
The man nodded firmly and struck his chest plate with his fist.
"Don’t worry, Princess."
His voice carried a firm resolve, and without wasting any more time, he jumped down from the spectator seat.
However, something unexpected happened the moment he did.
Instead of falling toward the arena, the space in front of him maginified, and in the next instant, he appeared at the exact center of the arena, standing an equal distance away from both sides.
No one among the spectators showed much surprise at the sight.
After what had happened earlier, they had already accepted that Peiro, the blue spirit of the Heaven’s Crucible, could freely manipulate space within this place.
Luke, however, noticed something that the others didn’t.
’Void movement?’
His eyebrow rose slightly in surprise as he carefully sensed what had just happened.

Earlier, when Peiro had transported everyone from one place to another, the process had happened too quickly for Luke to identify the exact method being used. This time, however, he had been paying attention from the beginning, and his newly awakened Void affinity allowed him to perceive those hidden spatial movement.
At that moment, the small figure of Sevaroth also materialized on Luke’s shoulder after previously retreating inside his body.
"You are right. It’s Void movement."
Sevaroth gave a small nod, confirming Luke’s guess.

Although Sevaroth wasn’t a Void Master like his brother Nyx, that didn’t mean his understanding of the Void was shallow. At his level, he had witnessed many delicate and concealed Void techniques, and he had also spent a long time observing Nyx and his methods.

Because of that, Sevaroth had a far deeper understanding of the hidden aspects of Void techniques than Luke currently possessed. Even if he wasn’t a master himself, there were likely many gods within Valtharion whose understanding of the Void couldn’t compare to his.
Hearing that, Luke paid even closer attention.

He rarely got the opportunity to receive direct explanations from his Titans, especially while his other three Titans were still sleeping, so he naturally didn’t want to miss anything Sevaroth had to say.
"This whole place is situated in the Void rather than on Valtharion."
However, Sevaroth’s next words, still caught Luke off guard.
’What?’
Sevaroth continued without immediately answering his surprise.
He also added, that earlier gate and that chamber location, Luke had told him, was the only place on Valtharion, but when they enter that Blue portal, they had came outside the Valtharion.
Upon this, Luke’s expression became thoughtful.
’Are we completely outside Valtharion, or only partially outside it?’
He asked the question immediately.
"Hmm."
Sevaroth slowly rubbed his chin helmet, apparently trying to find the simplest way to explain the situation.

"Well, you may already know that the Void doesn’t behave like normal space. It isn’t simply a larger empty area surrounding ordinary worlds. Within the Void, there can be multiple dimensions, and even entire realities connected through it."
Luke nodded.
That much made sense based on what he already knew.
Sevaroth continued.

"So, right now, we’re in a different dimension, another layer of space connected to the Void. As far as I can tell, that blue portal on Valtharion is the only entrance that allows access to this particular place."
Luke’s expression grew more serious.
"So, if there are other powerful beings present in this dimension, such as a Warden..."
He paused as he considered the possibility before shaking his head.
"Nah. If a Warden were here, it would already locate this place."
Sevaroth glanced around before adding,
"Unless this entire place is being hidden by another Warden... or perhaps a Void Warden."
He then gave Luke a more reassuring answer.
"And it’s seems, those beings didn’t, means, for now, this place is safe."
After saying that, however, Sevaroth revealed something even more surprising.
"Also, the entire Heaven’s Crucible is alive and Peiro is merely its outer manifestation."
Luke went quiet.
For several seconds, he simply tried to process what he had just heard.
The Heaven’s Crucible was alive?

Until now, Luke had assumed that this place was some kind of ancient artifact, a mysterious artifact that had existed for countless years, with Peiro being the consciousness that had developed within it.
But if Sevaroth was correct, then his entire understanding of the Heaven’s Crucible had been slightly wrong from the beginning.
The thought also reminded Luke of Kiki.
Sevaroth had created Kiki, and despite being created rather than naturally born, Kiki had born with consciousness.
’Does being a living artifact work differently from being born as an ordinary living being?’
So, this thought crossed his mind, and Luke instinctively felt that there was probably some distinction between the two, although he couldn’t explain exactly what it was.
Still, he didn’t ask Sevaroth about it.
There was another realization that was far more difficult to ignore.
’I am outside Valtharion.’
Luke’s eyes widened slightly at the thought.
He had spent so long thinking about spatial travel in terms of crossing distances between planets and worlds that the idea of simply leaving Valtharion through a portal felt almost absurd.
Rather than using some grand spatial ability to travel across an distance, he had essentially found a back door and walked through it.
’Let’s calm down.’
Luke quickly suppressed the excitement rising in his mind.
Even so, a small part of him was already wondering when he would finally be able to use his own Void abilities to travel between dimensions.
However, another question immediately surfaced.
’Sevaroth, did this place come into existence on its own, or was it created by someone?’
Sevaroth had been examining the cracks and strange beast-shaped markings spread across the dark walls, but when he heard Luke’s question, he turned toward him.
A faint smile appeared on his face.
"I don’t know."
Luke couldn’t hide the slight disappointment in his expression.
He had genuinely thought Sevaroth might know the answer.
"But," Sevaroth continued, "it could be either."
Luke’s disappointment only lasted for a brief moment before Sevaroth added something that made him pause again.
"But for your information, Caelith, at her peak, could create a place like this with a single thought."
Luke fell silent.
An image of Caelith immediately appeared in his mind.
He remembered her gentle smile, followed by the memory of her forging a Demigod weapon almost effortlessly and in an instant, even while she had still been in her weakened state.
"Seems like it." So, Luke slowly nodded.
That small movement, however, immediately attracted Selene’s attention.
"What happened?"
She looked at her husband with slight concern.
Luke had been behaving strangely for some time now.

Ever since their second meeting, she had noticed that there were moments when he would become lost in his own thoughts, but lately, he seemed to be doing it even more frequently. Even now, despite everything happening around them, he had once again become absorbed in some thought she couldn’t understand.
Then another possibility entered her mind.
’Is he thinking about Aurielle?’
Selene’s eyes narrowed.
The concern that had been present a moment earlier disappeared, replaced by another kind of determination.
’I have to make him addicted to me.’
With that thought, she leaned toward Luke and gave him a small peck on the lips.
"Ahem."
A cough immediately came from beside them.
Estelle, who was sitting nearby, turned her head slightly with an awkward expression, while Zeyr simply smiled.

A few of the others looked at them with obvious jealousy, while several more wore expressions of annoyance, as though silently asking why the couple couldn’t keep their affection to themselves for a few minutes.
"Should we focus on the fight?"
Arwen finally spoke from the side, his tone carrying clear discomfort.
Although he still didn’t particularly like working with Luke, there were only two sides in this round, so neither he nor Lirael had much choice but to join Luke’s group.
Hearing Arwen, everyone finally redirected their attention toward the arena.
Luke and Selene did the same, although by then the two were sitting considerably closer together than before, almost leaning into one another.
Their attention returned to the center of the arena, where the Infernal Choir had also sent one of the Sunborn Kingdom’s traitorous warriors into battle.
"Seems like both of your teams think the same."
Peiro, now floating above the arena, looked between the two fighters and casually made his comment.
With a small flick of his hand, the battle began.
The two warriors immediately moved toward each other.
As the fight unfolded below, Brynessa’s gaze remained fixed on Luke.
It wasn’t merely because of what had happened now.
She had been watching him ever since he first appeared before her.
There were several reasons for it.
The first was what Marrec had told her about Luke’s strength despite his relatively low realm.
And the second reason.
Even after learning that she, a High B-rank, was present, Luke had shown no fear.
Instead, he was busy acting lovey dovey with his wife.
’Love.’
The familiar yet distant word surfaced within Brynessa’s mind.
That single word was enough to stir memories she had buried long ago.
Memories of the time when she had once fallen in love with a hero.
An Elf hero.
Her gaze slowly shifted toward Arwen and Lirael.
They belonged to the same race as that man.
The memory of him rejecting her because of her lower snake body resurfaced, followed by the humiliation and suffering he had brought upon her.
’I will erase your entire race.’
Her eyes narrowed as that hatred rose again.
The people around her immediately noticed the subtle change in her expression.
At the same time, starlight-colored snake scales began appearing along her cheeks.
They spread gradually down toward her neck before continuing across her hands and legs, indicating that her transformation was beginning to surface once again.
However, before those changes could develop any further, another voice interrupted her thoughts.
"Miss?"
It was Mella, another black-robed member of the Infernal Choir.
Brynessa’s expression shifted slightly as she heard her.
Marrec also turned toward Brynessa, but the instant he looked at her, his gaze dropped.
There was unmistakable fear in his eyes.
Brynessa noticed neither reaction for long.
She took a slow breath and forced herself to calm down, causing the transformation to stop before it could progress further.
"I’m fine."
Her voice was calm, and she took another slow breath to completely settle her emotions.
Yet her gaze remained fixed on Luke.
Then Iveron’s words surfaced in her mind.
’A hero will never love you. They are merely tools used to increase their gods’ power, while you princes and princesses are nothing more than parts of that tool.’
The words lingered in her thoughts.
And at that moment—
BANG!
The battle below came to an abrupt end.

sentences.text: The moment those words were spoken, a brief silence settled over both groups as the fighters on either side looked toward each other, each waiting to see who would make the first move.
From Luke’s side, the representatives of Empyrean Academy didn’t move, apparently choosing to wait and see what the Infernal Choir would do first.
Seeing this, Estelle finally decided to send one of her kingdom warriors into the arena.
"Bring victory to us."
She looked toward the warrior standing before her.
The man nodded firmly and struck his chest plate with his fist.
"Don’t worry, Princess."
His voice carried a firm resolve, and without wasting any more time, he jumped down from the spectator seat.
However, something unexpected happened the moment he did.
Instead of falling toward the arena, the space in front of him maginified, and in the next instant, he appeared at the exact center of the arena, standing an equal distance away from both sides.
No one among the spectators showed much surprise at the sight.
After what had happened earlier, they had already accepted that Peiro, the blue spirit of the Heaven’s Crucible, could freely manipulate space within this place.
Luke, however, noticed something that the others didn’t.
’Void movement?’
His eyebrow rose slightly in surprise as he carefully sensed what had just happened.
Earlier, when Peiro had transported everyone from one place to another, the process had happened too quickly for Luke to identify the exact method being used.
This time, however, he had been paying attention from the beginning, and his newly awakened Void affinity allowed him to perceive those hidden spatial movement.
At that moment, the small figure of Sevaroth also materialized on Luke’s shoulder after previously retreating inside his body.
"You are right.
It’s Void movement."
Sevaroth gave a small nod, confirming Luke’s guess.
Although Sevaroth wasn’t a Void Master like his brother Nyx, that didn’t mean his understanding of the Void was shallow.
At his level, he had witnessed many delicate and concealed Void techniques, and he had also spent a long time observing Nyx and his methods.
Because of that, Sevaroth had a far deeper understanding of the hidden aspects of Void techniques than Luke currently possessed.
Even if he wasn’t a master himself, there were likely many gods within Valtharion whose understanding of the Void couldn’t compare to his.
Hearing that, Luke paid even closer attention.

He rarely got the opportunity to receive direct explanations from his Titans, especially while his other three Titans were still sleeping, so he naturally didn’t want to miss anything Sevaroth had to say.
"This whole place is situated in the Void rather than on Valtharion."
However, Sevaroth’s next words, still caught Luke off guard.
’What?’
Sevaroth continued without immediately answering his surprise.
He also added, that earlier gate and that chamber location, Luke had told him, was the only place on Valtharion, but when they enter that Blue portal, they had came outside the Valtharion.
Upon this, Luke’s expression became thoughtful.
’Are we completely outside Valtharion, or only partially outside it?’
He asked the question immediately.
"Hmm."
Sevaroth slowly rubbed his chin helmet, apparently trying to find the simplest way to explain the situation.
"Well, you may already know that the Void doesn’t behave like normal space.
It isn’t simply a larger empty area surrounding ordinary worlds.
Within the Void, there can be multiple dimensions, and even entire realities connected through it."
Luke nodded.
That much made sense based on what he already knew.
Sevaroth continued.
"So, right now, we’re in a different dimension, another layer of space connected to the Void.
As far as I can tell, that blue portal on Valtharion is the only entrance that allows access to this particular place."
Luke’s expression grew more serious.
"So, if there are other powerful beings present in this dimension, such as a Warden..."
He paused as he considered the possibility before shaking his head.
"Nah.
If a Warden were here, it would already locate this place."
Sevaroth glanced around before adding,
"Unless this entire place is being hidden by another Warden... or perhaps a Void Warden."
He then gave Luke a more reassuring answer.
"And it’s seems, those beings didn’t, means, for now, this place is safe."
After saying that, however, Sevaroth revealed something even more surprising.
"Also, the entire Heaven’s Crucible is alive and Peiro is merely its outer manifestation."
Luke went quiet.
For several seconds, he simply tried to process what he had just heard.
The Heaven’s Crucible was alive?

Until now, Luke had assumed that this place was some kind of ancient artifact, a mysterious artifact that had existed for countless years, with Peiro being the consciousness that had developed within it.
But if Sevaroth was correct, then his entire understanding of the Heaven’s Crucible had been slightly wrong from the beginning.
The thought also reminded Luke of Kiki.
Sevaroth had created Kiki, and despite being created rather than naturally born, Kiki had born with consciousness.
’Does being a living artifact work differently from being born as an ordinary living being?’
So, this thought crossed his mind, and Luke instinctively felt that there was probably some distinction between the two, although he couldn’t explain exactly what it was.
Still, he didn’t ask Sevaroth about it.
There was another realization that was far more difficult to ignore.
’I am outside Valtharion.’
Luke’s eyes widened slightly at the thought.
He had spent so long thinking about spatial travel in terms of crossing distances between planets and worlds that the idea of simply leaving Valtharion through a portal felt almost absurd.
Rather than using some grand spatial ability to travel across an distance, he had essentially found a back door and walked through it.
’Let’s calm down.’
Luke quickly suppressed the excitement rising in his mind.
Even so, a small part of him was already wondering when he would finally be able to use his own Void abilities to travel between dimensions.
However, another question immediately surfaced.
’Sevaroth, did this place come into existence on its own, or was it created by someone?’
Sevaroth had been examining the cracks and strange beast-shaped markings spread across the dark walls, but when he heard Luke’s question, he turned toward him.
A faint smile appeared on his face.
"I don’t know."
Luke couldn’t hide the slight disappointment in his expression.
He had genuinely thought Sevaroth might know the answer.
"But," Sevaroth continued, "it could be either."
Luke’s disappointment only lasted for a brief moment before Sevaroth added something that made him pause again.
"But for your information, Caelith, at her peak, could create a place like this with a single thought."
Luke fell silent.
An image of Caelith immediately appeared in his mind.
He remembered her gentle smile, followed by the memory of her forging a Demigod weapon almost effortlessly and in an instant, even while she had still been in her weakened state.
"Seems like it." So, Luke slowly nodded.
That small movement, however, immediately attracted Selene’s attention.
"What happened?"
She looked at her husband with slight concern.
Luke had been behaving strangely for some time now.
Ever since their second meeting, she had noticed that there were moments when he would become lost in his own thoughts, but lately, he seemed to be doing it even more frequently.
Even now, despite everything happening around them, he had once again become absorbed in some thought she couldn’t understand.
Then another possibility entered her mind.
’Is he thinking about Aurielle?’
Selene’s eyes narrowed.
The concern that had been present a moment earlier disappeared, replaced by another kind of determination.
’I have to make him addicted to me.’
With that thought, she leaned toward Luke and gave him a small peck on the lips.
"Ahem."
A cough immediately came from beside them.
Estelle, who was sitting nearby, turned her head slightly with an awkward expression, while Zeyr simply smiled.

A few of the others looked at them with obvious jealousy, while several more wore expressions of annoyance, as though silently asking why the couple couldn’t keep their affection to themselves for a few minutes.
"Should we focus on the fight?"
Arwen finally spoke from the side, his tone carrying clear discomfort.
Although he still didn’t particularly like working with Luke, there were only two sides in this round, so neither he nor Lirael had much choice but to join Luke’s group.
Hearing Arwen, everyone finally redirected their attention toward the arena.
Luke and Selene did the same, although by then the two were sitting considerably closer together than before, almost leaning into one another.
Their attention returned to the center of the arena, where the Infernal Choir had also sent one of the Sunborn Kingdom’s traitorous warriors into battle.
"Seems like both of your teams think the same."
Peiro, now floating above the arena, looked between the two fighters and casually made his comment.
With a small flick of his hand, the battle began.
The two warriors immediately moved toward each other.
As the fight unfolded below, Brynessa’s gaze remained fixed on Luke.
It wasn’t merely because of what had happened now.
She had been watching him ever since he first appeared before her.
There were several reasons for it.
The first was what Marrec had told her about Luke’s strength despite his relatively low realm.
And the second reason.
Even after learning that she, a High B-rank, was present, Luke had shown no fear.
Instead, he was busy acting lovey dovey with his wife.
’Love.’
The familiar yet distant word surfaced within Brynessa’s mind.
That single word was enough to stir memories she had buried long ago.
Memories of the time when she had once fallen in love with a hero.
An Elf hero.
Her gaze slowly shifted toward Arwen and Lirael.
They belonged to the same race as that man.
The memory of him rejecting her because of her lower snake body resurfaced, followed by the humiliation and suffering he had brought upon her.
’I will erase your entire race.’
Her eyes narrowed as that hatred rose again.
The people around her immediately noticed the subtle change in her expression.
At the same time, starlight-colored snake scales began appearing along her cheeks.
They spread gradually down toward her neck before continuing across her hands and legs, indicating that her transformation was beginning to surface once again.
However, before those changes could develop any further, another voice interrupted her thoughts.
"Miss?"
It was Mella, another black-robed member of the Infernal Choir.
Brynessa’s expression shifted slightly as she heard her.
Marrec also turned toward Brynessa, but the instant he looked at her, his gaze dropped.
There was unmistakable fear in his eyes.
Brynessa noticed neither reaction for long.
She took a slow breath and forced herself to calm down, causing the transformation to stop before it could progress further.
"I’m fine."
Her voice was calm, and she took another slow breath to completely settle her emotions.
Yet her gaze remained fixed on Luke.
Then Iveron’s words surfaced in her mind.
’A hero will never love you.
They are merely tools used to increase their gods’ power, while you princes and princesses are nothing more than parts of that tool.’
The words lingered in her thoughts.
And at that moment—
BANG!
The battle below came to an abrupt end.

chapters.title: Chapter 303: The Weak Ones Are Gone—Now the Monsters Fight!
paragraphs: Brynessa’s warrior had killed his opponent before the man could even surrender.
"First victory goes to the Infernal Choir."
Peiro’s voice announced the result.
Yet Luke’s side wasn’t focused on Peiro or the fallen warrior.
Their attention was on the victor.
His eyes had turned a deep crimson, the whites of them filled with blood vessels, while portions of his skin had darkened until they resembled the flesh of a demon.
"Was that Demonic Berserk?"
The words escaped from several people.
They knew the danger of demonic corruption.
Demon Whispers were infamous for brainwashing people and corrupting them through Demonic Mana, gradually influencing their minds until they began displaying increasingly beast-like behavior.
One of the results could be a berserk state that granted a short-term increase in strength.
While in that state, the corrupted individual no longer cared about injuries or even death.
Everything was reduced to a single purpose.
"To be useful to their master."
Estelle whispered those words, her expression becoming ugly.
The result of the first battle had already made their situation worse than before.
Zeyr shook his head.
"Be more careful from now on, all of you. Surrender the moment you feel that something is wrong."
His expression was serious as he continued.
"Those demonic-corrupted warriors can even choose to self-destruct their cores as a final attack."
His gaze moved toward the center arena.
"If they do that, the casualties on our side could increase considerably."
Hearing his warning, the remaining Sunborn warriors and mages nodded.
Another warrior then stepped forward and jumped down from the spectator seat.
Just like the previous fighter, he was immediately appeared to the center of the arena.
The earlier demonic warrior was still standing there and with bloodshot eyes waiting for the next prey.
"Fight."
Peiro gave the command almost nonchalantly.
He clearly wasn’t interested in battles of this level.
After all, during his time, he had witnessed gods themselves fighting within this arena, so watching ordinary warriors clash was naturally nothing particularly impressive to him.
Still, his gaze briefly shifted toward Luke.
A faint light of curiosity flashed through his eyes.
’Would he be the one?’
The thought surfaced briefly.
But after considering it, Peiro merely shrugged it off and returned his attention to the battle.
When the time came, he would know whether Luke was truly the one or not.
What Peiro failed to notice was that another consciousness was watching him.
A consciousness belonging to a being whose level of existence was entirely different from that of ordinary spirits, and one that even Peiro couldn’t constantly perceive.
Sevaroth, sitting quietly on Luke’s shoulder, stared directly at Peiro.
"Peiro has already sensed and identified your affinities."
The moment Sevaroth spoke, Luke’s body gave a slight involuntary flinch.
He immediately controlled his reaction, however, and made sure not to give Selene any reason to notice that something was wrong.
After confirming that everything around him remained normal, Luke asked inwardly, his voice carrying a trace of concern.
’Is this a problem?’
Sevaroth shook his head.
"No."
Then he added,
"It seems he wants the anomaly to come here."
Luke remained silent.
Sevaroth continued,
"And you may not be the first anomaly who has come here."
Those words immediately reminded Luke of the system quest description he had received earlier.
[Their web was created long before you arrived.]
[You were not the only one who discovered their scheme.]
[You merely stepped into a position they had already prepared.]
Another set of lines followed.
[Those beings have already woven their web far deeper than she can imagine.]
[Every possibility and variable.]
[Even the beings that should never have been discovered...]
[They were already within their calculations.]
Luke’s eyes narrowed slightly.
’So this is what it meant by prepared.’
He remembered the first clue he had received regarding the Origin Fragment.
The system had already implied that he wasn’t the first person who had attempted to find it.
’Another Hero of Light?’
The possibility entered his mind.
’Or perhaps the Saintess again?’
Unfortunately, there was no way for him to know yet.
He could only wait.
Unless he entered that ancient temple himself, he wasn’t going to find the answer.
"Second Round, Sunborn Kingdom won."
Peiro’s announcement pulled Luke’s attention back toward the arena.
The Sunborn warrior had managed to defeat the demonic warrior, but rather than continuing the fight, he had chosen to surrender once he had secured the victory.
From there, the battles continued.
One after another, warriors and mages from both sides stepped into the arena, fought, and either defeated their opponents or surrendered when continuing became too dangerous.
The exchange continued until the number of victories on both sides finally became equal.
"Twenty-five victories for the Infernal Choir and twenty-five victories for the Sunborn Kingdom."
Peiro announced the result in his usual calm voice.
Estelle and the others, however, didn’t look relieved.
Quite the opposite.
"So many of them are still left."
Estelle looked toward the opposing side.
Twenty-five demonic warriors were still standing there, each of them ready to enter the arena when their turn came.
Their own side had already paid a heavy price to reach the same score.
Despite taking precautions, ten Platinum Knights had lost their lives, while two mages had also been killed.
The difference in strategy between the two sides was becoming increasingly obvious.
The Infernal Choir had used twenty-five warriors so far, and every single one had fought until death.
Not one of them had surrendered.
Their side, however, had already used fifty warriors and mages to achieve the same number of victories.
The numerical cost was becoming difficult to ignore.
Isaria noticed Estelle’s troubled expression and gently patted her back.
It did little to improve Estelle’s mood.
Even if they somehow managed to survive these ruins, she knew their kingdom would still suffer another major setback.
The loss of so many powerful warriors could eventually result in a serious shortage of B-rank beings within the Sunborn Kingdom.
And that would affect much more than this single battle.
That thought made Estelle even more worried.
Luke also noticed her expression and couldn’t help feeling bad for her.
However, he knew he couldn’t simply step into the arena at the beginning.
They still had no idea whether the Infernal Choir had prepared some hidden method of killing their stronger combatants, perhaps through a suicide attack or another form of sacrifice.
Until they understood what else the enemy had prepared, sending one of their strongest fighters into the arena without knowing the risks would be reckless.
That was also why none of the higher-quality combatants on either side had entered the arena yet.
But it seemed that time had finally come.
"Arwen, Lirael."
Zeyr turned toward the two of them.
"Which of you will go first?"
All the lower-ranked warriors had already been used, so it was finally time for the stronger representatives to take their turns.
Among the remaining representatives from Empyrean Academy, Arwen and Lirael were the weakest.
Zeyr didn’t mention Isaria and Estelle.
And he certainly didn’t mention Luke.
The expressions of Arwen and Lirael changed slightly, and a hint of anger appeared on their faces.
Neither of them liked the idea of being sent into the arena first while the those remained safely behind.
Still, after exchanging a brief glance, they nodded.
At least they were allowed to surrender once the situation became too dangerous.
They didn’t have to fight until death.

chapters.title: Chapter 304: Arwen Wins Ten Battles by Himself!
paragraphs: Arwen and Larael looked at each other for a moment before Arwen finally decided to go first.
"Good."

Zeyr nodded in approval. Since Arwen was stronger than Larael, even if the Infernal Choir tried to play some kind of trick, he had a better chance of dealing with it without putting his life at serious risk.
From Brynessa’s side, another of the demonic warriors stepped forward.
Peiro gave Arwen a brief glance before turning his attention back toward the arena.
"Start."
The moment Peiro’s voice fell, Arwen raised one hand.
"Orphelios, come forth."
The space in front of him shimmered, and a bright golden circular portal suddenly opened in the air.
It was roughly thirty feet tall and ten feet wide, its surface radiating a warm golden light that illuminated the nearby spectator seats.
From it, a presence emerged.
A twenty-foot-tall figure stepped through the portal.
THUD!
The moment Orphelios planted his foot on the arena floor, the ground cracked beneath it, several thin fractures spreading outward from the point of impact.

The arena had been specifically modified by Peiro to withstand B-rank battles rather than using earlier dark stones, which could bear gods level attack, so the damage wasn’t enough to threaten its structure, but it was still clear that the massive spirit wasn’t some weak elemental creature.
Orphelios resembled a robust giant formed from fire, its body carrying a dense, almost tangible heat. Above its head floated a crown made entirely of flames.
"He already summoned it."
Zeyr’s expression carried a trace of surprise.
He hadn’t expected Arwen to reveal his spirit immediately instead of testing the opponent first.
"Maybe he’s already playing safe." Karon spoke casually from beside him.
The others nodded.
Meanwhile, Luke continued staring at Orphelios.

He had seen plenty of elemental creatures before in his world, movies, but there was something different about this one. The flames covering its body weren’t loose or scattered; they seemed to form the spirit’s very structure, while the fiery crown above its head gave it the impression of a being that stood at a higher rank even among spirits.
Selene, who noticed his interest, began explaining.
"Luke, you’ve already seen many different power classifications and cultivation methods, and the Elves have their own system as well."
She paused briefly to make sure he was listening, and when she saw his attention was fully on her, she continued.

"Elves follow the power classification of Spiritance. As they progress through the Spiritance realms, the bond between them and their contracted spirits becomes deeper, allowing them to synchronize more closely and gain greater access to their spirit’s power."
Luke nodded.
Selene continued.

"Their ultimate goal is to reach the highest level of spiritual connection and eventually form a connection with the World Tree Spirit itself, which is considered the greatest and most ancient spirit associated with the Elven race."

After explaining that, she took a breath before adding, "That’s why an Elf’s strength depends heavily on their spirit. It is also the reason you were able to defeat Arwen so easily earlier. Since, he hadn’t used his spirit."
The moment she finished that sentence, she reached out and pinched Luke’s waist.
Luke flinched.
"Ouch—ouch. Okay, okay, I understand."
He immediately raised both hands in surrender.
Selene released him only after apparently deciding that he had understood the lesson. After all, earlier he attacked the Arwen, without knowing his strength.
Luke rubbed his side before turning his attention back toward the arena.
By then, the demonic warrior had barely gotten into position.
Orphelios had already raised one arm, a concentrated beam of solar fire gathering around his palm before suddenly shooting forward.
WHOOOSH!
The attack crossed the arena in an instant, giving the demonic warrior barely enough time to widen his eyes and raise his weapon defensively before the beam engulfed him.
"WHAT—?!"
BOOM!
"AAAAARGH!"

His scream tore across the arena as the solar flames swallowed his body and armor together. He desperately held his weapon in front of himself, trying to shield his body from the overwhelming heat, but the brilliant flames quickly obscured his figure, leaving only his silhouette visible within the raging fire.
"AAAGH—!"
His scream abruptly cut off as his silhouette disappeared completely.

When the solar fire finally faded, the arena fell silent once again. Nothing remained except a few glowing fragments of melted equipment scattered across the arena floor, their faint red-orange glow gradually fading as they cooled.
"Huh?"
Luke blinked. "So strong."
He had expected a fight.
After all, both Arwen and the demonic warrior were at the same level.
Yet Orphelios had burned through the opponent as though there had been no resistance at all.
Selene noticed the confusion on his face and couldn’t help sighing.

She had gradually realized that Luke had spent most of his time simply overpowering his enemies. He understood how to use his own strength extremely well, but when it came to the finer applications of different elements, there were still many things he hadn’t learned.
That realization was understandable, though.

It had only been about a month since Luke had gone from being an ordinary mortal to possessing enough strength to fight B-rank beings, and he had done most of that while remaining in the relatively remote Blackstone territory.
Luke was undeniably talented.
He had simply never received proper instruction.
With proper guidance, his understanding of his abilities could increase much faster.
"Luke."
Selene called his name again.

"If Arwen, or anyone else, used Fire Essence to achieve that same effect, they would have to spend more energy first overcoming the opponent’s Essence before they could properly burn through their B-rank body."
She paused.
"But—"
Before she could finish explaining, Peiro’s voice came from above.
"Victory goes to the Sunborn Kingdom."
The match had already ended.
Another demonic warrior immediately stepped into the arena, apparently without being bothered by what had happened to his companion.
However, the moment he appeared, a gigantic sphere of fire streaked toward him.
BOOM!
He reacted quickly and tried to dodge, but his body suddenly jerked to a stop. Chains made of fire had already wrapped tightly around his arms and legs, locking him in place.
"What—?!"
He struggled violently, flames bursting from his body as he tried to break free, but the fiery chains held firm. The fire sphere closed the remaining distance and slammed directly into him.
BOOM!
His entire body vanished beneath the roaring flames.
"AAAAARGH!"
His panicked scream echoed across the arena, but it lasted only a few seconds before the flames swallowed his voice completely.
When the attack finally disappeared, the demonic warrior was gone, leaving behind nothing but a pile of blackened ash scattered across the arena floor.
Selene continued her explanation as though the fight itself had demonstrated her point.
"But Orphelios is a Fire Element Spirit, meaning it can directly use pure fire rather than having to imitate fire through Fire Essence. That’s an important difference."
Luke listened carefully.

"Because the attack is actual fire, it already possesses the destructive characteristics of fire without needing to be created through the same process that an ordinary user of Fire Essence would require."
She looked toward the remains in the arena.

"That’s why those demonic warriors are having such a difficult time resisting it. They haven’t reached a point where they can properly counter the elemental properties of such attacks with their own Essence, so a direct elemental spirit has a major advantage against them."
Luke nodded slowly.
He remembered the temperature comparisons shown by the system, as well as the Solar Flare he had once used against the vampire near Blackthorn.
That attack had also contained the properties of a real element rather than merely imitating one through ordinary Essence.
’So, overall, I don’t need to worry about Essence that much.’
The thought had barely formed when Sevaroth’s voice came from his side.
"Don’t get arrogant yet, Luke."
Luke turned toward him.
Sevaroth continued calmly.
"Real fire can still differ greatly from one source to another. A candle flame and magma are both fire, but you already know which one is more destructive."
Luke’s expression changed.
’Yeah... I forgot.’
The realization came naturally.
His elemental mastery was still low, and his energy hadn’t reached the level of compression that would allow him to bring out the full potential of those elements.
’So even if the nature of an attack matters, I can’t simply assume that having the real element means I’ve already reached the strongest possible application.’
He began thinking about how he could improve that aspect of his abilities while, below them, Arwen continued cutting through one demonic warrior after another.
Orphelios made the battles almost one-sided.
Its attacks were precise rather than wasteful, burning through enemies before they had enough time to establish a proper counter.
Eventually, Peiro announced the updated result.
"Thirty-fifth victory goes to the Sunborn Kingdom. The Infernal Choir remains at twenty-five victories."
Of those thirty-five victories, Arwen alone had secured ten.
"Hmm." Zeyr looked toward the arena.
"Those victory buffs only last for a few minutes."

He had noticed that the bonuses granted by the Heaven’s Crucible weren’t anything extraordinary. They consisted of temporary increases to speed, strength, damage reduction, evasion, accuracy, and similar abilities.
They provided a short-term boost, but nothing that could completely overturn a battle.
"Seems like they didn’t want the victory advantage to become too extreme through outside interference or additional methods."
Zeyr’s eyes narrowed slightly as he considered the rules.
Perhaps that was also why potions and other external buffs weren’t allowed.

"Good."
Zeyr nodded in approval.
Since Arwen was stronger than Larael, even if the Infernal Choir tried to play some kind of trick, he had a better chance of dealing with it without putting his life at serious risk.
From Brynessa’s side, another of the demonic warriors stepped forward.
Peiro gave Arwen a brief glance before turning his attention back toward the arena.
"Start."
The moment Peiro’s voice fell, Arwen raised one hand.
"Orphelios, come forth."
The space in front of him shimmered, and a bright golden circular portal suddenly opened in the air.
It was roughly thirty feet tall and ten feet wide, its surface radiating a warm golden light that illuminated the nearby spectator seats.
From it, a presence emerged.
A twenty-foot-tall figure stepped through the portal.
THUD!
The moment Orphelios planted his foot on the arena floor, the ground cracked beneath it, several thin fractures spreading outward from the point of impact.

The arena had been specifically modified by Peiro to withstand B-rank battles rather than using earlier dark stones, which could bear gods level attack, so the damage wasn’t enough to threaten its structure, but it was still clear that the massive spirit wasn’t some weak elemental creature.
Orphelios resembled a robust giant formed from fire, its body carrying a dense, almost tangible heat.
Above its head floated a crown made entirely of flames.
"He already summoned it."
Zeyr’s expression carried a trace of surprise.
He hadn’t expected Arwen to reveal his spirit immediately instead of testing the opponent first.
"Maybe he’s already playing safe." Karon spoke casually from beside him.
The others nodded.
Meanwhile, Luke continued staring at Orphelios.
He had seen plenty of elemental creatures before in his world, movies, but there was something different about this one.

The flames covering its body weren’t loose or scattered; they seemed to form the spirit’s very structure, while the fiery crown above its head gave it the impression of a being that stood at a higher rank even among spirits.
Selene, who noticed his interest, began explaining.
"Luke, you’ve already seen many different power classifications and cultivation methods, and the Elves have their own system as well."
She paused briefly to make sure he was listening, and when she saw his attention was fully on her, she continued.
"Elves follow the power classification of Spiritance.

As they progress through the Spiritance realms, the bond between them and their contracted spirits becomes deeper, allowing them to synchronize more closely and gain greater access to their spirit’s power."
Luke nodded.
Selene continued.

"Their ultimate goal is to reach the highest level of spiritual connection and eventually form a connection with the World Tree Spirit itself, which is considered the greatest and most ancient spirit associated with the Elven race."
After explaining that, she took a breath before adding, "That’s why an Elf’s strength depends heavily on their spirit.
It is also the reason you were able to defeat Arwen so easily earlier.
Since, he hadn’t used his spirit."
The moment she finished that sentence, she reached out and pinched Luke’s waist.
Luke flinched.
"Ouch—ouch.
Okay, okay, I understand."
He immediately raised both hands in surrender.
Selene released him only after apparently deciding that he had understood the lesson.
After all, earlier he attacked the Arwen, without knowing his strength.
Luke rubbed his side before turning his attention back toward the arena.
By then, the demonic warrior had barely gotten into position.
Orphelios had already raised one arm, a concentrated beam of solar fire gathering around his palm before suddenly shooting forward.
WHOOOSH!
The attack crossed the arena in an instant, giving the demonic warrior barely enough time to widen his eyes and raise his weapon defensively before the beam engulfed him.
"WHAT—?!"
BOOM!
"AAAAARGH!"
His scream tore across the arena as the solar flames swallowed his body and armor together.

He desperately held his weapon in front of himself, trying to shield his body from the overwhelming heat, but the brilliant flames quickly obscured his figure, leaving only his silhouette visible within the raging fire.
"AAAGH—!"
His scream abruptly cut off as his silhouette disappeared completely.

After all, both Arwen and the demonic warrior were at the same level.

That realization was understandable, though.

It had only been about a month since Luke had gone from being an ordinary mortal to possessing enough strength to fight B-rank beings, and he had done most of that while remaining in the relatively remote Blackstone territory.
Luke was undeniably talented.
He had simply never received proper instruction.
With proper guidance, his understanding of his abilities could increase much faster.

chapters.title: Chapter 305: The Battle Reaches the Mid-B-Rank Level!
paragraphs: "Yeah."
Nolan, Kira, Estelle, and the others nodded in agreement.
Their attention soon returned to Arwen.
The earlier confidence in his expression had faded.
He looked pale, and his breathing had become noticeably heavier.
The reason was simple.
Maintaining Orphelios required a constant amount of energy from his body, and after using the spirit repeatedly, Arwen’s Essence reserves had dropped considerably.
Even his physical stamina was starting to reach its limit.
Peiro noticed it as well. "Do you want to continue?"
Arwen slowly raised his head, his shoulders still rising and falling from his heavy breathing.
Sweat ran down the side of his face, and he remained silent for a brief moment as he caught his breath. His fingers tightened slightly before he finally shook his head.
"No."
Peiro nodded.
The next instant, Orphelios vanished in a flicker of golden light, and Arwen was transported back to his seat.
Since he hadn’t surrendered the round, he could still return later if he recovered enough strength.
"Well, you’ve done enough."
Karon looked toward him.
She clearly understood what Arwen had been doing.
He had been burning through his Essence to maintain Orphelios and repeatedly use highly concentrated attacks, so continuing would have left him with little strength for anything else.
She didn’t say that part aloud.
There was no need.
Everyone could already see it.
"Hmm." Arwen nodded.
He also noticed that a few of his teammates didn’t look particularly pleased with his decision, but he didn’t care.
He wasn’t foolish enough to throw his life away simply to prove that he was patriotic.
From the beginning, Peiro had made surrender one of the available options.
There was no shame in using it.
If everyone eventually lost, perhaps another route back would open.
’Life is more important.’ With that thought, Arwen looked toward Larael.
She was already preparing herself.
Then Peiro’s voice rang out again.
"Start."
Another round began.
This time, Larael raised her hand.
"Elvar, lend me your strength."
Her voice was gentle.
A moment later, a wide silver-white portal opened behind her.
WHOOSH!
A figure emerged from it.
It was roughly thirty feet tall and humanoid, with a broad and muscular build.
Its arms were covered by silver-white roots that formed something resembling armored gauntlets, while silver-white bark spread across its torso and limbs, creating a layer of natural armor.
More bark rose from its back and curved upward, eventually forming a crown around its head.
Green energy flowed through its body like veins.

Along the outer edges of its form, several long silver leaves had appeared. They eventually detached, drifting through the air before breaking apart into silver particles that were absorbed back into the spirit.
The sight left many of the spectators surprised.
Orphelios had been impressive, but Elvar’s presence had a different kind of majesty to it.
"Sadly, her spirit isn’t a full combat type."
Zeyr sighed from the side.
"Otherwise, her strength would be even greater."
The other representatives from Empyrean Academy nodded in agreement.
Arwen, however, remained seated with a normal expression.
He wasn’t bothered by the fact that Larael’s spirit looked stronger in some aspects.
Its specialty was simply different.
A spirit didn’t need to be overwhelmingly destructive to be valuable.
Soon, the next battle began.
Larael’s spirit, Elvar, faced another demonic warrior.
Its combat method was straightforward.
Roots emerged from the ground and wrapped around its opponent’s limbs before the spirit followed up with sharp silver branches.
SNAP!
Roots burst from the arena floor.
The demonic warrior tried to move, but several thick roots wrapped around his legs and tightened.
He swung his weapon, cutting through the first layer.
CRACK!
But more roots immediately emerged beneath him.
Before he could break free, silver-white branches shot forward like spears.
THRUST!
They pierced through his defense, making the warrior stumbled.
More roots climbed around his body, restricting his movement until another silver branch struck through his torso.
The battle ended soon afterward.
Luke watched the process carefully.
"Hmm. Its crowd-control capability is pretty good."
"If used properly, her spirit could have a major role on a large battlefield."
By then, Larael had already defeated five demonic warriors.
Yet unlike Arwen, her energy reserves remained relatively high.
Elvar was also consuming much less energy during combat, allowing it to maintain its abilities without draining Larael nearly as quickly.
Some of the demonic warriors were able to break the silver branches, but every time one was destroyed, another quickly took its place.
The continuous pressure made it difficult for them to escape.
Selene nodded at Luke’s observation.
"In the academy, Larael has always played an important role whenever we participate in large-scale battlefield missions."
She paused before adding,

"Her silver-white roots aren’t only useful for restraining enemies. They can also provide a strong defensive barrier when enough of them are gathered together. They’re resistant to fire as well because of their unique variation, which makes her spirit useful in a lot of different situations."
Luke nodded, somewhat impressed by the versatility.
At that moment, Larael looked toward Peiro.
"Lord Peiro, I can’t continue the next battle."
Several people immediately raised their eyebrows.
Brynessa and the members of her group, however, remained calm.
Larael’s stamina still appeared good enough for a few more fights.
But Peiro simply nodded.
"Sure."
He announced the result.
"Forty-fifth victory goes to the Sunborn Kingdom, while the Infernal Choir remains at twenty-five victories."
With that, Larael was teleported back to her seat.
The moment she returned, several expressions around her changed slightly, but no one said anything.
Because, everyone had already expeced her half-heart, effort in the match.
"Well, Marius, you go now."
Zeyr turned toward the male vampire.
Marius nodded.
Before jumping down, however, he gave one last look toward Selene and Luke, who were still discussing something together.
Then he leaped from the spectator seat.
As before, the space below him shifted, transporting him directly into the center of the arena.
’I will deal with only five.’
That was all he needed to accomplish.
He wasn’t particularly concerned about the others.
His only real reason was Selene and that was also why, he had come here.
But ever since Luke had appeared, Selene’s attention had remained almost entirely on him.
Even if Marius displayed some impressive strength, he already knew his chances of impressing her were practically nonexistent.
And his strength was still inferior to hers.
’Well, she was never impressed by strength.’ Marius sighed inwardly.
He had known Selene since their student days.
That fact alone made him understand her personality better than most.
"Are you ready?" Peiro’s voice came from above.
Marius nodded. "Yeah."
His reply lacked enthusiasm.
But, Peiro didn’t care.
"Start."
The battle began.

As a vampire, Marius immediately relied on his blood manipulation. Whenever one of the demonic warriors approached, he made a sharp movement with his hand, and a thin cut suddenly opened across the opponent’s body.
"Bring it out..."
The blood flowing from the wound lifted into the air under his control.
Marius curled his fingers slightly, manipulating the blood with precise movements. The injury widened as he drew more blood from the wound, making it difficult for the opponent to recover.
One warrior charged at him with a roar.
Marius calmly stepped aside, narrowly avoiding the attack. At the same time, a thin line of blood followed the movement of his fingers.
Slash!
Another wound opened across the warrior’s body.
"ARGH!"
The warrior stumbled, losing his balance for a moment.

Marius took a step back, his eyes remaining fixed on his opponent as he continued manipulating the blood pouring from the wound. The warrior’s movements gradually became weaker until his knees finally gave out and he collapsed onto the arena floor.

Marius fought in much the same way against the next four warriors. Rather than relying on some large-scale or highly destructive technique, he focused on endurance and control, carefully opening wounds, drawing out blood, and using it against his opponents. As a vampire, his stamina was considerable, making the method perfectly suited to him.
One after another, the five demonic warriors fell.
After the fifth opponent collapsed, Marius lowered his hand and took a slow breath, his chest rising slightly as he steadied himself.
He ran a hand through his silver hair, pushing it back from his forehead before glancing toward the spectator seats.
His gaze immediately searched for one person.
Selene.
She was still there.
Still talking with Luke.
Still laughing.
She hadn’t even looked toward the arena.
’That bastard, Luke.’
The curse remained unspoken, existing only inside Marius’s mind.
’Why?’
He couldn’t understand how things had ended up like this.
Unfortunately, nobody cared about his thoughts.
Everyone’s attention had already shifted toward Brynessa’s side.
Marrec finally stood up.
He stretched his neck slightly before taking a step forward.
Then he kicked off the ground.
WHOOSH!
His body shot toward the center of the arena.
Of course, he couldn’t physically cross the fifty-kilometer distance in a single jump.
The familiar Void movement activated.
Space twisted around him.
In the next instant, Marrec appeared directly above the arena and dropped toward the ground.
THUD!
His landing was far heavier than Arwen’s Spirit.
The impact cracked a roughly ten-meter section of the arena floor, while a small cloud of dust rose around his feet.
Marius finally came out of his thoughts and looked toward him.
Peiro’s voice followed.
"Do you want to continue?"
Marius wasn’t stupid enough to answer otherwise.
"No."
Peiro gave a small nod.
He had expected that response.
With another spatial shift, Marius was teleported back to the spectator seat.
None of the Empyrean Academy representatives said anything to him.
They knew Marius well enough to understand his personality, and although he was weaker than both Arwen and Larael, Zeyr hadn’t asked him to fight more than necessary.
After all, Marius was a vampire, just like Selene.
The same consideration didn’t extend to Nolan and Kira.
Both were human members of Empyrean Academy, while the fifty previous warriors sent out by the Sunborn Kingdom had also been humans.
That distribution had been intentional.
The other races would need to participate after that.
It was also why Zeyr had chosen Arwen and Larael earlier.
But now the opponent was different.
Zeyr turned toward Nolan and Kira with a serious expression.
"Nolan, Kira, try to defeat him. If you can’t, surrender."
He knew that the situation became much more dangerous once a mid-B-rank entered the battle.
The difference between the earlier opponents and someone like Marrec couldn’t be ignored.
"Sure."
Both nodded.
They exchanged a brief glance and began deciding who would enter the arena first.

The warrior’s movements gradually became weaker until his knees finally gave out and he collapsed onto the arena floor.
Marius fought in much the same way against the next four warriors.
Rather than relying on some large-scale or highly destructive technique, he focused on endurance and control, carefully opening wounds, drawing out blood, and using it against his opponents.
As a vampire, his stamina was considerable, making the method perfectly suited to him.
One after another, the five demonic warriors fell.
After the fifth opponent collapsed, Marius lowered his hand and took a slow breath, his chest rising slightly as he steadied himself.
He ran a hand through his silver hair, pushing it back from his forehead before glancing toward the spectator seats.
His gaze immediately searched for one person.
Selene.
She was still there.
Still talking with Luke.
Still laughing.
She hadn’t even looked toward the arena.
’That bastard, Luke.’
The curse remained unspoken, existing only inside Marius’s mind.
’Why?’
He couldn’t understand how things had ended up like this.
Unfortunately, nobody cared about his thoughts.
Everyone’s attention had already shifted toward Brynessa’s side.
Marrec finally stood up.
He stretched his neck slightly before taking a step forward.
Then he kicked off the ground.
WHOOSH!
His body shot toward the center of the arena.
Of course, he couldn’t physically cross the fifty-kilometer distance in a single jump.
The familiar Void movement activated.
Space twisted around him.
In the next instant, Marrec appeared directly above the arena and dropped toward the ground.
THUD!
His landing was far heavier than Arwen’s Spirit.
The impact cracked a roughly ten-meter section of the arena floor, while a small cloud of dust rose around his feet.
Marius finally came out of his thoughts and looked toward him.
Peiro’s voice followed.
"Do you want to continue?"
Marius wasn’t stupid enough to answer otherwise.
"No."
Peiro gave a small nod.
He had expected that response.
With another spatial shift, Marius was teleported back to the spectator seat.
None of the Empyrean Academy representatives said anything to him.
They knew Marius well enough to understand his personality, and although he was weaker than both Arwen and Larael, Zeyr hadn’t asked him to fight more than necessary.
After all, Marius was a vampire, just like Selene.
The same consideration didn’t extend to Nolan and Kira.
Both were human members of Empyrean Academy, while the fifty previous warriors sent out by the Sunborn Kingdom had also been humans.
That distribution had been intentional.
The other races would need to participate after that.
It was also why Zeyr had chosen Arwen and Larael earlier.
But now the opponent was different.
Zeyr turned toward Nolan and Kira with a serious expression.
"Nolan, Kira, try to defeat him.
If you can’t, surrender."
He knew that the situation became much more dangerous once a mid-B-rank entered the battle.
The difference between the earlier opponents and someone like Marrec couldn’t be ignored.
"Sure."
Both nodded.
They exchanged a brief glance and began deciding who would enter the arena first.

chapters.title: Chapter 306: An A-Rank Origin Skill Appears in the Arena!
paragraphs: After a brief discussion, Nolan finally decided to go first.
"I will go."
With those words, he pushed himself away from the specter seat and jumped down.
Wrrr...

The moment his body left the seat, the surrounding space rippled softly, as though the air itself had turned into water. The distortion spread around him, swallowing his figure before the spatial force carried him directly toward the arena.
A second later, Nolan appeared at the center of the battlefield.
Marrec was already waiting for him.
He stood there with both arms folded over his chest, his posture relaxed and his expression calm, as though he had all the time in the world.
His half-demonic face was still visible, with the black leather armor covering his body and the crimson eye on the corrupted side of his face watching Nolan quietly.
What stood out, however, was what he didn’t have.
There was no weapon in his hands.
Nolan’s gaze briefly moved over Marrec’s body before his brows furrowed.
’No weapon?’
That raised an obvious question.
Was he a mage-type fighter?

Nolan wasn’t willing to assume anything, so he immediately reached into his spatial ring and pulled out his silver greatsword. At the same time, he had already equipped his black plate armor, the metallic surface reflecting the dim light hanging over the arena.
After checking the locking mechanism of his helmet, he lowered the visor over his face.
"I’m ready."
Peiro floated higher above the arena and looked down at the two combatants.
"Start."
Below, Marrec made the first move.
"Let me show you, young man, the difference between a veteran and those earlier weaklings."
His gaze briefly shifted to the corpses of the demonic warriors who had already fallen during the previous battles.
There was no sadness in his expression.
Those warriors had been outer members of the Infernal Choir, people sent into this mission for precisely this kind of purpose, and Marrec clearly didn’t consider their deaths worth remembering.
Nolan tightened his grip around his greatsword.
"Bring it."
Marrec didn’t answer immediately.
Instead, he slowly closed his eyes.
His breathing became steady.
He remained still for a brief moment, inhaling deeply before slowly releasing the breath.
Then his eyes opened.
The calmness disappeared from them.
Only flickering flames remained.
’A-rank Origin Skill.’
Marrec raised both hands while slowly exhaling and brought his palms together.
Clap!
The sound was simple.
What followed was not.
The air behind Marrec rippled violently, and the space seemed to distort under an intense wave of heat, as though it were being softened by an invisible furnace.
A tiny flame appeared behind him.
Then another.
Then another.
One after another, ten small flames emerged until they formed a circular halo behind Marrec’s body.
The flames didn’t spread wildly.
Instead, each one remained suspended at an equal distance from the others, slowly rotating around an invisible center.
Several people in the spectator seats frowned in confusion.
Then Marrec’s voice echoed across the arena.
"SEARWHEEL!"
The ten small flames suddenly brightened.
FWOOM!
Infernal Flame surged through each spark, causing them to rapidly expand until the small flames transformed into ten red spheres.
Fwoosh! Fwoosh! Fwoosh! Fwoosh! Fwoosh! Fwoosh! Fwoosh! Fwoosh! Fwoosh! Fwoosh!
The ten spheres began rotating behind Marrec in a circular formation, their surfaces shimmering with concentrated heat.
Even from the spectator seats, the distortion around them was visible.
Nolan’s expression tightened.
"A fire user..."
That alone wouldn’t have frightened him.
A melee fighter generally had an advantage against a mage who needed distance to unleash attacks.
But Marrec didn’t feel like an ordinary fire-type mage.
The ten spheres behind him were enough to make Nolan reconsider his approach.
"Let’s start, young man."
Marrec casually raised one hand and pointed toward Nolan with his index finger.
The gesture looked almost inviting. "Come."
Kira sighed from the spectator seats.
"Seems like a tough match." She already had a bad feeling about it.
Zeyr nodded slowly.
"I didn’t expect this Infernal Choir member to be an Origin Skill user."
His expression became more serious.
"Hopefully Nolan can get out of there in one piece."
Luke, who had been watching the entire exchange, raised an eyebrow.
There was one thing he didn’t quite understand.
He knew that people with cruel personalities or those who had suffered tragedies could end up joining evil organizations, but Marrec had already displayed obvious signs of demonic transformation.
Half of his face had become demonic.
His body had also changed.
So why had Zeyr specifically called him uncorrupted?
Luke turned toward Selene.
"Do you know anything about this?"
Selene shifted her gaze from the arena to her husband and answered in a calm voice.
"Even though demon gods can give their followers access to a completely new power system, not everyone has to accept that system."
She briefly pointed toward Mella, who was sitting beside Brynessa across the arena.

"And even among those who do accept it, the more they rely on that demonic power, the greater the corruption becomes. Their minds gradually deteriorate, and they lose more and more control over themselves.
Luke nodded as he listened.
"As for the physical changes, those are different."
Selene continued.

"The demonic transformation is already part of their cultivation system. Many of them deliberately pursue it because their goal is to eventually become complete demon species and fully utilize demonic powers."
She glanced toward Marrec.

"So the changes in his appearance aren’t necessarily proof that he’s mentally corrupted. People at his level can also control how much of their demonic transformation they allow to appear externally."
Luke’s expression relaxed slightly.
That explanation cleared up some of his earlier doubts about Demon Whispers.
His attention returned to the battlefield just as the fight suddenly entered a higher intensity.
"SEARING BULLET!"
Marrec’s voice rang out.
The ten Sear spheres behind him rotated faster.
Then their surfaces opened.
Thousands of tiny fragments of compressed Infernal Flame shot out like a storm of bullets.
Fwoosh! Fwoosh! Fwoosh!
Nolan’s pupils contracted.
He immediately moved.
The first wave passed over his shoulder.
He twisted his body to avoid the second.
Several projectiles still struck his black plate armor.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
The impacts shook his body, sparks spraying from the damaged metal as the compressed flames tore through the armor.
Nolan gritted his teeth and kept moving.
He couldn’t afford to stay still.
More projectiles rained down.
Some slammed into the ground around him, blowing chunks of stone upward, while others struck his armor until pieces of the black plate cracked and fell away.
Clang!
A damaged section of armor broke loose and hit the ground.
Nolan didn’t even glance at it.
He raised his greatsword and charged.
"Hah!"
His feet hammered against the arena floor as he accelerated.
Marrec watched him approach without moving.
Nolan reached him in an instant.
He raised the silver greatsword above his head and swung downward with all his strength.
The blade whistled through the air.
Just before it reached Marrec—
"Sear Drift." The words were spoken calmly.
