Then a quiet, cutting sound finally echoed across the battlefield.
SSSHHKK...

That single sound carried farther than the previous explosions had, and when the delayed effect finally manifested, the ground beneath the attack separated along the same line while Brynessa’s gigantic serpent body also began slowly sliding apart, the two portions losing their connection as one side started falling away from the other.
Everyone watching was horrified.
Yet Brynessa’s dying serpent face still carried a faint smile.

Because at the exact moment Selene had used Sovereign Execution, the spectral serpent behind her had begun growing at an alarming rate, gaining another foot of length with every passing fraction of a second.
But instead of continuing to grow outward where everyone could see it, the spectral serpent suddenly moved toward the purple magic circle beneath Selene’s Crimson Throne.
It descended directly into the formation.
And under Brynessa’s dying but satisfied expression, the spectral serpent completely disappeared inside the purple magic circle.
BAAMM!
Brynessa’s half-cut gigantic serpent body finally crashed into the ground, producing another explosive impact that shattered a large section of the earth beneath her.
Mella and Marrec were left stunned.
The other spectators were equally silent.
The entire arena seemed to have fallen into an unnatural stillness.
Only Peiro, floating above the battlefield, let out a slow sigh.
"It’s too late."
His quiet words had barely left his mouth when the next stage of Brynessa’s plan finally began.
The seven symbols of Sevenfold Omen, which had been floating around Selene all this time, suddenly burst with intense purple light and shot toward her Blood Sovereign body.
TThis time, they didn’t merely surround her.
Instead, they merged directly into her.
’What?!’
Selene’s mind screamed, but she immediately discovered that she couldn’t speak.
No, it was worse than that.
She couldn’t feel anything.

Her all senses had disappeared completely, and even the connection between herself and the Crimson Throne, which had felt as natural as an extension of her own body until this moment, had suddenly been severed.
Outside, the World of Crimson began gradually losing its stability as Selene’s control disappeared, and the crimson domain slowly started being cancelled.
The Crimson Throne, however, remained summoned.

It still stood within the battlefield despite Selene no longer controlling it, while Selene’s Blood Sovereign form remained seated upon the throne in complete silence, with the seven purple symbols now embedded deep within its body.
Normally, the Blood Sovereign form should have been forced to revert and disappear once Selene lost control.
But that would only have been true if her innate ability had not inherited properties from a Demi-God, or if the technique itself had not originally been created through Demi-God-level power.
Because of that inherited property, the Blood Sovereign form remained.

And then, before anyone could understand what was happening, a gigantic, thick purple thread suddenly emerged and wrapped tightly around the Blood Sovereign’s body, binding it so firmly that any movement would be almost impossible.
Everyone stared at the scene in confusion.
"What the heck is going on?"
How could Brynessa still be doing something when her body had already been cut apart and she had seemingly died?
That was the question appearing in everyone’s minds.
Brynessa’s magic had continued.
Her curses had not died with her.
Yet almost everyone had forgotten one crucial detail.
From the beginning of this battle, Peiro had never declared the winner.
He always announced the result whenever one side surrendered, or when one side—
Died.
And so everyone continued watching the battlefield without realizing that the fight had already entered a completely different stage.

Suddenly, the purple magic circle beneath Selene’s Crimson Throne began rippling violently with purple light, and the entire formation trembled before releasing a sound like the world itself was being shattered apart.
BOOOOOOM!
A gigantic serpent emerged from the magic circle.
It was ten thousand feet long.

Its enormous jaws closed around the Crimson Throne itself, biting down on the structure as it attempted to crush it, while Selene’s Blood Sovereign form remained seated upon the throne, completely motionless and helpless because she could no longer control her body.
"NOOO!"
Luke’s voice finally exploded through the arena as he saw what was happening.
He immediately attempted to summon Valzareth so that he could use Void Step and reach Selene.
But—
Nothing happened.
Luke’s eyes widened when he realized that he couldn’t make the Void Step work, and his gaze immediately shot upward.
Peiro was looking directly at him.
Earlier, Peiro had allowed Luke to interfere when Kira’s life was in danger, but this time he wasn’t going to allow it again.
He didn’t need to say anything.
The meaning behind his expression was already clear.
Luke understood immediately that no matter what he attempted, Peiro would not permit him to interfere in the battle this time.
But that realization did nothing to calm him.
He was worried.
More than worried.

The sight of the ten-thousand-foot serpent holding Selene’s Crimson Throne between its jaws made Luke feel as though his mind was about to collapse, especially when he saw the first cracks beginning to spread across the throne’s crimson structure.
It was being crushed.
And if the throne shattered, Selene would be exposed completely.
At the same time, inside Luke’s heart, all five golden chains reacted.

They had already been clinging tightly around his heart, but now every one of them suddenly contracted with even greater force, squeezing his heart as though their message had become a command carved directly into his soul.
"Save her, or you will die!"
The contraction continued growing with every passing second, while the mysterious symbols engraved along the chains continued trying to suppress and weaken that pressure.
Yet their efforts were proving insufficient.
The chains kept tightening.
Luke’s heart kept compressing.
And the closer the Crimson Throne came to shattering, the stronger the warning inside his chest became.
At that moment, the System screen appeared directly before him.
[Luke, calm down!]
The System’s voice carried unusual urgency as it attempted to pull him back from the edge.
[Have faith in Selene!
She wouldn’t die from this!]
But Luke couldn’t calm himself.
His eyes remained fixed upon the gigantic serpent, and more importantly, upon the Crimson Throne trapped between its jaws, where cracks had already begun spreading across the crimson structure.
It wouldn’t hold for much longer.
And the moment it shattered, Selene would be left completely exposed.

chapters.title: Chapter 328: Two Gods Arrive... and Luke Is Caught in the Middle!
paragraphs: Crack!

The very thing Luke had been dreading finally happened as the crimson throne beneath Selene’s Blood Sovereign form shattered into fragments of condensed blood, leaving her exposed directly inside the jaws of the gigantic serpent, whose fangs were already closing around her body.
"Selene..." Luke muttered worriedly, his eyes remaining fixed on the scene despite the fact that he still couldn’t make his Void Step work.
With no other option available to him, Luke stared intensely toward the serpent’s mouth, silently hoping that Selene would regain control of her body before those fangs reached her.
But something completely unexpected happened instead.
The instant the serpent was about to close its jaws, the entire Heaven’s Crucible suddenly trembled as though a high-magnitude earthquake had erupted throughout the entire space.
"What’s happening?"
"Is Heaven’s Crucible breaking?"

The Sunborn warriors immediately became startled, their previous focus on the battlefield disappearing as they began looking around in confusion, desperately trying to determine where the strange disturbance had originated.

Even the Empyrean Academy representatives wore ugly expressions as they looked around, because everyone understood the danger of something happening to Heaven’s Crucible itself, and if this place truly began collapsing, they could all end up being buried inside it.
Then, above the sky of Heaven’s Crucible, something appeared.
A pair of enormous crimson eyes slowly opened.

The moment those eyes became visible, everyone who looked at them became completely mesmerized, because they were so beautiful and strangely captivating that controlling themselves became almost impossible.

One by one, the spectators stood from their seats as though their bodies were moving without their permission, and while their gazes remained locked upon those crimson eyes, thin streams of blood slowly began flowing from their own eyes.
Yet even as the blood continued trickling down their faces, none of them looked away.
It was as though even death itself could not force them to blink.
"Ughh..."
Luke was also staring toward the crimson eyes, but unlike everyone else, his reaction wasn’t quite the same.
His eyes merely became bloodshot, and although his vision was filled with red, no blood escaped from them.
The pressure on his mind, however, was completely different.

It felt as though his consciousness had been thrown inside a gigantic drum while a small hammer repeatedly struck its surface, sending violent waves of sound through his mind until his thoughts themselves began shaking apart.
"What’s this?" Luke muttered in confusion as he held his head, trying to withstand the pressure invading his consciousness.
At that moment, Sevaroth, who was floating beside him, stared toward the crimson eyes with an equally confused expression before quietly speaking the possibility that had just crossed his mind.
"A Demi-God?"
Luke’s eyes immediately widened, and his mouth opened completely upon hearing those words.
"A Demi-God here?"
He stared intently at the crimson eyes, unable to process what was happening, because never in his wildest expectations had he imagined that a Demi-God would actually appear within Heaven’s Crucible.
Not while Peiro was still here.
Yet before Luke could think any further, the crimson eyes shifted.
Their gaze moved away from the specters and focused directly upon the spectral serpent that had frozen in place from fear, with Selene’s Blood Sovereign body still trapped within its mouth.
The next moment, a pair of beautiful, mesmerizing lips manifested beneath those enormous crimson eyes.
Then a sweet, melody-filled voice emerged from them.
"A pet of Iveron~"
"Fufu~"
"But Iveron, don’t you think it’s too early to intervene?
The instant those words were completed, the very space of Heaven’s Crucible shattered like glass.
TINK...
KRRRK...
KRRRRAAAAAASH!!!
A gigantic spatial crack tore across the sky, and from the broken space beyond it, a crimson hand made entirely from solidified blood slowly emerged.
"The fck!"

Luke had finally recovered enough from the pressure affecting his ears and mind to speak clearly again, and he stared at the scene with wide eyes, because the appearance unfolding before him looked almost like the beginning of the world’s destruction.

Even Sevaroth became curious, because while everyone else was overwhelmed by what they were witnessing, he felt something different from the crimson hand, something that didn’t quite match the power level he had initially assumed.
Then another voice came from above.
"Sigh, I am getting rusty, that now even Demi-Gods are able to shatter Heaven’s Crucible’s space."
As those words spread through the arena, Peiro’s gigantic body suddenly began expanding.

His previous form grew until he became a ten-thousand-meter-tall blue spirit, and after reaching that size, he slowly lowered his enormous blue hands toward the approaching crimson hand and attempted to break it apart.
However, the instant Peiro’s hand touched the crimson hand, something completely unexpected happened.
His blue hand began turning crimson.
The color spread rapidly from the point of contact, covering more and more of his hand as though the crimson power were attempting to flow directly into him.
"Huh?" Peiro’s eyes widened.
"Divine Blood!"
Without hesitation, he severed his own right hand before the crimson substance could spread any farther throughout his body.
BOOOM!
His enormous detached hand crashed into the ground, shattering the earth beneath it and creating a gigantic crater.
Yet Peiro didn’t even look toward his fallen hand.

His widened eyes remained fixed on the crimson hand, which continued moving forward without the slightest interruption, completely ignoring his previous attempt to stop it as it reached toward the frozen spectral serpent.
"You are not a Demi-God!"
Peiro’s voice became serious.
"But a GOD!"
The words escaped his mouth, and the crimson lips immediately curved into a small, amused smile.
"Fufu~ Peiro, you have now become an ancient antique after your master used all your power during that day."
Peiro’s expression became ugly upon hearing those words, because he knew she was telling the truth.
He was no longer at his prime.

The nearly infinite amount of power he had once possessed had already been exhausted during that distant event, and the being before him clearly understood exactly how much weaker he had become since then.
Yet before Peiro could respond, the crimson hand continued forward and finally reached the spectral serpent.
Its fingers closed around the serpent’s head, completely trapping it within the crimson palm.
"Cutie, you shouldn’t have touched my descendant~" the mysterious woman said playfully, her sweet voice carrying an authority that made the surrounding space tremble.
With a simple movement of her hand, she broke the spectral serpent’s head apart and separated it completely from its enormous body.
Kshk!
BOOM!
The gigantic headless serpent body immediately dropped from the air and crashed into the ground, creating another crater beneath its enormous weight.
The crimson eyes, however, were no longer interested in the corpse.
Its attention shifted toward Selene’s Blood Sovereign body.
"Sigh, you are too weak to use its real power," the woman muttered with a trace of pity.
The next instant, the seven purple omen symbols embedded within Selene’s Blood Sovereign body suddenly disappeared.
At the same time, Selene’s gigantic Sovereign form reverted to her normal appearance, leaving her unconscious body resting within the crimson palm.
Yet before the mysterious woman could do anything else, her crimson eyes suddenly narrowed.
She looked toward the opposite side of Heaven’s Crucible.
"Peiro, it seems anyone can enter your little home nowadays~" she said playfully, and the teasing tone of her voice made Peiro’s already ugly expression become even darker.
He had felt it too. Someone else was coming.
And then it happened.
Another fracture appeared on the opposite side of Heaven’s Crucible, and just like the previous one, the surrounding space cracked apart as though made from glass.
KRRRRAAAAAK!!!
From within the broken space, a gigantic flaming hand emerged.
Above it, another pair of enormous eyes formed, followed by a mouth.
The newly arrived being slowly looked downward at the gathered specters, then shifted his attention toward Peiro, and finally toward Brynessa’s body lying within the arena.
His gaze remained upon her for a little longer than the others before finally turning toward the crimson eyes.
"Lilith, I didn’t expect you would come for your descendant."
The voice carried through the entire Heaven’s Crucible before the another amused voice came.
"And I also didn’t expect that you would come for your little toy."
Iveron’s mouth immediately closed.
There was no response.
But neither of them noticed that a small being was still present within the specter seat, fully awake, silently listening to every word they exchanged.
’Lilith? Iveron?’
Luke remained completely still, although not because he wanted to remain that way.
He simply couldn’t move.
Two different pressures were now bearing down upon his body, and each one was so powerful that merely existing beneath them made him feel as though his body could be crushed at any moment.
The same was true for every other specter.
From the Empyrean Academy representatives to the Sunborn warriors, from Mella to Marrec, none of them were spared from the overwhelming pressure radiating from the two divine beings.
Fortunately, Heaven’s Crucible was still protecting them.
Without Peiro’s protection, he was certain that the weaker spectators would have already been crushed into nothing more than meat paste merely by remaining within their presence.
Sevaroth, however, continued floating beside Luke as though nothing had happened, and after observing the crimson eyes carefully, he slowly nodded.
"No wonder she felt different earlier; she is a God, not a Demi-God."

chapters.title: Chapter 329: Luke Must Do What Even a God Failed to Do!
paragraphs: He nodded once more as he recalled the strange power he had sensed before.
Even now, however, Sevaroth couldn’t measure their true strength, because neither Lilith nor Iveron had actually descended here themselves.
Only their projections were present.
Hearing Sevaroth’s words, Luke didn’t react.
He didn’t dare.
He wasn’t even sure what these beings were capable of, and the last thing he wanted was to accidentally draw their attention toward himself.
More importantly, he didn’t know whether his Goddess of Light would send her own projection here.
And right now, with two Gods standing inside Heaven’s Crucible, Luke wasn’t sure whether the arrival of a third one would make his situation better...
...or far worse.

There, Iveron completely ignored Lilith and instead extended his hands toward the fallen remains of the ten-thousand-foot-long spectral serpent, carefully grasping its gigantic body before bringing it closer to Brynessa’s own serpent body, and the instant the two came within range of one another, an unfamiliar surge of power began gathering around them.
OHMMMM!

A tremendous influx of energy suddenly erupted from Iveron’s projection, causing the entire Heaven’s Crucible to tremble once again as though the very space itself was struggling to withstand the force being released, and under that overwhelming flow of energy, the spectral serpent’s body slowly began merging into Brynessa’s serpent body.
The two forms fused together.

The spectral serpent gradually disappeared into Brynessa, while her existing body expanded further and further until a completely new serpent form emerged from the fusion, one that had now reached ten thousand feet in length, yet still possessed Brynessa’s original serpent head.

Lilith watched the entire process calmly without making any attempt to interfere, because although she clearly possessed enough power to stop Iveron, neither of them could start a Divine War inside this place, at least not right now.
Still, that didn’t mean she had to remain silent.
"Iveron, you sure have gotten impatient, considering that you are already spreading your hands toward Valtharion."
She paused briefly before adding in her usual playful tone,
"Do you really want a hero that badly?"
Iveron didn’t answer.
Instead, both his eyes and Lilith’s crimson eyes slowly shifted in the same direction, and after looking through the gathered specters, they stopped upon a certain person.
This time, Luke was the one who froze.
His entire body stiffened under the attention of the two Gods.
"Hmm, this hero does seem different~" Lilith said playfully.
Her tone remained light, but Luke could feel the attention behind those words, while Iveron continued staring at him without speaking, carrying an emotion in his eyes that Luke couldn’t understand.
Lilith noticed that Iveron still wasn’t saying anything, and she clearly couldn’t resist teasing him further, she smiled.
"Iveron, you don’t deserve the Fire Authority, because you never seem to get angry like the usual Fire God."
At those words, the corner of Iveron’s mouth twitched slightly, almost as though he were silently telling her to look at herself before criticizing someone else.
Lilith noticed his expression, and her smile widened.
"Fufu~"
She then lowered her gaze toward Luke again, bringing the enormous crimson eyes slightly closer to him before speaking in a playful tone.
"Kid, we know you are awake.
Luke didn’t move.
Normally, after becoming a Titan, he rarely experienced something as ordinary as sweating from fear, yet those few words from Lilith somehow caused his Titan body to sweat anyway.
He still didn’t dare to react.
Seeing that Luke remained completely silent, Lilith continued speaking as though she didn’t particularly care whether he answered her or not.
"Sigh, kids nowadays are so troublesome, and my descendant chose such a boring husband for herself."
Luke’s mouth almost twitched at that statement, but he managed to suppress the reaction through sheer force of will.
[With fear, not with willpower. ¬‿¬]
Luke ignored the System’s message because by now he already understood that the System wasn’t going to provide him with any useful help in this situation.
[Luke, just chill. They wouldn’t dare to attack you directly, because the Goddess of Light is behind you.]
[And even if they actually tried something, don’t worry, Sevaroth is still here.]
Luke became slightly confused upon hearing that.
’Sevaroth?’
Sevaroth was currently in spirit form, and as far as Luke knew, he shouldn’t have been able to use his true power.

[Well, he can’t properly use it in Valtharion, but here, where Valtharion’s influence is only half-present, he can act, although the price will be sleep. Your Titan Spirits aren’t just there for decoration, after all.]

[That is also one of the reasons those two Gods were able to send their projections here, because outside this place, inside Valtharion itself, such a thing would be impossible without some kind of container.]
Before Luke could process that information, Lilith suddenly spoke again.
"Hmm, he is talking with someone~"
Her gigantic crimson eyes and beautiful mouth suddenly moved closer to Luke, coming so near that he felt as though she might simply swallow him in the next second.
Luke instinctively closed his eyes.
Nothing happened.
After a few moments, he slowly opened them again, feeling a small amount of relief when he realized that Lilith hadn’t actually done anything.
"Fufu~"
"Don’t worry, I am not going to kill my descendant’s husband, and your Goddess wouldn’t appreciate that."
Lilith’s gaze shifted away from Luke and toward Iveron, who was now looking toward the ancient gate with an expression filled with memories that no one else present could understand.
"And he wouldn’t dare kill you here either, since I am here."
Iveron still didn’t respond.
The next moment, his fiery eyes, hand, and mouth gradually disappeared, and along with him, Marrec, Mella, and Brynessa’s body also vanished from the Heavan’s Crucible.
FWOSH!
Lilith watched the empty space for a moment before sighing.
"Sigh, he’s gone, no fun."
’Miss, it’s actually good that he is gone, because he is a Demon God while I am merely a weak D-rank being, so staying around higher-ranked beings like him isn’t exactly healthy for my weak heart.’
’Hell, I’m just waiting for the moment you leave as well.’
Luke barely finished thinking those words when Lilith’s playful voice immediately reached him.
"Fufu~ Are you thinking about when I would leave?"
Luke’s body stiffened again.
He immediately shook his head, absolutely unwilling to admit that she had guessed correctly.
Lilith’s mouth curved downward slightly as though she had become genuinely sad.
"In my youth, there was a line of men who wanted to meet me and spend time with me, but now, here I am, and even the husband of my own descendant doesn’t want to spend time with me."
Luke’s face remained completely expressionless.
Inside, however, he was screaming.
’Miss, please think before saying.’
He desperately wanted her to reconsider the wording of her own sentence.

After another sigh, Lilith finally looked toward Peiro, who was standing farther away with his regenerated hands restored, although his expression was still extremely unpleasant after everything that had happened.
"Aww, don’t be mad, Peiro, I am leaving."
She waved her hand toward him playfully.
Then, without giving anyone another chance to react, all the remaining specters were suddenly teleported away from the area.
Lilith’s crimson eyes and mouth disappeared along with Selene, and the oppressive pressure that had been weighing upon the entire battlefield finally vanished.
"Huff!"
Luke finally released the breath he had been holding, deeply inhaling and exhaling now that the terrifying pressure from the two Gods had disappeared.
Meanwhile, Peiro repaired the two spatial fractures that had been torn open inside Heaven’s Crucible before turning his gaze downward toward Luke.
"Kid, all of them have returned to their places."
He was referring to the places from which the specters had originally come, meaning that everyone else had now been sent back to their respective locations.
Hearing those words, Luke immediately felt some relief because it meant that once he finally left this place, he would be able to meet Selene again.
However, another question soon entered his mind.
"Then why am I still here?"

A faint smile appeared on Peiro’s face when he heard that question, because if Luke succeeded in accomplishing what he was about to attempt, Peiro himself might finally be able to free himself from this place, where he had remained bound for so long while being forced to maintain and organize the arena.
"You have to open that door and defeat the being inside, and once you do that, you will find the strength you need to become stronger."
Luke looked toward the ancient gate.

He couldn’t help sighing upon hearing Peiro’s words, because he had already suspected that this ancient gate was connected to the Origin fragment gate he had encountered earlier, and after everything that had happened, it increasingly felt as though all of these events had ultimately been leading toward this exact moment.
"Fine."
Luke accepted the challenge.
The next moment, Peiro moved his power, and Luke’s body was instantly teleported away from the spectator area.
He reappeared directly in front of the ancient gate, while the arena and the space where the previous battle had taken place now remained behind him.
Peiro stayed where he was, folding his hands as he looked at Luke from a distance.
"Try your best, kid."

His expression carried genuine interest as he waited to see whether Luke could actually accomplish the impossible task placed before him, which even Iveron hadn’t able to do, because if Luke really managed to open that ancient gate and defeat whatever existed beyond it, then perhaps this young bring truly possessed the ability to reach the strength required for what was waiting ahead.
’Those Beings.’

Even now, however, Sevaroth couldn’t measure their true strength, because neither Lilith nor Iveron had actually descended here themselves.
Only their projections were present.
Hearing Sevaroth’s words, Luke didn’t react.
He didn’t dare.
He wasn’t even sure what these beings were capable of, and the last thing he wanted was to accidentally draw their attention toward himself.
More importantly, he didn’t know whether his Goddess of Light would send her own projection here.
And right now, with two Gods standing inside Heaven’s Crucible, Luke wasn’t sure whether the arrival of a third one would make his situation better...
...or far worse.

There, Iveron completely ignored Lilith and instead extended his hands toward the fallen remains of the ten-thousand-foot-long spectral serpent, carefully grasping its gigantic body before bringing it closer to Brynessa’s own serpent body, and the instant the two came within range of one another, an unfamiliar surge of power began gathering around them.
OHMMMM!

A tremendous influx of energy suddenly erupted from Iveron’s projection, causing the entire Heaven’s Crucible to tremble once again as though the very space itself was struggling to withstand the force being released, and under that overwhelming flow of energy, the spectral serpent’s body slowly began merging into Brynessa’s serpent body.
The two forms fused together.

The spectral serpent gradually disappeared into Brynessa, while her existing body expanded further and further until a completely new serpent form emerged from the fusion, one that had now reached ten thousand feet in length, yet still possessed Brynessa’s original serpent head.

Lilith watched the entire process calmly without making any attempt to interfere, because although she clearly possessed enough power to stop Iveron, neither of them could start a Divine War inside this place, at least not right now.
Still, that didn’t mean she had to remain silent.
"Iveron, you sure have gotten impatient, considering that you are already spreading your hands toward Valtharion."
She paused briefly before adding in her usual playful tone,
"Do you really want a hero that badly?"
Iveron didn’t answer.
Instead, both his eyes and Lilith’s crimson eyes slowly shifted in the same direction, and after looking through the gathered specters, they stopped upon a certain person.
This time, Luke was the one who froze.
His entire body stiffened under the attention of the two Gods.
"Hmm, this hero does seem different~" Lilith said playfully.
Her tone remained light, but Luke could feel the attention behind those words, while Iveron continued staring at him without speaking, carrying an emotion in his eyes that Luke couldn’t understand.
Lilith noticed that Iveron still wasn’t saying anything, and she clearly couldn’t resist teasing him further, she smiled.
"Iveron, you don’t deserve the Fire Authority, because you never seem to get angry like the usual Fire God."
At those words, the corner of Iveron’s mouth twitched slightly, almost as though he were silently telling her to look at herself before criticizing someone else.
Lilith noticed his expression, and her smile widened.
"Fufu~"
She then lowered her gaze toward Luke again, bringing the enormous crimson eyes slightly closer to him before speaking in a playful tone.
"Kid, we know you are awake.
Luke didn’t move.
Normally, after becoming a Titan, he rarely experienced something as ordinary as sweating from fear, yet those few words from Lilith somehow caused his Titan body to sweat anyway.
He still didn’t dare to react.
Seeing that Luke remained completely silent, Lilith continued speaking as though she didn’t particularly care whether he answered her or not.
"Sigh, kids nowadays are so troublesome, and my descendant chose such a boring husband for herself."
Luke’s mouth almost twitched at that statement, but he managed to suppress the reaction through sheer force of will.
[With fear, not with willpower. ¬‿¬]
Luke ignored the System’s message because by now he already understood that the System wasn’t going to provide him with any useful help in this situation.
[Luke, just chill.
They wouldn’t dare to attack you directly, because the Goddess of Light is behind you.]
[And even if they actually tried something, don’t worry, Sevaroth is still here.]
Luke became slightly confused upon hearing that.
’Sevaroth?’
Sevaroth was currently in spirit form, and as far as Luke knew, he shouldn’t have been able to use his true power.
[Well, he can’t properly use it in Valtharion, but here, where Valtharion’s influence is only half-present, he can act, although the price will be sleep.
Your Titan Spirits aren’t just there for decoration, after all.]

[That is also one of the reasons those two Gods were able to send their projections here, because outside this place, inside Valtharion itself, such a thing would be impossible without some kind of container.]
Before Luke could process that information, Lilith suddenly spoke again.
"Hmm, he is talking with someone~"
Her gigantic crimson eyes and beautiful mouth suddenly moved closer to Luke, coming so near that he felt as though she might simply swallow him in the next second.
Luke instinctively closed his eyes.
Nothing happened.
After a few moments, he slowly opened them again, feeling a small amount of relief when he realized that Lilith hadn’t actually done anything.
"Fufu~"
"Don’t worry, I am not going to kill my descendant’s husband, and your Goddess wouldn’t appreciate that."
Lilith’s gaze shifted away from Luke and toward Iveron, who was now looking toward the ancient gate with an expression filled with memories that no one else present could understand.
"And he wouldn’t dare kill you here either, since I am here."
Iveron still didn’t respond.
The next moment, his fiery eyes, hand, and mouth gradually disappeared, and along with him, Marrec, Mella, and Brynessa’s body also vanished from the Heavan’s Crucible.
FWOSH!
Lilith watched the empty space for a moment before sighing.
"Sigh, he’s gone, no fun."
’Miss, it’s actually good that he is gone, because he is a Demon God while I am merely a weak D-rank being, so staying around higher-ranked beings like him isn’t exactly healthy for my weak heart.’
’Hell, I’m just waiting for the moment you leave as well.’

"Aww, don’t be mad, Peiro, I am leaving."

chapters.title: Chapter 330: The Origin Fragment Doesn’t Recognize Luke?!
paragraphs: Luke took a deep breath before stepping several meters away from the ancient gate, giving himself enough room to build momentum and prepare properly.
Before he could begin, however, Peiro’s voice came from behind him.
"Kid, use your full strength. Before you, many Champions tried to open this gate, and every single one of them failed, including Iveron."
Luke’s expression immediately turned strange as he glanced back at him. "If even a god couldn’t open it, then how exactly am I supposed to do it as a D-Rank?"
Peiro shook his head. "That’s not how this gate works. It tests your strength according to the peak of your current realm."
He looked toward the towering ancient gate before continuing, "So, if you can produce strength equivalent to the strongest D-Rank of your species, the gate will open."
Hearing that, Luke finally understood and nodded slightly.
’Peak D-Rank Titan strength.’

Of course, his bloodline still hadn’t completely transformed into that of a true Firstborn Pure Titan, which meant he didn’t need to compare himself with the absolute peak among Titan bloodlines. At the very least, however, he would need to reach the Peak D-Rank physical standard of a Titan.
"Easy."

A confident smile appeared on Luke’s face because he already knew just how absurd Titan physiques became when compared with ordinary races. Even at D-Rank, a Titan could display physical strength capable of competing with humans far above the same realm, and although Luke didn’t know exactly how far a Peak D-Rank Titan could push that difference, he knew it would certainly be beyond anything his normal human body could achieve.
Without his Titan form, even after using everything available to him, his current body could only produce physical strength somewhere around Early C-Rank.
"Let’s do this."
Luke planted his feet firmly against the stone floor before calling upon the Titan that represented his greatest raw physical strength.
"Come forth!"
His voice echoed throughout the arena.
"Azrion! The Atlas Titan!"
RUMBLE—!
The instant those words left his mouth, the ancient gate suddenly released an overwhelming pressure, as though the entire structure had come alive and dropped its full weight directly onto Luke.
"What the—?!"
Luke’s body jerked backward as the pressure slammed into him, and for a brief moment, it genuinely felt as though an entire mountain had been placed against his chest.
’At least let my transformation finish, damn it!’

Luke groaned through clenched teeth as the muscles along his arms, shoulders, thighs, and back swelled violently under the sudden strain. His feet dug into the stone floor, cracking several tiles beneath him as the weight continued forcing his body backward.
For a moment, it looked as though the gate might simply crush him before Azrion’s transformation could even complete.
"NULLEX!"
Luke roared, and Nullex immediately responded.

White, mirror-like material spread over his body within an instant, wrapping around his limbs, chest, head, and back until his entire figure was enclosed within the armor. At the same time, four thick pillars formed from Nullex’s material and erupted from his back, extending backward in perfectly straight lines before slamming against the ground.
THUMP! THUMP! THUMP! THUMP!
All four pillars embedded themselves firmly into the stone, reinforcing Luke’s position and preventing his body from being pushed any farther.
With Nullex helping bear the pressure coming from the gate, Luke finally managed to stabilize himself.
’Thanks, Nullex.’
He released a strained breath just as Azrion’s transformation fully began.
His body expanded rapidly while Nullex continuously shifted along with him, metallic plates separating, enlarging, and locking back together around his growing frame.
CLICK—CLACK—CLANK!

Luke’s muscles thickened and reshaped themselves as the Atlas Titan physique emerged, every part of his body becoming proportionally larger and more powerful until, beneath Peiro’s calm gaze, a fifty-foot-tall Titan stood before the ancient gate, completely covered in Nullex’s almost mirror-white armor.
"HAH!"
Luke forced both hands forward and released his full physical strength.
Power surged from his legs, passed through his waist and shoulders, then gathered behind his arms as he pushed against the ancient gate with everything Azrion’s body could produce.
The tilted gate slowly began moving.
GRRRRRRNNNNN—!

Its ancient structure groaned under the force as Luke steadily pushed it back toward its original position, and the surrounding wall shifted along with it, extending behind the gate instead of exposing whatever lay beyond and forming something resembling a stone tunnel around its enormous frame.
Luke didn’t pay attention to any of that, because every bit of his concentration remained fixed on forcing the gate upright.

His feet continued grinding against the floor while his arms trembled beneath the weight, and only after nearly a full minute of continuous pressure did the ancient gate finally return to its original position.
Luke exhaled heavily.
"Now the real thing."

At his command, the four support pillars behind him withdrew and merged back into Nullex, while a layer of invisible Force spread across his Titan body, reinforcing his muscles and wrapping around his entire frame.
Luke tightened his grip against the gate.
"THIS GATE CAN’T STOP ME!"
With a roar, he drove everything forward at once.
BOOOOOOM—!
The thousand-foot-long ancient gate finally moved.
Its enormous structure swung inward under Luke’s strength before violently colliding with the interior wall.
BANG—!
The impact rolled through the chamber like thunder, while the opening behind it finally became visible.
"This..."
Luke’s eyes widened completely.
Beyond the gate wasn’t another ordinary chamber or hallway.
An entire world stretched before him.
Mountains rose across the distant land while vast seas reflected the strange light hanging above them, creating a landscape far too large to possibly exist behind the gate he had just opened.
Yet Luke barely paid attention to either.
His gaze had already locked onto the figure floating in the center of that world.
A one-thousand-foot-tall crystalline body stood upright in midair, completely motionless.
Peiro’s voice came from behind him.
"Impressive. You actually managed to open it."
Luke remained focused on the distant crystal figure while Peiro continued, and for once, there was clear satisfaction in the ancient spirit’s voice.
"That makes you the first person who has successfully opened this gate."
A faint smile appeared on Peiro’s face as he looked toward Luke, seemingly believing that this time, someone might finally complete the Origin Fragment’s trial.
"Now go and complete the trials. If you succeed, you may obtain the strength that even the forgotten desire."
The moment those words ended, Peiro’s body disappeared.
Before Luke could respond, an invisible force pulled him through the opening and into the world beyond.
The ancient gate immediately began closing behind him.
BAAAANG—!
Its thunderous impact echoed across the mountains and seas, but Luke barely reacted because his attention was still fixed on the gigantic figure floating in the distance.
"Earlier, it was a stone body... and this time, it’s crystal."
Luke narrowed his eyes and carefully observed the new Origin Titan manifestation.

Its entire thousand-foot frame was almost transparent, while faint white lines flowed beneath its surface and spread throughout its limbs, torso, and head like veins of light trapped inside crystal. Its exterior remained mostly smooth, although several sections naturally extended into sharp geometric formations, making the body resemble a single colossal crystal that had somehow been carved into the shape of a Titan.
Luke continued studying it.

The First Origin Fragment he had encountered represented Strength, and its Stone Body had perfectly reflected that Aspect, which made him increasingly curious about what this crystalline body represented.
At that moment, Sevaroth materialized beside him and began floating through the air while looking around at the mountains, distant seas, and finally the thousand-foot crystalline Titan.
"Is this the Origin Titan you told me about?"
"Only a fragment," Luke corrected him.

Even after hearing that, Sevaroth’s attention remained fixed on the crystalline figure because, just like Nyx and the others, he had heard stories concerning the Origin Titan long before meeting Luke.
Among the oldest Titan legends, there were whispers that before even the Firstborn Titans appeared within the universe, another existence had already been present—the Origin Titan.

Very little reliable information remained about it, and most Titans had eventually treated the story as little more than an ancient legend, because no one had ever found the Origin Titan itself. The only consistent claim surviving across those stories was that the Origin Titan possessed the power to control all forces and elements.
While Sevaroth continued observing the figure, the crystal Titan’s eyes suddenly opened.
Its gaze immediately fell upon Luke.
Luke noticed it at the same instant, because his attention had never left the body in the first place.
The Origin Fragment stared at him for several moments before finally speaking.
"Another Hero."
"Hello."
Luke greeted it in his usual casual manner, which seemed to draw a faint trace of curiosity from the Origin Fragment.
"It seems you have either encountered another fragment of mine or already heard about me."
The crystalline figure paused before carefully observing Luke’s body, but even after nearly a minute, the confusion surrounding its gaze didn’t disappear.
"You don’t possess an Origin Fragment."
It looked at Luke more carefully.
"Did you lose against my other self?"
Luke initially became confused by the question before quickly realizing what had happened.
’Right. The System absorbed that Fragment when it evolved my Origin Skill.’
The previous Origin Fragment no longer existed separately inside him, so naturally this one couldn’t sense it.
"Yeah."
Luke answered nonchalantly.

The Origin Fragment showed no noticeable reaction, although Luke wasn’t sure whether it actually could, considering its entire face was made from solid crystal. It possessed visible eyes and a mouth, but no other facial features capable of displaying normal expressions.

During their conversation, Luke had already returned to his ordinary human form, while Nullex had also disappeared from his body. Strangely, despite losing his Titan form and armor, he remained suspended in midair without needing to actively maintain himself there.
After a brief silence, the Origin Fragment finally continued.
"Well, whether you failed before doesn’t matter. The fact that you successfully opened this gate means you possess enough potential to attempt my trial."

Luke’s expression became more attentive at those words, because he wanted to finish whatever trial awaited him as quickly as possible, especially while the System’s earlier warning still lingered in the back of his mind.
The gigantic crystalline figure looked directly at him.
"I am an Origin Fragment of the Origin Titan, and the Aspect held within me is—Adaptation."
Its voice spread across the open world before it paused and asked,
"What Aspect did the Fragment you encountered before possess?"
"Strength," Luke replied calmly.
The Origin Fragment gave a slow nod.
"Strength... yes, that Fragment was always powerful. To overcome its trial, you would have needed to surpass the strength it placed before you."
Luke didn’t respond and simply remained silent, waiting for the Origin Fragment to explain what kind of trial awaited him this time.

chapters.title: Chapter 331: Something Is Wrong With This Origin Titan!
paragraphs: The Origin Titan didn’t seem bothered by Luke’s silence and continued calmly, "Since you have already faced one of my fragments before, I will be direct with you this time."
"My realm is the same as before, which means that since you are currently D-Rank, this body has been set at Peak D-Rank according to the base physical standard of the strongest Titan species."
Luke’s expression immediately changed as confusion appeared in his eyes.
’System, wasn’t the difficulty supposed to be Peak B-Rank?’
The System responded almost immediately.
[Luke, I displayed the difficulty according to human combat standards so that you could make a more accurate comparison.]

Hearing that explanation, Luke slowly nodded, because that meant the Titan standing before him was still technically Peak D-Rank, yet its actual combat strength could reach the level of a Peak B-Rank human.
Luke remained silent for a moment before his eyes widened.
’Wait, a Peak D-Rank Titan can reach Peak B-Rank combat strength? Are you kidding me?!’
That sounded absurd even by Titan standards, because the previous Origin Fragment had also possessed the peak strength of his realm, yet Luke didn’t remember it feeling anywhere near this ridiculous.
Before he could continue questioning it, another System screen appeared before his eyes.
[Keep listening to his explanation and you will understand why.]
Luke immediately stopped thinking about it and returned his attention to the Origin Titan, although the crystalline figure had already noticed his distracted expression.
"Were you speaking with someone?"
Luke shook his head without hesitation.

He had already noticed long ago that whenever he communicated with the System or his Titans internally, his expression sometimes became distant enough that other people could tell he was listening to someone, although he had no intention of explaining anything whenever they asked.
"No."
The Origin Titan stared at him for a moment before simply nodding. "Very well."
It clearly didn’t care enough to press the matter and instead continued explaining the rules of the trial.
"This Fragment embodies the Aspect of Adaptation, and your objective is simple: you must destroy this body."
The Origin Titan paused briefly before adding, "However, there is one condition you should understand before you begin."
"Every time you attack me, regardless of the method you use, this entire Crystal Body will adapt to that attack and become increasingly resistant to the same form of damage."
Luke’s eyes narrowed slightly.
The Origin Titan continued before he could respond.

"For your information, you will not be able to destroy this body during your first three attacks, even if you use your strongest technique, because I established that restriction as part of the trial itself, which means wasting your greatest attack during those first three attempts would accomplish nothing."
It then added another condition.

"However, you cannot exploit that rule by using insignificant attacks. Each of your first three attacks must contain at least thirty percent of the peak offensive power you can currently produce in whatever form you are using."
The Origin Titan stopped speaking for several seconds, allowing Luke enough time to properly understand the rules before continuing.
"You will have one full day."
"Within that time, you must completely destroy this body."
After saying that, the Origin Titan unexpectedly let out a sigh.
Luke immediately noticed it and became confused, because he couldn’t understand why something like this would cause the Fragment to react that way, although the answer came only a moment later.
"Unfortunately, the previous Hero who attempted this trial failed."
Luke’s gaze sharpened slightly.
’Why does he sound disappointed about that?’
More importantly, the mention of a previous Hero immediately caught his attention.
"What was the previous Hero of Light’s name?"
The Origin Titan slowly raised its head, and for the first time, clear confusion appeared within its crystalline eyes.
"Hero of Light?"
It looked directly at Luke before answering, "No. The one who came before you was the Hero of Space."
"O_O"
Luke’s mouth opened completely as he stared at the Fragment.
’What the hell?’

Until now, Luke had assumed that these Origin Fragment trials were connected specifically to the Hero of Light, especially because Peiro had just told him that he was the first person capable of opening the ancient gate.
He immediately asked, "Then how did the Hero of Space enter this place if I was supposedly the first person who managed to open that gate?"
The Origin Titan shook its head.
"The Hero of Space never entered through the gate."
"He teleported directly inside."
Luke’s expression became even stranger.
’Okay, now this is getting absurd.’
If Peiro had been outside at the time, then simply bypassing the entire gate and teleporting directly into this world should have required a ridiculous level of spatial control.
However, another possibility quickly came to Luke’s mind.
’What if he didn’t come here shortly after awakening?’

If the Hero of Space had arrived much later in his journey, after becoming significantly stronger and developing greater control over his authority, then teleporting into this place suddenly seemed far more believable. There was also the possibility that the god or goddess supporting that Hero had helped him reach this location.
While Luke was considering those possibilities, the Origin Titan continued without paying any attention to his confusion.
"The Hero of Space had already encountered another Origin Fragment before reaching me, and he successfully completed its trial."
Luke’s expression changed again.
’So other gods and goddesses were also interested in the Origin Titan.’

He immediately remembered his earlier conversations with the System, where it had become clear that many divine beings were trying to guide their Heroes toward forgotten powers and ancient existences.
Until now, Luke had assumed that because the Goddess of Light was pursuing the Origin Titan, the other gods would each be seeking entirely different forgotten existences.
Apparently, that assumption wasn’t completely correct.

The Origin Titan continued, "The Fragment conquered by the Hero of Space possessed the Aspect known as Distance, and at its true peak, even a single centimeter could be extended into a distance measured in light-years."
Luke’s mouth twitched violently.
’Then how the hell did the Hero of Space complete that trial?’
Almost as though it had noticed what Luke was thinking, the Origin Titan gave a faint laugh.
"Haha, I am speaking about when, I’m at my peak, when I possessed all my original power."
Luke released a small breath of relief.
’Alright, good.’

For a moment, he had thought the Fragment inside that origin titan, which hero of space face, could casually turn one centimeter into several light-years, which would have made the entire situation completely ridiculous. And he didn’t have to face that trial.
Unfortunately, that relief lasted only a few seconds.
The Origin Titan looked at him and said in the same calm tone, "Even so, the Hero of Space failed my trial."
Luke waited for the rest.
"And I ate him."
Luke became completely silent.
Sevaroth, who had been floating beside him throughout the conversation, also stopped moving for a moment, while even the System failed to immediately say anything.
An awkward silence settled over the strange world as the distant mountains remained motionless beneath the pale sky and the seas below reflected the gigantic crystalline figure hovering above them.
Luke’s eye twitched.
’Wait, System, you already knew about this, so why are you joining us in being silent?’
[Tch! You never let me participate in anything.]
Luke ignored the System’s childish complaint and immediately started connecting the information with everything he had learned earlier.
The System Quest had already hinted that something unusual was waiting here, and it had also stated that his Origin Skill would rank up twice after completing this part of the quest.
Now the reason suddenly became obvious.

If the Adaptation Fragment had killed and absorbed the Hero of Space, and that Hero had already obtained another Origin Fragment before coming here, then both fragments should still be present within this body.
Luke slowly looked toward the thousand-foot Crystal Body.
"Fragment of Adaptation... and Fragment of Distance."
The moment those words left his mouth, the gigantic crystalline body began to change.

A faint tremor passed through its transparent frame before something started emerging from deep within the crystal, initially appearing as a small shape buried near the center of its torso before rapidly expanding outward.
CRRRRKKK—!
Layers of crystal shifted apart as a second Titan body began growing around the original one.

The new body was formed from pale, nearly transparent glass, and as it expanded, reflections of distant mountains, seas, skies, and horizons began appearing across its surface as though entire landscapes had somehow become trapped within the material.
Within the center of that growing glass body, Luke could still clearly see the original Crystal Body suspended inside.
His expression immediately changed.
’Don’t freaking tell me...’
A bad premonition rose inside him as the new body continued expanding until it completely surrounded the Adaptation Fragment.
The Origin Titan’s voice then confirmed exactly what Luke had feared.
"The conditions of the trial have changed."
Luke stared at the newly formed Horizon Glass Body while the Origin Titan continued speaking from inside it.
"You must now cross this body, reach the Crystal Body at its center, and then destroy the Crystal Body before the trial ends."
Luke’s mouth twitched as he looked from the outer glass body toward the smaller crystalline figure trapped deep within its center.
"Sigh... alright, now this is getting out of control."
However, before he could complain any further, something changed.
The Origin Titan’s crystalline eyes, which had remained calm throughout their entire conversation, slowly turned crimson.
The change spread across both eyes until every trace of their original color disappeared, leaving behind a deep red glow that looked completely unnatural against the pale crystal.
Luke’s expression immediately hardened.
’Yeah... there it is.’
He finally understood the strange behavior, the altered trial, and why the Origin Fragment had killed the previous Hero instead of simply allowing him to fail.
’The corruption.’
Luke stared at the crimson eyes shining from within the Horizon Glass Body as the uneasy feeling inside him became certainty.
’This Titan Fragment has been corrupted.’

chapters.title: Chapter 332: At the Same Realm, Even Gods Can’t Defeat Me!
paragraphs: At that moment, Luke raised his eyes and looked directly into the Origin Titan’s crimson gaze, where traces of dark miasma continued leaking outward and made it increasingly obvious that the Fragment was no longer completely in its right mind.
"Do you know what I did with the Strength Fragment?"
The Origin Titan’s expression remained calm, although his crimson eyes stayed fixed on Luke as he asked, "What did you do? Didn’t you fail its trial?"
"Nah."

Luke shook his head with a quiet laugh, because although he had always felt weak whenever he compared himself with the existences standing far above him, every increase in realm, every newly unlocked Titan, and every portion of their forbidden power that became available to him had gradually changed that feeling.
He had finally begun to understand exactly what kind of power he possessed.
"I showed him why I am a perfect Titan."
The Origin Titan clearly didn’t understand what Luke meant, but Luke didn’t care enough to explain immediately and simply continued while looking straight into those crimson eyes.
"He wanted to test whether my strength could overcome his, so I showed him that his strength was never even close to mine."

A fierce light burned within Luke’s eyes as his body began transforming into Vorthar, the fusion between the Void Titan and Atlas Titan, while the confidence in his voice carried none of the uncertainty he once would have felt when standing before an existence like this.
This confidence hadn’t appeared from arrogance alone.
Luke had earned it through every fight that had nearly broken his body and every power he had slowly learned to control.
"At the same realm, even gods can’t defeat me!"
For the first time since their conversation began, the Origin Titan’s expression visibly changed.

Until now, the Fragment had paid far more attention to Luke’s current realm than to the strange composition of his body, which still possessed only portions of Titan-converted bloodlines instead of being completely transformed into that of a Firstborn Pure Titan.
However, the moment it looked deeper, that assumption began falling apart.
Those incomplete Titan bloodlines weren’t ordinary.
Each belonged to a Firstborn Titan, and Luke’s body somehow carried four of them simultaneously without suffering the slightest visible backlash from their coexistence.
’So he possesses the peak bloodlines of their kind...’
As that realization formed, another emotion quietly surfaced within the corrupted Fragment, resembling the same jealousy that the Strength Fragment had once felt toward Luke.
’His body carries bloodlines belonging to those who earned the title of Warden.’
While the Origin Titan was processing that discovery, Luke’s transformation had already finished.

His body now stood seventy feet tall in the form of Vorthar, with the perfectly proportioned physique created from the fusion of Atlas strength and Void nature, while Elythos spread over him in streams of golden-white light until the Armor of the Cosmic Heart covered his entire body from head to toe.
Luke slowly flexed his armored hand before looking back toward the Origin Titan.
"I don’t need three attacks."
His voice remained calm.
"One will be enough."
The Origin Titan’s crimson eyes narrowed slightly as miasma continued drifting from them.

"Don’t become delusional, young Titan. If you intend to destroy this body with a single attack and break the rule established by my Origin Fragment, then unless your attack possesses enough strength to surpass Peak B-Rank by your own standards, you should forget about even leaving a scratch."

Luke didn’t seem bothered by the warning because opportunities where he could genuinely unleash everything were rare, with the Valtharion Tribulation being one of the few times he had pushed his abilities far enough to destroy the Essence Clouds above him.
This time, he didn’t intend to hold anything back either.
"Come."
Luke whispered the word, and twelve different points in the Void behind him immediately rippled.

Dark distortions spread across the air before twelve figures emerged one after another, each carrying Luke’s appearance while already transformed into the Cosmic Heart Titan, their twenty-foot-tall bodies floating silently behind Vorthar.

The sudden appearance of twelve additional Lukes caused the Origin Titan’s attention to shift toward them, while Sevaroth, who was still floating nearby, also narrowed his eyes after realizing what Luke intended to attempt.
Before Luke could continue, the System’s warning appeared.
[Luke, don’t be foolish! After you became a real Titan, those bodies no longer act automatically because you are subconsciously controlling every single one yourself.]
[Your current mental strength isn’t sufficient to properly control this many separate selves at the same time.]
’I know.’
Luke didn’t stop.
’They only need to do one thing.’
He divided his concentration among the twelve bodies, and under his control, every Cosmic Heart Titan raised one hand at almost the same moment.
THUMP! THUMP! THUMP!
Their Cosmic Hearts began pulsing heavily as large amounts of Cosmic Energy surged through their bodies before pouring outward.
Above them, twelve miniature Cosmic Systems gradually manifested across the sky.

Asteroids, comets, moons, planets, and suns appeared within those systems as their gravitational fields began interacting with the surrounding world, while waves of heat spread through the air and space itself showed faint distortions around several of the larger celestial bodies.

Even without detonating them, the combined gravity and heat were already placing strain upon the surrounding space, which made it obvious that allowing those systems to collapse uncontrollably would produce consequences Luke had no desire to experience.
Still, he wasn’t finished.
Under the increasingly confused gaze of the Origin Titan, Luke began rearranging the celestial bodies.
Asteroids moved first, followed by comets, then moons and planets, while the suns gradually shifted toward the rear of the growing alignment.
’What is he trying to do?’
The Origin Titan observed the formation carefully.

He could clearly sense the energy stored inside those celestial bodies, yet even if Luke detonated everything simultaneously, the resulting destructive power still shouldn’t be enough to cleanly surpass Peak B-Rank.
More importantly, another problem immediately became obvious.
’Can his body even channel that much power?’
It was the same question almost everyone eventually asked whenever they saw Luke attempting to combine Caelith’s cosmic techniques with the body of the Atlas Titan.
This time, however, the Origin Titan’s concern wasn’t entirely wrong.
Even with Vorthar’s fused physique, Luke’s current D-Rank body couldn’t properly control the technique he was preparing.

At Vorthar’s true peak, the fusion body was supposed to possess the capability to carry the weight of the Endless Void itself, but Luke was nowhere near that level yet, and although his numerous stat multipliers had pushed his raw physical strength far beyond what an ordinary D-Rank should possess, there were still limits to how much force his current body could direct.
Vorthar could withstand the burden of the upcoming technique.
Controlling that burden was another matter.
Which was why Luke intended to borrow something else.
Using Myrkhal’s Form Assimilation, he replaced one of the two hearts within Vorthar with the heart of the Cosmic Heart Titan.

Luke had only recently noticed the strange detail that his fusion form still possessed two individual hearts, which shouldn’t have made sense because Vorthar was supposedly a true fusion between two Titans, and logically, those hearts should have fused along with the rest of the body.
Unfortunately, the only beings capable of properly explaining that were the System and Myrkhal.
If Myrkhal had been awake, he would have said.
"Luke, you still don’t understand what a real fusion is."
Then, as usual, he would probably stop there and leave Luke to remain confused.
Since Myrkhal was still asleep, however, Luke had no answer for the strange structure of Vorthar’s body and simply took advantage of it.
The newly assimilated Cosmic Heart immediately began beating within his seventy-foot frame.
THUMP!
Cosmic Energy surged outward.
Luke raised one hand, and another Cosmic System manifested behind the existing twelve before its celestial bodies gradually moved into position with the others.
Thirteen Cosmic Systems now surrounded him.
Luke still didn’t activate Cosmic Lock.

Trying to use that technique while forcing thirteen entire Cosmic Systems into the same straight gravitational alignment would only cause their gravitational fields to clash with one another, and if that happened, every celestial body within the formation could collapse together before Luke ever managed to release the attack.
So Luke chose a different method.
It was something that even Caelith might have been stunned to see if she were currently awake.
Sevaroth, however, understood.
The Crypt Titan’s expression changed sharply as he stared at the growing formation.
"Luke, are you crazy?"
Luke didn’t answer him because almost all of his concentration was already divided between his main body and the twelve Cosmic Heart copies maintaining their respective systems.
Instead, a command passed silently through every body.
’Fix the sizes.’
The celestial bodies immediately began changing.
Asteroids, comets, moons, planets, and suns adjusted their manifested sizes until the formation gradually took on a completely different shape.
The celestial body at the front became the smallest, while those behind it increased progressively in size until the largest sun occupied the very end of the alignment.
Viewed from the side, the entire arrangement resembled a gigantic cosmic funnel.
"THIS!"
