’What is he trying to do?’
The Origin Titan observed the formation carefully.

He could clearly sense the energy stored inside those celestial bodies, yet even if Luke detonated everything simultaneously, the resulting destructive power still shouldn’t be enough to cleanly surpass Peak B-Rank.
More importantly, another problem immediately became obvious.
’Can his body even channel that much power?’
It was the same question almost everyone eventually asked whenever they saw Luke attempting to combine Caelith’s cosmic techniques with the body of the Atlas Titan.
This time, however, the Origin Titan’s concern wasn’t entirely wrong.
Even with Vorthar’s fused physique, Luke’s current D-Rank body couldn’t properly control the technique he was preparing.

At Vorthar’s true peak, the fusion body was supposed to possess the capability to carry the weight of the Endless Void itself, but Luke was nowhere near that level yet, and although his numerous stat multipliers had pushed his raw physical strength far beyond what an ordinary D-Rank should possess, there were still limits to how much force his current body could direct.
Vorthar could withstand the burden of the upcoming technique.
Controlling that burden was another matter.
Which was why Luke intended to borrow something else.
Using Myrkhal’s Form Assimilation, he replaced one of the two hearts within Vorthar with the heart of the Cosmic Heart Titan.

Luke had only recently noticed the strange detail that his fusion form still possessed two individual hearts, which shouldn’t have made sense because Vorthar was supposedly a true fusion between two Titans, and logically, those hearts should have fused along with the rest of the body.
Unfortunately, the only beings capable of properly explaining that were the System and Myrkhal.
If Myrkhal had been awake, he would have said.
"Luke, you still don’t understand what a real fusion is."
Then, as usual, he would probably stop there and leave Luke to remain confused.
Since Myrkhal was still asleep, however, Luke had no answer for the strange structure of Vorthar’s body and simply took advantage of it.
The newly assimilated Cosmic Heart immediately began beating within his seventy-foot frame.
THUMP!
Cosmic Energy surged outward.
Luke raised one hand, and another Cosmic System manifested behind the existing twelve before its celestial bodies gradually moved into position with the others.
Thirteen Cosmic Systems now surrounded him.
Luke still didn’t activate Cosmic Lock.

Trying to use that technique while forcing thirteen entire Cosmic Systems into the same straight gravitational alignment would only cause their gravitational fields to clash with one another, and if that happened, every celestial body within the formation could collapse together before Luke ever managed to release the attack.
So Luke chose a different method.
It was something that even Caelith might have been stunned to see if she were currently awake.
Sevaroth, however, understood.
The Crypt Titan’s expression changed sharply as he stared at the growing formation.
"Luke, are you crazy?"
Luke didn’t answer him because almost all of his concentration was already divided between his main body and the twelve Cosmic Heart copies maintaining their respective systems.
Instead, a command passed silently through every body.
’Fix the sizes.’
The celestial bodies immediately began changing.
Asteroids, comets, moons, planets, and suns adjusted their manifested sizes until the formation gradually took on a completely different shape.
The celestial body at the front became the smallest, while those behind it increased progressively in size until the largest sun occupied the very end of the alignment.
Viewed from the side, the entire arrangement resembled a gigantic cosmic funnel.
"THIS!"

chapters.title: Chapter 333: Luke Creates His Own Version of Azrion’s Unwritten Art!
paragraphs: Both Sevaroth and the Origin Titan reacted at almost the same time, their eyes widening as they finally understood what Luke was constructing.

The Origin Titan could now feel the difference clearly because the energy, gravity, and other forces generated by the celestial bodies were beginning to move through the funnel-like alignment instead of simply interfering with one another.
If Luke could withstand the burden created when all of that power reached a single point, then the combined force of those systems could actually be used instead of merely detonated.
Sevaroth understood even more.
Only two words escaped his mouth.
"Cosmic Eclipse."
That was exactly what Luke was preparing.

Cosmic Eclipse was a technique developed by Caelith herself, and she had personally demonstrated its principle to Luke during their training inside the Time Chamber, where he had witnessed just how absurd the technique became once enough celestial systems were involved.
Caelith’s Cosmic System had always possessed one fundamental limitation.

One Cosmic System contained a fixed collection of celestial bodies, including its planets, moons, stars, asteroids, and other objects, which meant that although she could combine the power of everything inside a single system, any additional Cosmic Systems she created still functioned as separate entities.
After years of refining her own fighting methods, Caelith created Cosmic Eclipse to overcome that restriction.

Instead of treating every Cosmic System separately, the technique arranged their celestial bodies into a formation capable of gathering and channeling their combined strength through one path, allowing multiple systems to contribute toward a single attack.
That was how Cosmic Punch could evolve into something far more destructive.
"Cosmic Eclipse Punch"
A normal Cosmic Punch drew upon one Cosmic System.
Cosmic Eclipse Punch could draw upon many.
At her peak, Caelith couldn’t destroy a galaxy with the power of a single Cosmic Punch, but once enough Cosmic Systems were combined through Cosmic Eclipse, that limitation disappeared.
Luke, however, still wasn’t finished.

He slowly drew in a deep breath while forcing his mind to remain steady, because the twelve copies behind him still required constant subconscious control to maintain their Cosmic Systems, and even a brief lapse in concentration could destabilize the entire formation.
That was also why Luke had chosen Elythos for this attempt.

The Armor of the Cosmic Heart helped him manage and manipulate cosmic power, reducing some of the burden involved in maintaining the celestial systems while his attention remained divided across thirteen bodies.
Even with Elythos helping, Luke could already feel the pressure building inside his mind.

Unfortunately, what he intended to do next would place even greater strain on him, and he knew there was a very real chance that the moment he activated the next part of his plan, his concentration would break for at least an instant.
’Come, Crown of Creation.’

Luke called upon the halo belonging to the Cosmic Heart Titan, and almost immediately, golden-white radiance gathered behind his head before forming into a luminous halo that slowly rotated while pulsing with dense Cosmic Energy.

He still didn’t understand why the Crown of Void hadn’t manifested automatically after he transformed into Vorthar, but he didn’t have the time to think about that now, because the moment the halo appeared, his control over the thirteen Cosmic Systems noticeably improved, while the twelve Cosmic Heart copies behind him continued supplying their own Cosmic Energy to stabilize the celestial formation.
The strain inside Luke’s mind finally eased enough for him to focus on the next step.
He drew in another deep breath while staring at the crimson-eyed Origin Titan standing at the center of the distant landscape.
’It’s do or die.’
Luke wanted to know where his current limit truly stood.

He wanted to see the peak of what he could produce as a D-Rank being, and more importantly, whether everything he possessed together could finally break through the Peak B-Rank barrier and perhaps even touch the threshold of Half-A-Rank.
"Absolute Strength!"

The moment Luke activated Azrion’s Ultimate Ability, the muscles beneath Elythos swelled violently as power flooded every part of Vorthar’s seventy-foot body, while his already terrifying physical output instantly multiplied threefold.
For the first time since Luke had begun preparing his attack, the Origin Titan’s expression changed completely.
"This..."
His crimson eyes narrowed as he stared at Luke, because what had just happened didn’t properly follow the normal rules governing physical strength in this universe.

Then again, Azrion had never been an existence particularly interested in following such rules, even during the age of the Titans, because his ultimate ambition had been insane enough that he had created an entire fighting method around one impossible goal.
To construct a body capable of carrying the universe itself.
Luke had inherited that madness.
And now he used it.
"AZRION’S UNWRITTEN ARTS"
The moment the Unwritten Arts awakened, the sky of the trial world began to darken.

The change wasn’t caused by clouds or the Cosmic Systems above, because behind Luke, an immense phantom slowly emerged from the gathering Force, taking the form of Azrion with a calm expression and an impossibly large body that stretched across the horizon.

Its head seemed to reach the very ceiling of this artificial world, although that clearly wasn’t Azrion’s true limit; the trial world itself simply wasn’t large enough to contain a manifestation any greater.
Luke raised his hand.
"First Move! Heaven’s Palm!"
The phantom of Azrion responded.
Its arm slowly lifted before descending toward the Origin Titan, as though the heavens themselves had decided to press down upon the thousand-foot crystalline figure.
At the same moment, Force gathered across the darkened sky and rapidly condensed into a spectral palm nearly three kilometers across.
The palm was made entirely from the unique Force wielded by the Atlas Titan, and even before it fully materialized, the pressure rolling from it caused the atmosphere below to distort.
Luke still didn’t stop.
He couldn’t afford to.
Absolute Strength would last only ten seconds, and once those ten seconds ended, the physical foundation supporting what he was about to attempt would disappear with it.
The thirteen Cosmic Systems immediately began moving.

Their carefully aligned celestial bodies shifted together until the entire funnel-like formation passed directly in front of the largest sun, and as planets, moons, comets, asteroids, and stars covered its radiance, darkness spread across the entire trial world like an eclipse had swallowed the sky.
Luke then moved Heaven’s Palm directly before the cosmic alignment.
The instant the three-kilometer spectral palm entered the path of the eclipse, black Void Energy ignited across its surface.
Nyx’s Authority of Severance had entered the attack.

Luke currently possessed only the aspects he had already awakened, so he poured both Physical Severance and Energy Severance into Heaven’s Palm, causing thin black lines to spread throughout the gigantic manifestation while its original Force remained underneath.

If Luke had already awakened deeper forms of Severance involving things such as distance, life, or other fundamental connections, the attack could have become far more terrifying, because at Nyx’s true peak, Severance possessed the potential to cut apart things on a scale that ordinary beings couldn’t even comprehend.
For now, however, physical matter and energy were enough.
The Heaven’s Palm, now carrying the Authority of Severance, floated directly before the thirteen aligned Cosmic Systems.

Luke finally raised his own giant hand and positioned it along the path of the eclipse, making sure his palm, Heaven’s Palm, and every celestial body behind it formed one continuous line toward the Origin Titan.
Then his hand slowly began descending.
"COSMIC SEVERINITY ECLIPSE PUNCH!!!"
The instant those words thundered across the trial world, Luke curled his fingers inward.
Sevaroth’s expression immediately froze.
"What the fuck?!"
The Crypt Titan stared at the three-kilometer Heaven’s Palm in disbelief because Luke had just attempted something that wasn’t part of Azrion’s First Art at all.
He was trying to turn Heaven’s Palm into a fist.

Azrion’s Unwritten Arts did contain methods involving larger portions of his manifested body, but Luke’s current physique wasn’t supposed to be capable of bearing the backlash required to transform and control that much externalized Force.
Yet Luke wasn’t relying only on Azrion.

He was using the gravitational flow of Cosmic Eclipse itself to help force the gigantic spectral fingers inward, making the thirteen Cosmic Systems act upon Heaven’s Palm while Vorthar carried the resulting burden.
Even then, what he was trying to do was absurd.
The three-kilometer palm began moving.

Its spectral fingers trembled under the combined gravitational pressure before slowly bending inward, one after another, while the surrounding air distorted under the Force required to control something of that scale.
Sevaroth’s eyes widened further.
’He’s actually doing it?!’
At the same time, the backlash reached Luke.
BOOOOM!

Invisible pressure crashed through Vorthar’s entire body, concentrating most heavily along his raised arm as the muscles beneath Elythos tightened under a weight that would have torn apart a weaker Titan instantly.
Luke gritted his teeth.
If he had attempted this with Azrion alone, he wasn’t even sure whether the Atlas Titan’s current D-Rank body could have completed the transformation of the palm.
Vorthar was different.
This fusion had been created from the Atlas Titan and the Void Titan, and at its true peak, its existence was meant to bear the weight of the Endless Void itself.

Luke was nowhere near that peak yet, but if his present Vorthar body couldn’t carry even the weight of his own attack for several seconds, then the fusion wasn’t worthy of that future in the first place.
"HAHHHHHH!"
Luke roared as his fingers continued closing.
"COME DOWN!!!"
He clenched his fist completely.
At the same instant, the enormous Heaven’s Palm responded.
BOOOOOOM!
All five spectral fingers finally folded inward, compressing the three-kilometer manifestation into the shape of a gigantic fist.
Sevaroth’s mouth twitched uncontrollably.
"He actually did it..."

chapters.title: Chapter 334: Luke Destroyed Adaptation Before It Could Adapt!
paragraphs: For a moment, he didn’t even know whether to be impressed or irritated, because Luke constantly called the ancient Titans maniacs for attempting impossible things, yet whenever he was given the slightest opportunity, he immediately tried something even more unreasonable himself.
At that even System screen appeared beside Sevaroth.
[Yeah. Luke is the biggest maniac among all of you. He keeps attempting impossible things and nearly getting himself killed.]
The System was obviously remembering the Essence Cloud Tribulation.
Luke completely ignored both of them.
His attention remained fixed on the Origin Titan.
However, something unexpected was happening inside the Fragment.
The crimson glow filling the Origin Titan’s eyes had begun fading slightly as he stared at Luke and the cosmic formation filling the sky.
"A being who accepts the impossible... and then makes it happen."
The words escaped his mouth almost absentmindedly.
His gaze remained fixed on Luke, but his thoughts had already drifted toward a distant past.
"Is that why your body can hold four Forbidden bloodlines?"
Memories that had remained buried beneath corruption began surfacing.

Once, the Origin Titan had possessed overwhelming power from the moment of his birth, and because victory had always come naturally to him, there had eventually been little reason to challenge himself beyond what he already believed possible.
He had been strong.
He had kept winning.
And somewhere along the way, he had stopped attempting things that seemed impossible.
Then those beings had come.
Everything he possessed had become useless before them, and only when defeat had already become unavoidable had he finally attempted something that should have been impossible.
’But I failed.’
Regret passed through the Origin Fragment’s fading crimson eyes.
That failure had eventually left him broken into fragments and imprisoned, forced to remain here while waiting for the mercy of beings he could no longer oppose.
Luke noticed none of it.
His entire concentration remained on the attack.
"HAH!"
He drove his fist forward.
The Cosmic Severinity Eclipse Punch moved with him.

The three-kilometer Force fist carrying Physical and Energy Severance surged through the celestial alignment, drawing upon the combined flow created by the thirteen Cosmic Systems before descending toward the Origin Titan’s thousand-foot body.
The air in front of it didn’t simply move aside, because the pressure behind the strike violently tore through it as the fist crossed the remaining distance.
Then it reached the outer Horizon Glass Body.
BOOOOOOM!
The pale glass prism shattered on contact.
SHATTER—!

Fragments burst outward across the sky as the outer body broke apart without slowing the fist enough to matter, while the Aspect of Distance hidden within it immediately tried to stretch the remaining path between the attack and the Crystal Body.
This time, however, the effect could no longer create an unreachable horizon.
The Origin Fragment was restricted by the rules of its own trial body.

Its current vessel remained at Peak D-Rank, and even after combining the powers of Adaptation and Distance, the effective strength it could produce had reached only around Peak B-Rank according to the human combat comparison Luke understood.
The Cosmic Severinity Eclipse Punch had already surpassed that limit.
It hadn’t reached Half-A-Rank.
Luke could feel that much.

Yet the sheer physical output carried by the fist was still far beyond an ordinary Peak B-Rank attack, reaching something comparable to the accumulated force of nearly a hundred Peak B-Rank punches, and that was before considering the Authority of Severance woven throughout it.
The stretched distance continued resisting.
The fist continued advancing.

Black Severance lines flickered across its surface as sections of the Distance Aspect’s influence broke apart along the path, while the overwhelming Force behind the attack simply kept consuming whatever separation remained.
Meter after meter disappeared.
Until finally—
The gigantic fist reached the Crystal Body.
For a fraction of a second, the entire world seemed to become still.
Then the fist struck.
KRAAAAAAAAAAASH!
The thousand-foot Crystal Body shattered instantly.

Crystalline fragments exploded in every direction as the Adaptation Fragment was broken apart before its body could complete any meaningful response to the attack, while streaks of white crystal scattered across the sky like broken stars.
The Cosmic Severinity Eclipse Punch continued forward.
Luke’s expression changed.
’Wait—’
The remaining force crossed the space where the Origin Titan had stood and crashed directly into the land beneath him.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!!!
The entire trial world shook.
The ground didn’t merely crater beneath the impact, because cracks immediately spread for kilometers in every direction before tearing deeper into the foundation of the artificial world itself.
Luke’s eyes widened.
’Damn it! I messed up!’
It was already too late.

The fractures raced outward like cracks spreading through glass, cutting through mountains, splitting coastlines, and tearing across the seas as entire sections of the artificial landscape began collapsing into one another.
The world itself was breaking.
Fortunately, this place was only the world created for the Origin Fragment’s trial, while the true prison surrounding it was still the Heaven’s Crucible outside.

If Luke had released the same attack directly against the real Heaven’s Crucible, destroying it wouldn’t have been anywhere near this simple, and without accessing the genuine depth of his Forbidden powers, he doubted he could have broken that place at all.
CRAAAAACK—!
Another fracture spread across the sky.

The mountains in the distance began collapsing as the seas rose violently around broken landmasses, while pieces of the sky itself separated like shattered glass and revealed darkness beyond the artificial world.
Luke immediately tried to stabilize himself, but the destruction was already spreading toward his position.

Before the collapsing world could reach him, the twelve Cosmic Heart copies disappeared together with their Cosmic Systems, while the Crown of Creation faded behind Luke’s head and Vorthar rapidly reverted to his normal human body.
Elythos vanished immediately afterward.
Luke barely had enough time to realize what was happening before two gigantic blue hands suddenly manifested within the collapsing world.

One swept toward Luke and enclosed his body before the advancing destruction could touch him, while the other reached through the storm of shattered crystal and gathered the two Origin Fragments left behind after the destruction of the Origin Titan’s body.
Then, before the trial world completely collapsed, both blue hands pulled Luke and the fragments away from the destruction and disappered.

’Damn it!
I messed up!’
It was already too late.

The fractures raced outward like cracks spreading through glass, cutting through mountains, splitting coastlines, and tearing across the seas as entire sections of the artificial landscape began collapsing into one another.
The world itself was breaking.
Fortunately, this place was only the world created for the Origin Fragment’s trial, while the true prison surrounding it was still the Heaven’s Crucible outside.

If Luke had released the same attack directly against the real Heaven’s Crucible, destroying it wouldn’t have been anywhere near this simple, and without accessing the genuine depth of his Forbidden powers, he doubted he could have broken that place at all.
CRAAAAACK—!
Another fracture spread across the sky.

The mountains in the distance began collapsing as the seas rose violently around broken landmasses, while pieces of the sky itself separated like shattered glass and revealed darkness beyond the artificial world.
Luke immediately tried to stabilize himself, but the destruction was already spreading toward his position.

Before the collapsing world could reach him, the twelve Cosmic Heart copies disappeared together with their Cosmic Systems, while the Crown of Creation faded behind Luke’s head and Vorthar rapidly reverted to his normal human body.
Elythos vanished immediately afterward.
Luke barely had enough time to realize what was happening before two gigantic blue hands suddenly manifested within the collapsing world.

One swept toward Luke and enclosed his body before the advancing destruction could touch him, while the other reached through the storm of shattered crystal and gathered the two Origin Fragments left behind after the destruction of the Origin Titan’s body.
Then, before the trial world completely collapsed, both blue hands pulled Luke and the fragments away from the destruction and disappered.

chapters.title: Chapter 335: Seventy-Five B-Rank Warriors Never Came Back!
paragraphs: Outside the Twilight Ruins, within one of the hidden chambers beneath the royal palace, Roderan and Drevian stood before the circular spatial formation that had remained inactive since the expedition entered the Twilight Ruins, while pale runes across the floor began glowing and the air above them slowly twisted inward.
A portal formed, and some of the tension immediately left Roderan’s shoulders as he released a long breath and said, "They’re coming out. It seems the expedition is finally over."
Drevian gave a small nod while keeping his attention on the unstable surface, which suddenly rippled before several beams of pale blue light shot toward different empty sections of the chamber.
WHOOSH! WHOOSH! WHOOSH! WHOOSH!

Zeyr materialized first, planting both feet firmly on the floor while his dark brown hair fell around his shoulders, and although his posture remained composed, the breath he released showed his relief. Karon appeared several meters away, her long black hair settling behind her as she looked around and said, "We’re finally back."

Another beam brought Marius Duskraven, while Fael and Joria appeared shortly afterward, both Marinthians visibly exhausted despite their usual calm. Kira materialized next, followed by Nolan, who steadied himself and said with a tired laugh, "After this, I think I’ll avoid ancient ruins for a while."
Kira replied, "Give yourself a few months and you’ll forget you ever said that."
More light swept across the chamber as Arwen and Lirael appeared together, both quickly recovering their proud composure, while Alia materialized nearby."
Isaria appeared next, followed closely by Estelle, and the princess visibly relaxed after recognizing the royal palace chamber around them.
"We made it back safely," Estelle said.
"Some of us did," Isaria replied softly, and the meaning behind those words briefly darkened Estelle’s expression.

Another beam brought Selene near the center of the chamber, yet unlike the others, she did not relax, because the instant she materialized, her crimson gaze moved across Zeyr, Karon, Marius, Fael, Joria, Kira, Nolan, Arwen, Lirael, Alia, Isaria, and Estelle, confirming that Luke wasn’t there.

More beams continued emerging as the surviving Sunborn warriors and mages returned, but when the final cluster materialized, barely twenty-five remained, with only a few mages among them and their damaged armor, torn robes, and exhausted faces making the losses obvious.
Roderan counted them twice before the relief disappeared from his face, then asked, "Where are the rest of the Sunborn warriors, and where are Ivar and Luke?"
The chamber became quiet as Drevian also realized that around one hundred B-Rank Sunborn members had entered the ruins and only a fraction had returned.
Zeyr answered first. "Ivar never reached Heaven’s Crucible with us. The Infernal Choir was involved before everyone gathered there, so most of us assumed something happened to him."
That answer only worsened the situation, because Ivar was a prince of the Owl Kingdom, and his death inside Eldric Sunborn territory could create a political crisis.
Drevian looked toward the still-active portal and asked, "Then where is the Hero of Light? Luke should have returned with the rest of you."

No one answered immediately, because all of them found the same strange gap in their memories; they remembered the battles inside Heaven’s Crucible and the first fracture across the arena, but nothing involving Lilith, Iveron, or what happened to Luke afterward.
Karon pressed two fingers against her temple and said, "Luke was definitely with us before the fracture, but I can’t remember what happened after that."
Zeyr shook his head. "Neither can I, which means something happened to all of our memories."
Nolan looked between them in confusion. "How could every one of us lose the same part?"
Fael and Joria exchanged uneasy looks, while Arwen and Lirael said nothing.
Estelle stepped closer to the portal and said, "Luke should have been transported out with everyone else."
"Exactly, so there was no reason for him to remain behind," Isaria replied, although uneasiness had already entered her voice.
Alia stopped beside them and stared into the rippling blue surface. "Then why hasn’t he come out?"
Selene’s breathing became unsteady as fear replaced her confusion, and she approached the portal before calling, "Luke, if you’re still inside, stop messing around and come out right now."
Nothing happened, while the portal continued rippling without sending another beam.
Selene clenched her hands and called again, louder this time, "Luke, answer me. I’m serious."
Roderan approached carefully and said, "Princess Selene, the portal is still active, so there may simply be a delay in the final transfer.
"Then why has everyone else returned while he hasn’t?" Selene demanded, her face already pale.

Before Roderan could answer, golden light appeared over Selene’s chest, and a thin golden chain emerged from near her heart before stretching toward the portal and disappearing into the distorted space.
She immediately grabbed it and whispered, "Luke is still alive, and this connection says he is still inside."
Estelle went pale, while Isaria moved closer and Alia became completely still.

Roderan and Drevian exchanged a grave look, because losing Ivar could provoke the Owl Kingdom, while losing the Hero of Light could bring the Holy Light Church and even the Goddess of Light herself against them.
Roderan looked at Selene and said, "As long as the passage remains open, we can still reach him, so stay back and let us handle this."
The portal suddenly flickered, and before anyone could react, its blue surface contracted violently until the entire passage collapsed into a point of light and vanished.
"No! Luke is still inside!" Selene shouted as she rushed toward the empty space.
Estelle, Isaria, and Alia all went pale, while Zeyr and the others stared at the place where the portal had disappeared.
Drevian immediately told Roderan, "Open the passage again. Reaching the original entrance should be enough."
Roderan was already moving, raising both hands as his power flooded the chamber and lit the surrounding runes.
KRRRRRNNNN—
Space warped between his hands as he pulled outward, forcing a narrow tear to appear, yet despite the strength pouring from his body, the opening barely widened.
"Damn it, the connection isn’t responding," Roderan said before releasing even more power.
BOOOOOOM!
A violent shockwave blasted across the chamber and hurled almost everyone into the reinforced walls, while Drevian alone remained beside Roderan and immediately added his own strength.
"Pull with me, and don’t let the tear close," Drevian said.
Both men seized the unstable edges of space with their power and forced them apart.
KRRRRRRRNNNN!
The tear widened by only a few inches before stopping again, refusing to open despite their combined strength.
"It still isn’t connecting to the ruins," Drevian said.
"I know, but keep pulling until we have no strength left," Roderan replied as another wave of pressure rolled across the chamber.
Behind them, Selene stared at the golden chain stretching from her heart toward the sealed space and shouted, "Luke is still there, so do not stop until you open it."
Estelle clasped her hands tightly, Isaria remained silent beside her, and Alia pressed her nails into her palms without looking away.

Farther back, Marius watched the failed passage with a faint smile that he quickly concealed, while Arwen and Lirael exchanged a brief glance that carried none of the fear shown by the others, because if Luke remained trapped inside the Twilight Ruins forever, neither of them would consider it a loss.
Then space suddenly ripped open by itself.
RRRIP!
Roderan and Drevian both stepped back as blue light burst from the opening, and a human figure materialized directly in the center of the chamber.
Luke looked around at the glowing runes and the dozens of people staring at him before asking, "Why does everyone look like something terrible just happened?"
"Luke, you’re finally back!" Selene shouted as she reached him first and wrapped both arms around him so tightly that he staggered half a step backward.
"Selene, I’m fine, so you don’t have to crush me," Luke said, surprised by how hard she was holding him.
"You idiot, the portal closed while you were still inside, and you expect me to be calm after that?" Selene replied without loosening her grip.

Before Luke could answer, Estelle, Isaria, and Alia rushed forward as well, with Estelle hugging him from one side, Isaria from the other, and Alia pressing in from behind until Luke found himself surrounded by four women.
The chamber became strangely quiet, while Nolan stared at the scene before muttering, "He disappears for a few minutes and somehow comes back to this. That hardly seems fair."
Fael covered a smile, Joria shook her head, Marius’s face darkened, and Arwen looked away with visible irritation.
Luke raised his hands as much as the four women allowed and said, "Everyone, I really am fine, so can you give me a little room to breathe?"
That finally made Selene notice who else was clinging to him, and after looking at Estelle, Isaria, and Alia, she said in disbelief, "Why are all three of you hugging my husband?"
Estelle immediately stepped back and replied, "I thought something had happened to him, so I reacted without thinking."
Isaria quickly released Luke as well. "The portal collapsed while he was still inside, so of course we were worried."
Alia remained in place for another second before saying, "I was worried too, and I only hugged him because he came back safely."
"So was I, but he is still my husband, so all three of you can worry without clinging to him," Selene replied as she pulled Luke closer and pushed Alia away with her free hand.
Alia finally released him, although her displeased expression made it clear she had only done so reluctantly.

Roderan and Drevian watched with tired amusement before Roderan said, "Since everyone who can return has finally returned, we should report to His Majesty before another section of the palace gets damaged."
Drevian nodded and added, "The king has been waiting for the expedition report, and after these losses, we should not keep him waiting any longer."

That reminder suppressed the lighter mood, because Ivar was still missing and most of the Sunborn force had not returned, even though both Roderan and Drevian found that half of the sunborn warriors were traitor.
Still, Roderan and Drevian then led the survivors through the guarded corridors toward the main hall, where King Demerak and Crown Prince Lucan were already waiting.

Demerak stood before the throne, his golden hair framing a middle-aged face while his broad, muscular build remained obvious beneath his royal clothing, and his black gaze settled on the depleted Sunborn forces.
Beside him stood Lucan, a man in his early thirties with the same golden hair and black eyes, whose composed expression disappeared when he saw Estelle.
"Estelle, come here and tell me whether you’re injured anywhere," Lucan said as he stepped down and checked his sister from head to toe.
"I’m fine, Brother, although I would prefer if you stopped examining me in front of everyone," Estelle replied with tired embarrassment.
Lucan finally relaxed after confirming that she was unharmed, while Demerak continued studying the small number of Sunborn warriors and mages behind them.
He turned toward Roderan and asked, "You took one hundred B-Rank members of my kingdom into those ruins, so tell me what happened to the rest of them."
The atmosphere inside the hall immediately became heavy.

Roderan stepped forward and answered, "Your Majesty, the expedition changed far beyond what any of us expected, because the Infernal Choir had already infiltrated the group before we entered the deepest part of the Twilight Ruins."
The remaining relief disappeared from Demerak’s face as everyone in the hall fell silent.

chapters.title: Chapter 336: The King Wants Luke as His Son-in-Law!
paragraphs: Even Lucan’s expression changed after hearing Roderan’s report, because the implications were far more concerning than simply losing several B-Rank warriors inside the ruins. If the Infernal Choir had managed to infiltrate a group of specially selected B-Rank members trusted enough to participate in a secret royal expedition, then there was no telling how deeply their influence had already spread throughout the Sunborn Kingdom.
"Your Majesty, we cannot ignore this," Lucan said as he looked toward Demerak.

Demerak gave a slow nod, because he had already reached the same conclusion, then leaned back against his throne and rested his chin against one hand while considering how many problems this revelation could create.
’We’re already going through a difficult period, and now this happens as well.’

A tired sigh escaped him after several moments, because one of the reasons he had approved such a dangerous expedition was the possibility that the academy representatives might recover an ancient relic capable of helping the kingdom through its current problems. Unfortunately, after listening to the survivors, he learned that the deeper section of the Twilight Ruins had turned out to be an ancient arena, where the victorious side would normally receive rewards, yet this time everyone had returned empty-handed.

What Demerak didn’t know was that the interference of gods had disrupted the normal conclusion of Heaven’s Crucible, which was why Peiro hadn’t distributed any artifacts or rewards to the surviving participants.

While considering the losses, Demerak’s attention eventually shifted toward Luke, who was standing among the others while Selene remained pressed closely against his side, clearly unwilling to let him disappear from her sight again after what had happened earlier.
’Hmm... perhaps there is still something useful I can gain from this situation.’
His thoughts moved quickly before his attention shifted toward Estelle, who was occasionally glancing at Luke from the side whenever she thought no one was paying attention.
’Perfect. It seems she already has some feelings for him.’
That realization immediately improved Demerak’s mood, and after considering the matter for a few more moments, he raised one hand and addressed everyone gathered inside the hall.
"You have all experienced enough for one day, so go and rest for now, and please make sure to attend the royal dinner later this evening."
No one objected, and Demerak didn’t bother mentioning the treasures from the ruins, because if no one had obtained anything, then there was nothing that needed to be divided or discussed.
The representatives gradually began leaving the hall, yet before Luke could follow Selene toward the exit, Demerak called after him.
"Sir Hero, would you remain for a moment? There is something I would like to discuss with you privately."

Luke stopped and looked back, while several of the nearby representatives became curious about what the king wanted from him. However, once it became obvious that Demerak intended to speak with Luke separately, everyone continued toward the exit, including Selene, although she was clearly reluctant to leave him alone after what had just happened.
"I’ll be waiting in the room, so don’t take too long," Selene told him before finally following the others.
Luke gave her a small nod, then turned back toward Demerak.
Lucan remained beside the king, while Estelle had also stayed behind, and both of them were curious about why Demerak had specifically asked the Hero of Light to remain.

Demerak stepped forward and formally introduced himself. "Although we have already met indirectly through everything that happened today, allow me to properly introduce myself. I am Demerak Sunborn, current king of the Eldric Sunborn Kingdom."
Luke responded calmly, "Luke Voidheart, Hero of Light and Baron of the Blackstone Highlands."

He didn’t bow when introducing himself, something Demerak immediately noticed, but the king showed no offense because Luke’s status as a recognized Hero placed him on a level comparable to emperors in the eyes of many powers, while Demerak himself ruled only a kingdom.

"Sir Luke, there is something rather important I would like to discuss with you, although this hall isn’t the best place for such a conversation," Demerak said with a polite smile before gesturing toward one of the adjoining corridors. "Please come with me."
Lucan and Estelle’s curiosity only increased, and both followed as Demerak led Luke toward a private reception room reserved for distinguished guests.

The room was lavishly furnished without being excessively large, with comfortable seats arranged around a low table and several royal decorations placed along the walls. Demerak took a seat on one side while Luke sat opposite him, after which Lucan and Estelle settled into the remaining seats.
Demerak remained silent for a few seconds before deciding there was no reason to drag the conversation out.
"Sir Luke, I don’t particularly enjoy beating around the bush, so I will simply ask you directly. Would you be willing to marry my daughter, Estelle?"
For several seconds, neither Luke, Lucan, nor Estelle responded.
Then a System screen appeared in front of Luke.
[YES! LUKE, SAY YES! EVEN IF ESTELLE ISN’T A QUEEN, A PRINCESS IS MORE THAN GOOD ENOUGH!!!]
Luke’s mouth twitched.
’Do you seriously like collecting princesses this much?’

The System offered no shame whatsoever, while Sevaroth remained silent because he was still sleeping inside Luke, having explained earlier that his spirit required time to properly adjust to Valtharion.
Estelle, meanwhile, had frozen after hearing her father’s question, and a faint redness quickly spread across her face as she lowered her head.
’What is Father thinking? How can he suddenly ask Luke to marry me like this?’

She wasn’t opposed to marrying Luke, especially after everything that had happened between them, and she had already considered the possibility herself, yet she had expected to spend more time together and gradually make Luke develop feelings for her instead of having her father suddenly throw a marriage proposal directly at him.
Lucan was equally stunned, although his attention quickly shifted toward his sister when he noticed her reaction.
’She’s actually interested in the Hero of Light?’

Concern appeared across his face because he had spent years protecting Estelle from political marriages, and although Luke possessed an extraordinary status, Lucan also knew that the Hero of Light already had several women around him, including princesses from different races.
’Heroes rarely live ordinary lives, and someone surrounded by that many women may never be able to give one person his complete attention.’

Lucan wasn’t going to interfere immediately, especially after seeing that Estelle herself seemed interested, but the protective older brother within him couldn’t help worrying about what might happen if she became deeply attached to Luke and later ended up hurt.
’I just hope she hasn’t already fallen too deeply for him.’
While Lucan remained silent, Luke finally answered.
"King Demerak, I appreciate the offer, but I’m not planning to marry anyone right now."
He deliberately added the final two words so the refusal wouldn’t sound unnecessarily absolute or disrespectful.

Estelle’s earlier embarrassment immediately faded as she raised her head and looked toward Luke, disappointment clearly appearing across her face as though silently asking why he had rejected the proposal.
Luke noticed her reaction but didn’t address it directly, because he already understood why Demerak had suddenly proposed the marriage.

That realization immediately improved Demerak’s mood, and after considering the matter for a few more moments, he raised one hand and addressed everyone gathered inside the hall.
"You have all experienced enough for one day, so go and rest for now, and please make sure to attend the royal dinner later this evening."
No one objected, and Demerak didn’t bother mentioning the treasures from the ruins, because if no one had obtained anything, then there was nothing that needed to be divided or discussed.
The representatives gradually began leaving the hall, yet before Luke could follow Selene toward the exit, Demerak called after him.
"Sir Hero, would you remain for a moment?
There is something I would like to discuss with you privately."
Luke stopped and looked back, while several of the nearby representatives became curious about what the king wanted from him.

However, once it became obvious that Demerak intended to speak with Luke separately, everyone continued toward the exit, including Selene, although she was clearly reluctant to leave him alone after what had just happened.
"I’ll be waiting in the room, so don’t take too long," Selene told him before finally following the others.
Luke gave her a small nod, then turned back toward Demerak.
Lucan remained beside the king, while Estelle had also stayed behind, and both of them were curious about why Demerak had specifically asked the Hero of Light to remain.
Demerak stepped forward and formally introduced himself.
"Although we have already met indirectly through everything that happened today, allow me to properly introduce myself.
I am Demerak Sunborn, current king of the Eldric Sunborn Kingdom."
Luke responded calmly, "Luke Voidheart, Hero of Light and Baron of the Blackstone Highlands."

He didn’t bow when introducing himself, something Demerak immediately noticed, but the king showed no offense because Luke’s status as a recognized Hero placed him on a level comparable to emperors in the eyes of many powers, while Demerak himself ruled only a kingdom.

"Sir Luke, there is something rather important I would like to discuss with you, although this hall isn’t the best place for such a conversation," Demerak said with a polite smile before gesturing toward one of the adjoining corridors.
"Please come with me."
Lucan and Estelle’s curiosity only increased, and both followed as Demerak led Luke toward a private reception room reserved for distinguished guests.
The room was lavishly furnished without being excessively large, with comfortable seats arranged around a low table and several royal decorations placed along the walls.
Demerak took a seat on one side while Luke sat opposite him, after which Lucan and Estelle settled into the remaining seats.
Demerak remained silent for a few seconds before deciding there was no reason to drag the conversation out.
"Sir Luke, I don’t particularly enjoy beating around the bush, so I will simply ask you directly.
Would you be willing to marry my daughter, Estelle?"
For several seconds, neither Luke, Lucan, nor Estelle responded.
Then a System screen appeared in front of Luke.
[YES!
LUKE, SAY YES!
EVEN IF ESTELLE ISN’T A QUEEN, A PRINCESS IS MORE THAN GOOD ENOUGH!!!]
Luke’s mouth twitched.
’Do you seriously like collecting princesses this much?’

The System offered no shame whatsoever, while Sevaroth remained silent because he was still sleeping inside Luke, having explained earlier that his spirit required time to properly adjust to Valtharion.
Estelle, meanwhile, had frozen after hearing her father’s question, and a faint redness quickly spread across her face as she lowered her head.
’What is Father thinking?
How can he suddenly ask Luke to marry me like this?’

She wasn’t opposed to marrying Luke, especially after everything that had happened between them, and she had already considered the possibility herself, yet she had expected to spend more time together and gradually make Luke develop feelings for her instead of having her father suddenly throw a marriage proposal directly at him.
Lucan was equally stunned, although his attention quickly shifted toward his sister when he noticed her reaction.
’She’s actually interested in the Hero of Light?’

Concern appeared across his face because he had spent years protecting Estelle from political marriages, and although Luke possessed an extraordinary status, Lucan also knew that the Hero of Light already had several women around him, including princesses from different races.
’Heroes rarely live ordinary lives, and someone surrounded by that many women may never be able to give one person his complete attention.’

Lucan wasn’t going to interfere immediately, especially after seeing that Estelle herself seemed interested, but the protective older brother within him couldn’t help worrying about what might happen if she became deeply attached to Luke and later ended up hurt.
’I just hope she hasn’t already fallen too deeply for him.’
While Lucan remained silent, Luke finally answered.
"King Demerak, I appreciate the offer, but I’m not planning to marry anyone right now."
He deliberately added the final two words so the refusal wouldn’t sound unnecessarily absolute or disrespectful.

Estelle’s earlier embarrassment immediately faded as she raised her head and looked toward Luke, disappointment clearly appearing across her face as though silently asking why he had rejected the proposal.
Luke noticed her reaction but didn’t address it directly, because he already understood why Demerak had suddenly proposed the marriage.

chapters.title: Chapter 337: Luke’s Origin Skill Finally Reaches SSR+ Rank!
paragraphs: During his earlier travels, Luke had heard enough about the difficulties currently facing the Sunborn Kingdom, while the decision to send one hundred B-Rank warriors into such a dangerous ruin already showed how desperate they were to obtain something useful. B-Rank combatants weren’t people a kingdom could casually replace, especially after suffering losses like the ones they had just experienced.
Demerak studied Luke for another moment before simply nodding.
"Very well. I understand."

He didn’t repeat the proposal or attempt to pressure Luke, because regardless of how useful such a marriage could be, he was still a king and had no intention of lowering himself by begging someone to marry his daughter.
Lucan quietly released some of the tension he had been holding, believing the matter had ended before Estelle could become more involved, but Luke spoke again before anyone could move on.

"However, Estelle is already my friend, so she is welcome to visit Blackstone whenever she wishes, and I would also be interested in expanding cooperation between Blackstone and the Sunborn Kingdom, especially through trade."

That suggestion would have sounded absurd if it came from an ordinary baron, because Blackstone was merely a barony while Demerak controlled an entire kingdom, yet the king didn’t dismiss Luke’s words.
Roderan had already informed him of something far more important than Luke’s noble title.
According to the warriors who had witnessed the battles within Heaven’s Crucible, Luke was already capable of producing attacks that reached the level of Peak B-Rank.

Even if some of those reports had been exaggerated, Luke’s status as the Hero of Light, his connections with several powerful races, and the strength he had displayed were already enough to make cooperation worthwhile. If outside forces believed Luke and the Sunborn Kingdom had formed a meaningful alliance, his name alone could discourage some of those currently considering taking advantage of their weakened state.
Demerak smiled. "The Sunborn Kingdom would gladly welcome greater cooperation with Blackstone, Sir Luke, and I believe there are several areas where both territories could benefit from one another."

Lucan remained somewhat confused by how naturally his father was treating a baron as an equal negotiating partner, but he kept that confusion to himself, understanding that Demerak clearly knew something about Luke that he hadn’t yet been told.
Estelle, on the other hand, immediately brightened after hearing Luke’s words.
’If I can visit Blackstone whenever I want, then this isn’t over yet.’
The rejected proposal no longer seemed nearly as devastating, because she still had plenty of time to make Luke fall in love with her naturally.
Luke happened to look toward her at that moment and gave her a small smile, which only strengthened that thought.
"Then I’ll leave the details for another time, King Demerak. I should go and rest as well."
"Of course, Sir Luke. We can discuss trade during the royal dinner or sometime afterward."

Luke stood and left the reception room while Demerak, Lucan, and Estelle watched him disappear through the doorway, and the moment the door closed behind him, the silence inside the room ended as the three members of the Sunborn royal family began discussing everything that had just happened.
"Finally, some free time."
Luke muttered with satisfaction as he walked through the palace corridors toward Selene’s room, while servants and royal guards occasionally passed him along the polished stone hallway.
After everything that had happened since entering the Twilight Ruins, he finally had enough time to properly process the events of the last few hours.
His thoughts naturally returned to what had happened immediately after he destroyed the small artificial world.
BOOOOOOOOM!

The small world continued collapsing around him as mountains shattered, seas surged violently, and fractured pieces of the artificial sky disappeared into spreading cracks, yet before any of that destruction could reach Luke, an overwhelming spatial force pulled him away.
By the time his surroundings became clear again, he had already returned to Heaven’s Crucible.
"Peiro?
Luke looked around in confusion before realizing who had brought him back.
Peiro stood nearby while the ancient arena around them had already begun showing signs of collapse, yet instead of appearing worried, the blue spirit wore a relieved smile.
"Thank you, young Titan. Because of what you accomplished inside that trial, I am finally free."
Luke looked toward the damaged Heaven’s Crucible before understanding what Peiro meant.

The ancient arena had also functioned as a prison, while Peiro had remained here as its guardian, waiting for challengers and ensuring that the existence imprisoned within could not freely escape. Now that the Origin Titan’s remaining Fragments had been removed from the trial world, there was no longer anything left for the prison to contain.
Peiro raised one hand and revealed two shining crystals resting above his palm.
"These belong to you."

The first was the Adaptation Origin Fragment, whose primary emerald color continuously shifted through cyan, turquoise, violet, and faint traces of gold whenever Luke viewed it from a different angle, causing the crystal to appear as though it were constantly changing even while remaining perfectly still.

Beside it floated the Distance Origin Fragment, an almost transparent crystal with a pale blue center and silver-white edges, while the deeper Luke looked into it, the farther away its center seemed to become, creating the strange impression that an impossible distance existed inside something small enough to fit within his hand.
Luke accepted both fragments.
"Thanks, Peiro, and not just for these. You saved me back there."
Only after saying those words did Luke notice something strange.
The backlash from Cosmic Severinity Eclipse Punch was gone.
His body no longer carried the pain that should have followed such an insane combination of abilities, while the exhaustion caused by draining so much strength and energy had also disappeared.
Luke looked toward Peiro.
The ancient spirit merely smiled, making it obvious that restoring him had been Peiro’s own way of thanking him.
Luke returned the gesture with a small nod before looking down at the two Origin Fragments.
Then both crystals vanished from his hands.
Peiro assumed Luke had absorbed them directly into his body, but the truth was different.
[Second Origin Fragment detected: Adaptation.]
[Third Origin Fragment detected: Distance.]
[SSS+ Rank Origin Skill evolution initiated.]
[Estimated completion time: 1 hour.]
Luke smiled after reading the notifications.

Peiro watched him for a moment before saying, "If fate allows it, perhaps we will meet again someday, young Titan. For now, you should return to your companions before this place completely collapses.
Luke nodded, and soon afterward Peiro sent him out of Heaven’s Crucible.
Once Luke disappeared, Peiro remained alone within the weakening arena and released a long sigh as he examined his own condition.
His freedom had returned, yet his current strength remained only around the Demigod level, far below what he had possessed at his peak.
"It seems recovering my strength will take some time."
With those words, Peiro disappeared from Heaven’s Crucible.

The ancient arena immediately began compressing inward once its final guardian had left, with its vast internal space folding upon itself until a small black hole appeared where the structure had existed.

The black hole consumed the remaining traces of Heaven’s Crucible, erasing the presence of the Eternal-Rank artifact so thoroughly that anyone arriving later would find no evidence that something of such value had ever existed there.
Then the black hole disappeared as well.
Far away, Peiro stopped.
He slowly turned his attention toward the distant dimension where Heaven’s Crucible had just vanished, because the way the black hole had erased everything wasn’t natural.
A trace of seriousness appeared on his face.
"Their power has already reached this place."
Peiro remained there for only another moment before disappearing completely from that dimension.
Current time...
Luke continued walking through the palace hallway when a familiar notification suddenly appeared before him.
[Evolution complete.]
[Congratulations, Luke.]
[Your SSS+ Rank Origin Skill has evolved into an SSR+ Rank Origin Skill.]
[Two new Titan Legacies have been acquired.]
Luke immediately came out of his thoughts, and after reading the notification once more to make sure he hadn’t misunderstood anything, excitement spread across his face.
"Finally."
He kept his voice low because several maids and palace guards were passing through the corridor, and he had no desire to make them wonder why the Hero of Light was suddenly celebrating by himself.
His attention immediately returned to the System screen as he prepared to inspect the two new Titan Legacies.

Nexus Titan had already been absurdly powerful despite being only SSS+, especially after Titan Harmony allowed his different Titan abilities and Armaments to function as one unified system, so Luke was naturally curious about what kind of abilities an SSR and SSR+ evolution could possibly give him.
’If Nexus Titan was already that broken, then these two should be even more ridiculous.’
With that thought, Luke eagerly opened the first Titan Legacy.

chapters.title: Chapter 338: The Titans Who Could Forge Anything!
paragraphs: [ANVIL TITAN]
Rank: SSR
Type: Origin Skill
Classification: Origin Authority
Status: Awakened
Previous Evolution:
"NEXUS TITAN — SSS+"
[DESCRIPTION]
"The Origin Skill born from the Titans who forged impossibility itself."
Beyond the realities known to Valtharion once existed an ancient universe inhabited by a Titan civilization that did not depend upon gods, predetermined paths, or any single natural law.
They were known as—
"THE ANVIL TITANS"

Unlike ordinary Titans who specialized in particular elements, bodies, Authorities, or laws, the Anvil Titans devoted themselves entirely to Forging, and to them, ordinary metal was merely the simplest material that could enter a forge.

Fire, gravity, bloodlines, abilities, souls, curses, techniques, divine power, celestial bodies, Authorities, natural phenomena, and even forces that should normally be incompatible could all be treated as forging materials.
Through this path, they eventually created an Origin Method that surpassed every conventional form of fusion.
[ORIGIN AUTHORITY]
■ "HEAVEN FORGE"
"The forge does not care what something once was; it only cares what it can become."

Heaven Forge allows the wielder to treat powers, abilities, techniques, energies, substances, phenomena, and other valid existences as forging materials, then merge and reforge them into a completely new result.

The process does not simply activate several abilities at the same time, because once the forging is completed, the original materials are combined into a single unified phenomenon that carries properties from everything used to create it.
[ANVIL TITAN LORE...]
"Okay, this is even more broken than the previous one."

Luke muttered in genuine surprise as he continued reading the new Authority, because what Heaven Forge allowed him to accomplish reminded him of the attack he had created inside the artificial world, yet the principle behind the two was completely different.

Back then, Luke had forced several techniques and abilities to work together at the same time, using Cosmic Eclipse, Heaven’s Palm, Severance, Absolute Strength, and the support of multiple Cosmic Systems to create the Cosmic Severinity Eclipse Punch. The result had been absurdly powerful, but achieving it had required several different conditions to align, along with enough control to keep all those powers functioning together without collapsing.

More importantly, Luke had only been able to attempt something on that scale because he was using an Atlas-based physique, and even then, Vorthar had been the better choice because its body could endure far greater backlash than his other Titan forms.

If Luke had attempted the same combination through one of his weaker Titan bodies, the strain alone would likely have overwhelmed the transformation and forced him back into his human form long before the attack was completed.
Heaven Forge completely changed that problem.

Instead of forcing several independent powers to cooperate temporarily, the Anvil Titan’s method could take those abilities, techniques, energies, or other materials and genuinely forge them into a single unified result, meaning the finished technique would no longer behave like several different powers being maintained at once.

Even better, because Heaven Forge had become part of his Origin Skill, Luke could access it through any of his Harmonized Titans rather than being restricted to Atlas Titan or Vorthar whenever he wanted to create a complicated combination.
’System, thanks for finding me such an amazing Titan.’
Luke praised the System sincerely while continuing through the palace corridor.
[It’s fine.]

[You should also read their lore. Understanding where these Titans came from and how they used their abilities may help you grasp their methods faster, and you might even learn something that isn’t immediately obvious from the Authority description.]
Luke paused for half a step before continuing forward as though nothing had happened, while several servants passed through the corridor without paying him much attention.

Recently, he had noticed that the System had begun providing far more detailed lore concerning the Titans connected to him, just as it had done after Sevaroth awakened, and although Luke had originally treated those histories as additional information, he had gradually realized how useful they actually were.

Knowing how a Titan civilization had developed its methods, what problems those methods were created to solve, and how their strongest members had used them gave Luke far more insight than simply reading an ability description.
"Alright, show me."
The System responded immediately, and the previous screen disappeared before another page unfolded in front of Luke.
[ANVIL TITAN — LORE]

Long before the rise of many known civilizations, somewhere beyond the realities connected to Valtharion existed a universe called *Vorgael*, a realm where an ancient Titan race developed along a path completely different from ordinary elemental, physical, or Authority-based Titans. These beings eventually became known as the *Anvil Titans*, although the name had little to do with ordinary blacksmithing, because by the height of their civilization, metal was considered one of the simplest materials their forges could handle.

The foundation of their civilization was an ancient Origin Method known as *Heaven Forge*, a technique born from a simple belief that defined their entire species: if something existed, then under the correct conditions, it could become material for something new.

Anvil Titans could certainly forge weapons, armor, cities, and artifacts like ordinary craftsmen, but those were merely the earliest applications of their power, since their true mastery allowed them to forge things that other civilizations did not even consider physical materials. Fire could be placed inside their forge alongside gravity, while bloodlines could be combined with elements, curses could be fused with weapons, and techniques could be reforged together with supernatural Authorities until the original distinction between them disappeared.
This was the true nature of Heaven Forge.

When several things entered the Forge, they were not simply attached together or activated at the same time, because Heaven Forge broke them down to their fundamental properties before rebuilding them as a new and unified existence. A blade forged from fire and lightning would therefore not merely possess flames surrounding electricity, because the finished creation could become something whose very nature carried both properties as one, while more advanced Anvil Titans could perform the same process with abilities, souls, divine energies, celestial phenomena, bloodlines, natural laws, and even powers belonging to completely different systems.

Because of this, the Anvil Titans never developed a strict classification for what could or could not become forging material, and their only true limitations were the strength of the smith, the stability of the materials, and the amount of energy required to complete the forging.
As their understanding grew, Vorgael itself gradually changed alongside them.

Stars were converted into furnaces whose heat could temper powers that ordinary Titan flames could not affect, while black holes became compression chambers used to force incompatible materials together under gravity that few living bodies could survive. Dead planets were reshaped into planetary anvils, and entire nebulae became reservoirs containing matter, elemental energy, and rare cosmic substances collected over millions of years.

Their cities were forged instead of constructed, and some of their greatest structures were created from materials taken from several different worlds, causing entire continents to possess properties that had never naturally existed in Vorgael.
Eventually, the strongest Anvil Titans learned to carry living forges inside their own bodies.

At that level, they no longer required stationary workshops, because their hearts became furnaces while their bodies served as anvils capable of containing the pressure produced during supernatural forging. During battle, such Titans could seize an incoming attack, combine it with one of their own Authorities and material taken from the battlefield, then forge everything into a new technique before the fight had even ended.

This ability made encounters with high-level Anvil Titans increasingly unpredictable, because revealing a powerful technique before them could potentially provide another material for the Titan’s next creation.

Their civilization reached its highest point after the completion of The First Grand Forge, a structure located at the center of Vorgael and connected to countless lesser forges throughout the universe.

According to the surviving records, the First Grand Forge was constructed using the core of Vorgael’s first star, the gravitational remnant of a collapsed galaxy, fragments of several natural laws, and the remains of three divine beings defeated during the Anvil Titans’ expansion. The soul-fire of their first emperor was eventually added as the final component, turning the Forge into something that behaved less like a machine and more like a living extension of their entire civilization.
With the First Grand Forge, projects that no single Anvil Titan could complete became possible.

Thousands of Titans could contribute power simultaneously while the Forge processed materials on a universal scale, allowing Vorgael to create new supernatural phenomena that had never naturally formed anywhere within their reality.

Among their greatest smiths were beings who earned titles such as World-Smith, Law-Forger, and God-Anvil, with each title representing achievements rather than simple positions of nobility. A World-Smith could use planets and celestial structures as forging material, while a Law-Forger possessed enough understanding to place fragments of natural laws inside the Forge, and those known as God-Anvils had developed bodies capable of enduring forces that could destroy ordinary divine beings during the forging process.
Standing above all of them was the ruler of their civilization, remembered only as The First Smith.

The First Smith was considered the greatest practitioner of Heaven Forge ever born among the Anvil Titans, and legends claimed that he could simultaneously control forging processes that would normally require entire groups of Law-Forgers. One surviving story described him taking seven incompatible Authorities belonging to different cosmic beings and reforging them into a single attack, after which he used that creation against something located beyond the boundary of Vorgael.
No surviving record explains what he struck.
However, something answered.
That event became the beginning of the end for the Anvil Titans.

Their success had gradually convinced them that everything capable of interacting with existence could eventually be understood as material, so after detecting something beyond the borders of their universe, the greatest smiths of Vorgael made a decision that later records described as their final forging.
Instead of merely observing the unknown existence, they opened the First Grand Forge toward it and attempted to drag a portion of whatever existed beyond Vorgael into their universe.
Their intention was simple.
They wanted to forge it.
For the first time in the history of their civilization, the First Grand Forge rejected the material.
Before the connection could be closed, something crossed through instead.

No complete record exists of what followed, because the destruction of Vorgael did not resemble an ordinary war or universal collapse. Stars began disappearing without explosions, while forge networks went silent one after another, and several Anvil Titan cities were later found completely intact despite every inhabitant having vanished.
There were no corpses left behind.
There were no souls waiting to be recovered.
There was no residual energy suggesting that those Titans had fought or fled.
Even unfinished weapons remained resting beside active anvils, as though their smiths had simply disappeared between one hammer strike and the next.
The First Grand Forge eventually stopped burning, and soon afterward, Vorgael itself vanished from the pathways connecting realities.

Whether the Anvil Titans were destroyed, transported somewhere beyond their universe, or transformed into something through the very principle they had spent their existence mastering has never been confirmed.
Only fragments of their teachings survived.
Among those remnants, one principle appears repeatedly within every surviving record of Heaven Forge:
The forge does not care what something once was, because its purpose is to decide what that thing can become.
That principle eventually became the Origin Law associated with the Anvil Titans, and it explained both the greatness of their civilization and the mistake that ended it.
They believed there was no absolute incompatibility between powers, no final state that could never be changed, and no material that could not eventually enter the Forge.
For most of their history, they were right.
Until the day they tried to forge something that should never have been brought into their universe.

Luke fell silent after finishing the Anvil Titan’s lore, because despite becoming a civilization capable of forging abilities, laws, celestial bodies, and almost anything else they could understand, the Anvil Titans had still disappeared in the end because of the same philosophy that had driven their entire race forward.
They had believed that anything could become material for the Forge, and eventually, they had tried to prove that belief against something they didn’t understand.
"Sigh..."
Luke released a quiet sigh as he continued walking through the palace corridor, while the System screen floated beside him and the last lines of the Anvil Titan’s history remained visible.
