Rank: SSR
Type: Origin Skill
Classification: Origin Authority
Status: Awakened
Previous Evolution:
"NEXUS TITAN — SSS+"
[DESCRIPTION]
"The Origin Skill born from the Titans who forged impossibility itself."
Beyond the realities known to Valtharion once existed an ancient universe inhabited by a Titan civilization that did not depend upon gods, predetermined paths, or any single natural law.
They were known as—
"THE ANVIL TITANS"

Unlike ordinary Titans who specialized in particular elements, bodies, Authorities, or laws, the Anvil Titans devoted themselves entirely to Forging, and to them, ordinary metal was merely the simplest material that could enter a forge.

Fire, gravity, bloodlines, abilities, souls, curses, techniques, divine power, celestial bodies, Authorities, natural phenomena, and even forces that should normally be incompatible could all be treated as forging materials.
Through this path, they eventually created an Origin Method that surpassed every conventional form of fusion.
[ORIGIN AUTHORITY]
■ "HEAVEN FORGE"
"The forge does not care what something once was; it only cares what it can become."

Heaven Forge allows the wielder to treat powers, abilities, techniques, energies, substances, phenomena, and other valid existences as forging materials, then merge and reforge them into a completely new result.

The process does not simply activate several abilities at the same time, because once the forging is completed, the original materials are combined into a single unified phenomenon that carries properties from everything used to create it.
[ANVIL TITAN LORE...]
"Okay, this is even more broken than the previous one."

Luke muttered in genuine surprise as he continued reading the new Authority, because what Heaven Forge allowed him to accomplish reminded him of the attack he had created inside the artificial world, yet the principle behind the two was completely different.

Back then, Luke had forced several techniques and abilities to work together at the same time, using Cosmic Eclipse, Heaven’s Palm, Severance, Absolute Strength, and the support of multiple Cosmic Systems to create the Cosmic Severinity Eclipse Punch.
The result had been absurdly powerful, but achieving it had required several different conditions to align, along with enough control to keep all those powers functioning together without collapsing.

More importantly, Luke had only been able to attempt something on that scale because he was using an Atlas-based physique, and even then, Vorthar had been the better choice because its body could endure far greater backlash than his other Titan forms.

If Luke had attempted the same combination through one of his weaker Titan bodies, the strain alone would likely have overwhelmed the transformation and forced him back into his human form long before the attack was completed.
Heaven Forge completely changed that problem.

Instead of forcing several independent powers to cooperate temporarily, the Anvil Titan’s method could take those abilities, techniques, energies, or other materials and genuinely forge them into a single unified result, meaning the finished technique would no longer behave like several different powers being maintained at once.

Even better, because Heaven Forge had become part of his Origin Skill, Luke could access it through any of his Harmonized Titans rather than being restricted to Atlas Titan or Vorthar whenever he wanted to create a complicated combination.
’System, thanks for finding me such an amazing Titan.’
Luke praised the System sincerely while continuing through the palace corridor.
[It’s fine.]
[You should also read their lore.

Understanding where these Titans came from and how they used their abilities may help you grasp their methods faster, and you might even learn something that isn’t immediately obvious from the Authority description.]
Luke paused for half a step before continuing forward as though nothing had happened, while several servants passed through the corridor without paying him much attention.

Recently, he had noticed that the System had begun providing far more detailed lore concerning the Titans connected to him, just as it had done after Sevaroth awakened, and although Luke had originally treated those histories as additional information, he had gradually realized how useful they actually were.

Knowing how a Titan civilization had developed its methods, what problems those methods were created to solve, and how their strongest members had used them gave Luke far more insight than simply reading an ability description.
"Alright, show me."
The System responded immediately, and the previous screen disappeared before another page unfolded in front of Luke.
[ANVIL TITAN — LORE]

Long before the rise of many known civilizations, somewhere beyond the realities connected to Valtharion existed a universe called *Vorgael*, a realm where an ancient Titan race developed along a path completely different from ordinary elemental, physical, or Authority-based Titans.

These beings eventually became known as the *Anvil Titans*, although the name had little to do with ordinary blacksmithing, because by the height of their civilization, metal was considered one of the simplest materials their forges could handle.

The foundation of their civilization was an ancient Origin Method known as *Heaven Forge*, a technique born from a simple belief that defined their entire species: if something existed, then under the correct conditions, it could become material for something new.

Anvil Titans could certainly forge weapons, armor, cities, and artifacts like ordinary craftsmen, but those were merely the earliest applications of their power, since their true mastery allowed them to forge things that other civilizations did not even consider physical materials.

Fire could be placed inside their forge alongside gravity, while bloodlines could be combined with elements, curses could be fused with weapons, and techniques could be reforged together with supernatural Authorities until the original distinction between them disappeared.
This was the true nature of Heaven Forge.

When several things entered the Forge, they were not simply attached together or activated at the same time, because Heaven Forge broke them down to their fundamental properties before rebuilding them as a new and unified existence.

A blade forged from fire and lightning would therefore not merely possess flames surrounding electricity, because the finished creation could become something whose very nature carried both properties as one, while more advanced Anvil Titans could perform the same process with abilities, souls, divine energies, celestial phenomena, bloodlines, natural laws, and even powers belonging to completely different systems.

Because of this, the Anvil Titans never developed a strict classification for what could or could not become forging material, and their only true limitations were the strength of the smith, the stability of the materials, and the amount of energy required to complete the forging.
As their understanding grew, Vorgael itself gradually changed alongside them.

Stars were converted into furnaces whose heat could temper powers that ordinary Titan flames could not affect, while black holes became compression chambers used to force incompatible materials together under gravity that few living bodies could survive.
Dead planets were reshaped into planetary anvils, and entire nebulae became reservoirs containing matter, elemental energy, and rare cosmic substances collected over millions of years.

Their cities were forged instead of constructed, and some of their greatest structures were created from materials taken from several different worlds, causing entire continents to possess properties that had never naturally existed in Vorgael.
Eventually, the strongest Anvil Titans learned to carry living forges inside their own bodies.

At that level, they no longer required stationary workshops, because their hearts became furnaces while their bodies served as anvils capable of containing the pressure produced during supernatural forging.

During battle, such Titans could seize an incoming attack, combine it with one of their own Authorities and material taken from the battlefield, then forge everything into a new technique before the fight had even ended.

This ability made encounters with high-level Anvil Titans increasingly unpredictable, because revealing a powerful technique before them could potentially provide another material for the Titan’s next creation.

Their civilization reached its highest point after the completion of The First Grand Forge, a structure located at the center of Vorgael and connected to countless lesser forges throughout the universe.

According to the surviving records, the First Grand Forge was constructed using the core of Vorgael’s first star, the gravitational remnant of a collapsed galaxy, fragments of several natural laws, and the remains of three divine beings defeated during the Anvil Titans’ expansion.

The soul-fire of their first emperor was eventually added as the final component, turning the Forge into something that behaved less like a machine and more like a living extension of their entire civilization.
With the First Grand Forge, projects that no single Anvil Titan could complete became possible.

Thousands of Titans could contribute power simultaneously while the Forge processed materials on a universal scale, allowing Vorgael to create new supernatural phenomena that had never naturally formed anywhere within their reality.
Among their greatest smiths were beings who earned titles such as World-Smith, Law-Forger, and God-Anvil, with each title representing achievements rather than simple positions of nobility.

A World-Smith could use planets and celestial structures as forging material, while a Law-Forger possessed enough understanding to place fragments of natural laws inside the Forge, and those known as God-Anvils had developed bodies capable of enduring forces that could destroy ordinary divine beings during the forging process.
Standing above all of them was the ruler of their civilization, remembered only as The First Smith.

The First Smith was considered the greatest practitioner of Heaven Forge ever born among the Anvil Titans, and legends claimed that he could simultaneously control forging processes that would normally require entire groups of Law-Forgers.

One surviving story described him taking seven incompatible Authorities belonging to different cosmic beings and reforging them into a single attack, after which he used that creation against something located beyond the boundary of Vorgael.
No surviving record explains what he struck.
However, something answered.
That event became the beginning of the end for the Anvil Titans.

Their success had gradually convinced them that everything capable of interacting with existence could eventually be understood as material, so after detecting something beyond the borders of their universe, the greatest smiths of Vorgael made a decision that later records described as their final forging.
Instead of merely observing the unknown existence, they opened the First Grand Forge toward it and attempted to drag a portion of whatever existed beyond Vorgael into their universe.
Their intention was simple.
They wanted to forge it.
For the first time in the history of their civilization, the First Grand Forge rejected the material.
Before the connection could be closed, something crossed through instead.
No complete record exists of what followed, because the destruction of Vorgael did not resemble an ordinary war or universal collapse.

Stars began disappearing without explosions, while forge networks went silent one after another, and several Anvil Titan cities were later found completely intact despite every inhabitant having vanished.
There were no corpses left behind.
There were no souls waiting to be recovered.
There was no residual energy suggesting that those Titans had fought or fled.
Even unfinished weapons remained resting beside active anvils, as though their smiths had simply disappeared between one hammer strike and the next.
The First Grand Forge eventually stopped burning, and soon afterward, Vorgael itself vanished from the pathways connecting realities.

Whether the Anvil Titans were destroyed, transported somewhere beyond their universe, or transformed into something through the very principle they had spent their existence mastering has never been confirmed.
Only fragments of their teachings survived.
Among those remnants, one principle appears repeatedly within every surviving record of Heaven Forge:
The forge does not care what something once was, because its purpose is to decide what that thing can become.
That principle eventually became the Origin Law associated with the Anvil Titans, and it explained both the greatness of their civilization and the mistake that ended it.
They believed there was no absolute incompatibility between powers, no final state that could never be changed, and no material that could not eventually enter the Forge.
For most of their history, they were right.
Until the day they tried to forge something that should never have been brought into their universe.

Luke fell silent after finishing the Anvil Titan’s lore, because despite becoming a civilization capable of forging abilities, laws, celestial bodies, and almost anything else they could understand, the Anvil Titans had still disappeared in the end because of the same philosophy that had driven their entire race forward.
They had believed that anything could become material for the Forge, and eventually, they had tried to prove that belief against something they didn’t understand.
"Sigh..."
Luke released a quiet sigh as he continued walking through the palace corridor, while the System screen floated beside him and the last lines of the Anvil Titan’s history remained visible.

He was still curious about what the First Grand Forge had refused to process, and even more curious about what had actually happened to the Anvil Titans afterward, because the records never clearly stated whether they had been destroyed, taken somewhere else, or transformed into something through their own final forging.
Still, there was no point thinking too deeply about a mystery he couldn’t solve right now, especially when even the System hadn’t provided an answer.

chapters.title: Chapter 339: The Titans Who Turned Existence Into Records!
paragraphs: [EPITAPH TITAN]
Rank: SSR+
Type: Origin Skill
Classification: Origin Authority
Status: Awakened
Previous Evolution:
"ANVIL TITAN — SSR"
[DESCRIPTION]
"The Origin Skill born from those who refused to allow existence to disappear."

Within another reality once existed an ancient Titan civilization that feared neither death nor destruction, because they believed true loss occurred only when every trace of an existence was forgotten.
They were known as—
"THE EPITAPH TITANS"

Through studying existence itself, the Epitaph Titans discovered that everything which exists leaves behind information recording what it was at a particular instant, whether it is a living being, soul, weapon, technique, structure, natural phenomenon, celestial body, or even an entire world.

They called this information a Record, and after countless generations of study, they eventually learned how to perceive those Records, preserve them, and restore what had once existed through their supreme Origin Method—
"FINAL RECORD"
[ORIGIN AUTHORITY]
■ "FINAL RECORD"
"Existence may end, but its Record does not."

Anything that exists within Luke’s effective presence can leave behind an Origin Record, preserving the complete state of that existence at the moment it was recorded rather than merely storing its appearance or physical condition.

Depending on the target, a Record may preserve its body, soul, memories, bloodline, energy, cultivation, abilities, injuries, equipment, techniques, structure, supernatural properties, and other information belonging to its existence at that instant.

This authority is not limited to living beings, allowing weapons, artifacts, summons, constructs, terrain, natural phenomena, celestial bodies, and eventually far greater existences to be recorded as Luke’s mastery grows.
"Okay, now this one is even more absurd than the last."

Luke commented after finishing the description, because the Epitaph Titans had somehow reached into aspects such as time, fate, creation, oblivion, and several other forces before eventually developing a supreme Origin Method that allowed them to preserve the existence of almost anything.
"A supreme Origin Method really isn’t an exaggeration this time."
Luke continued walking through the palace corridor while rereading the description of Final Record, and the more he understood what the Authority actually did, the more ridiculous it seemed.

If someone died after being properly recorded within his presence, Luke could potentially restore that person through their Final Record, and this wasn’t some ordinary resurrection method that summoned a soul back into a recreated body or produced an imitation carrying the deceased person’s memories.

The Record preserved the existence itself at that instant, including the person’s body, soul, memories, bloodline, cultivation, abilities, and identity, meaning that if Luke possessed a valid Record and enough power to restore it, the person who had died could genuinely return according to the state preserved within that Record.
Luke remained quiet for several seconds after realizing what that actually meant.

Even his current restriction, which only allowed him to restore things that had already been destroyed or killed, didn’t make the Authority feel any less unreasonable, especially when he considered what it might become once his strength increased.
"If the Authority description is already this ridiculous, I really want to know what kind of civilization managed to create it."
With that thought, Luke dismissed the ability page and called up the next section of the System.
"Alright, let’s see what the Epitaph Titans’ lore contains."
The screen changed immediately, and a new page unfolded before him.
[EPITAPH TITAN — LORE]

Far beyond the realities known to Valtharion once existed a universe called Mementh, a realm inhabited by an ancient Titan civilization whose development followed a path unlike almost anything found in other worlds. While many civilizations pursued greater strength, immortality, divine authority, or control over natural laws, the beings who came to be known as the Epitaph Titans devoted themselves to a single question that eventually shaped their entire existence: if something had truly existed once, why should its destruction mean that it could never exist again?

Their search for an answer led to the discovery of an ancient Origin Method known as Final Record, an ability based upon the understanding that everything leaves behind information simply by existing.

A sword possessed a Record describing the material, shape, energy, enchantments, damage, and every other property composing it at a particular moment, while a living being carried an incomparably more complex Record containing the body, soul, memories, bloodline, cultivation, abilities, injuries, and countless smaller details that together formed that person’s existence.
The Epitaph Titans discovered that these Records were not merely memories.
They were blueprints of existence.

Once they learned how to perceive those Records, their civilization changed permanently, because destruction gradually stopped carrying the same finality it possessed everywhere else. If a treasured weapon shattered during battle while a valid Record remained preserved, an Epitaph Titan could reconstruct the weapon according to that Record, while a destroyed fortress, broken artifact, collapsed magical formation, or even a celestial construct could be restored in exactly the condition it possessed when recorded.
Eventually, they discovered that living beings were no exception.

If an Epitaph Titan successfully recorded someone while that person was alive and later witnessed their death, Final Record could reconstruct the deceased existence from its last valid living Record, returning the same body, soul, memories, bloodline, abilities, and identity rather than creating an imitation or placing another soul inside a recreated vessel.
To the Epitaph Titans, this was not considered necromancy or conventional resurrection, because they were not commanding the dead to return.
They were simply restoring an existence whose complete Record had never been lost.

As their mastery increased, Mementh gradually transformed around this philosophy, and ordinary monuments became increasingly uncommon because the Epitaph Titans preferred to preserve civilizations through enormous Archives containing Records rather than statues describing what had once existed. Cities recorded themselves at regular intervals, royal families maintained generations of living Records, military fleets carried independent Archives into distant wars, while important worlds maintained planetary Records capable of preserving landscapes, oceans, civilizations, and structures should catastrophe ever destroy them.
At the center of this civilization stood the greatest structure ever created by their species, an Origin Archive known as The Great Epitaph.

The Great Epitaph eventually expanded across a region larger than several star systems, with entire sections devoted to storing Records gathered throughout Mementh’s history. Within its depths were preserved kings who had died millions of years earlier, extinct Titan lineages, vanished species, destroyed cities, ancient weapons, fallen moons, dead stars, forgotten oceans, and civilizations whose final surviving members had chosen to entrust their existence to the Archive before disappearing from history.
Because of this, the Epitaph Titans gradually developed a relationship with history that would appear almost incomprehensible to ordinary civilizations.
For them, the past was not completely unreachable.
If the Record survived, the past could return.

The greatest practitioners of Final Record eventually advanced far beyond restoring destroyed objects or recently deceased beings, because once their understanding reached its peak, they learned how to call upon Records belonging to previous ages and temporarily replace portions of the present with what had existed before.

A battlefield ruined by centuries of war could be restored to the landscape recorded before the first battle occurred, while a planet shattered generations earlier could be reconstructed from a complete planetary Record if sufficient power was available. Dead armies could return exactly as they had existed before their deaths, including their weapons, cultivation, memories, and identities, while celestial bodies that had collapsed long ago could once again burn within the sky.

The most powerful Epitaph Titans even maintained continuous Records of themselves, updating those Records throughout their lives so that destroying their body or soul was no longer enough to guarantee death.
As long as a sufficiently complete Record remained somewhere beyond the enemy’s reach, the Titan could eventually be restored.

Among their entire civilization, however, one existence surpassed every other master of Final Record, and history eventually forgot the being’s original name because only one title remained associated with him.
The Last Scribe.

The Last Scribe possessed an understanding of Records so profound that he could preserve events and existences on scales that other Epitaph Titans could scarcely manage. Where lesser masters recorded individuals or cities, he recorded continents, while worlds that entered his perception could be preserved with enough detail that their civilizations, environments, and living populations could later be reconstructed together.
Eventually, even that became insufficient for him.

Near the height of Mementh’s civilization, the Last Scribe began creating the greatest Record their species had ever attempted, gathering information from every major Archive and connecting the Great Epitaph directly to the Record network spread throughout their universe.
The result became known simply as the Final Record of Mementh.

Within it were supposedly contained every world, star, city, Titan, civilization, Archive, and major existence belonging to their universe at the moment the Record was completed, creating the theoretical possibility that even if Mementh itself were somehow destroyed, their entire civilization could one day be restored.
For a people who had spent ages defeating the finality of destruction, it should have represented their greatest achievement.
Instead, sometime after the Record was completed, Mementh disappeared.
There was no known universal war preceding the event, no recorded explosion capable of destroying the realm, and no surviving account describing armies invading their territory.
One moment, pathways between realities still led toward Mementh.
Later, those same pathways ended in emptiness.
Nothing remained where their universe should have been.

Centuries later, fragments believed to have belonged to the Great Epitaph began appearing throughout completely unrelated realities, yet what made these discoveries disturbing was that every recovered fragment carried exactly the same final inscription, despite having been found across worlds that had never communicated with one another.
The message contained only four words:
"DO NOT RESTORE US."

No surviving Record explains why the Epitaph Titans left that warning, although its meaning created a terrifying contradiction surrounding their disappearance, because these were beings who had spent their entire civilization defeating death and preserving everything they considered precious.
Whatever happened inside Mementh had therefore frightened them enough that restoration itself became something they wished to prevent.

Some ancient scholars later suggested that Mementh had not actually been destroyed, but deliberately removed from the pathways connecting realities, while others believed the Epitaph Titans discovered something hidden inside their own Records that should never have been restored.

A darker possibility suggested that something entered the Great Epitaph and became part of the Final Record of Mementh, meaning restoring their civilization would also restore whatever had caused them to disappear.
No proof remains for any explanation.
The Final Record of Mementh has never been found.
The Record belonging to the Last Scribe has also never been recovered.
Yet among the scattered remnants of their civilization, one principle continues appearing again and again, representing the belief that once allowed the Epitaph Titans to challenge death itself:
Existence may end, but its Record does not, and as long as the Record remains, what was lost may one day return.
"Another incredible Titan race was born, and yet this civilization also disappeared because of its obsession with recording everything."
Luke muttered after finishing the lore, while his thoughts naturally returned to the possibilities surrounding Mementh’s disappearance.

One possibility bothered him more than the others: perhaps the Epitaph Titans had truly recorded something that had already been erased from existence and was never meant to return, and if that unknown being had somehow become linked to the Final Record, then whatever force had erased it in the first place might have also erased Mementh simply because the entire civilization had become connected to that same Record.

If that theory was correct, then restoring Mementh could also restore the very existence that had caused its disappearance in the first place, which would explain why fragments of the Great Epitaph carried the warning telling anyone who found them not to restore their civilization.
"Another unsolved mystery."

Luke let out a quiet sigh as he dismissed the lore page, because every world and every universe seemed to contain histories and secrets buried so deeply that even beings standing near the peak of existence could disappear without leaving behind a complete answer.
"Whatever. I’ll find out someday if I ever reach that far."
With that thought, Luke finally looked ahead and realized that while reading through the System’s lore, he had already reached the end of the corridor.
Selene’s room was directly in front of him.
A small smile appeared on Luke’s face as he reached for the handle.
"I’m here."
His hand closed around the knob before turning it downward.
CLICK.

chapters.title: Chapter 342: An Organization Where Nobody Shows Their Real Face!
paragraphs: 18th day of Fructus, Year 50,001.

Night had already settled over the underground city, although there was no moon or open sky here to mark its arrival, and the only difference between day and night came from the hundreds of hanging lamps burning along the streets and the pale crystals embedded across the cavern ceiling far above, whose usual glow had been dimmed until only muted blue-white light spread between the stone buildings.

Among the people moving through one of the broader streets was a man completely covered by a long brown robe, with the hood pulled low enough to conceal most of his face, yet the quality of the cloth, his clean leather boots, and the well-maintained gloves visible beneath his sleeves made it clear that he was considerably wealthier than the average person walking around him.

He moved at an unhurried pace through the crowd while wagons and caravans passed on either side, some pulled by ordinary horses and others by muscular beasts fitted with iron harnesses, their wheels repeatedly striking the uneven stone road with dull CLACK—CLACK—CLACK sounds as workers shouted at people to clear the way.
"Move aside! If you lose a foot under these wheels, don’t expect me to pay for it!"
"Then learn how to control your damn beast!"
"Say that again."
The second man immediately placed his hand on the sword hanging from his waist, while the caravan driver reached beneath his seat and pulled out a short iron club.
Several nearby people glanced toward them, though instead of becoming alarmed, most merely shifted a little farther away so they would not accidentally become involved.
"Go fight somewhere else," a scar-faced vendor shouted from behind his stall. "You’re blocking customers."
"Shut your mouth!"

The argument quickly escalated until the swordsman’s fist slammed into the caravan driver’s face with a heavy THUD, sending him stumbling against the side of the wagon, while the frightened draft beast jerked against its harness and released a rough snort.
The brown-robed man simply stepped around them without slowing.

His gaze barely remained on the fight for more than an instant, because scenes like this were hardly unusual here, and the crowd itself treated the violence with the same indifference, with some continuing their conversations while others briefly watched in case the fight became entertaining enough to justify stopping.
The deeper he walked, the more obvious the nature of the underground city became.

Almost every uncovered face carried something that separated its owner from an ordinary citizen above ground, whether it was an old sword scar crossing a cheek, a burn mark near the jaw, a missing ear, a crooked nose that had clearly been broken more than once, or the rough expression of someone accustomed to solving disputes with steel rather than law. Many others wore cloaks and robes similar to his own, keeping their appearances hidden while moving between dim taverns, weapon shops, gambling houses, medicine stalls, and narrow buildings whose true businesses were rarely advertised openly.
"Three bottles of Nightroot Poison, same strength as last time."
"Six gold each."
"You charged four yesterday."
"Yesterday, the city guard hadn’t seized one of my suppliers."

A few steps farther away, another pair stood beneath a hanging lamp while exchanging a small wrapped package without even looking directly at one another, and nearby, two armored men dragged an unconscious fellow through an alley while a woman leaning against the wall watched them disappear before returning to the drink in her hand.
The brown-robed man ignored all of it.

He had walked these streets enough times that the shouting, occasional clash of steel, muffled conversations, rattling caravans, and suspicious figures had already become part of the city’s background noise, while the dim lighting from the lamps and overhead crystals only made the shadows between the buildings deeper.

After passing through several crowded streets, he eventually left the noisier market lanes and entered a quieter section where fewer stalls occupied the roadside and most businesses operated behind closed doors.
His pace remained unchanged until a familiar three-story building appeared ahead.

Its lower floor had been constructed from dark stone, while the upper two floors used reinforced timber that had long since lost whatever color it originally possessed, and the narrow shuttered windows made the building appear more like an old record house than the headquarters of an information organization. A faded wooden sign hung above the entrance advertising ordinary copying and record services, while nothing on the exterior carried the name by which certain people knew the place.
The Prime Archive.
The man’s expression did not change as he approached.
This was far from his first visit.

Two bulky men stood beside the entrance wearing simple shirts, dark trousers, and leather boots, making them look more like hired guards than members of a secret organization, although the swords resting openly in their hands made it clear that nobody was expected to enter without permission.
Both guards looked toward the brown-robed visitor.
Neither stopped him.
One merely shifted his sword slightly aside, allowing the man to pass through the doorway without a word.
The atmosphere changed immediately once he entered.

Compared with the streets outside, the first floor was almost unnaturally quiet, despite several people coming and going through the building. Five wide rooms occupied the floor around a central passage, and visitors were quietly separated depending on what they had come to buy, sell, or investigate, with ordinary requests handled in the rooms below while anything requiring greater secrecy was taken upstairs.

A hooded woman emerged from one room holding a folded document against her chest and left without speaking to anyone, while an older man waiting beside another doorway was called inside moments later.
"Room three."
The older man nodded and entered without asking questions.
At the far end of the corridor, another customer was being led toward the stairs, suggesting that whatever information he sought was considered important enough for the second floor.
The brown-robed man had barely stopped when a plainly dressed male member approached him.
"Please follow me, sir."
The visitor gave a small nod and followed him upstairs.

No unnecessary conversation occurred during the climb, and even upon reaching the second floor, the same restrained atmosphere remained, with footsteps kept quiet and voices coming through the closed doors reduced to indistinct murmurs.
The man guiding him stopped before one of the five rooms, opened the door, and gestured for him to enter.
Inside sat a woman behind a broad wooden desk.

Her loose gray-brown clothing concealed the shape of her body almost completely, while her face belonged to what appeared to be an ordinary middle-aged woman, with slightly weathered skin, plain brown hair, and features so average that most people would struggle to remember them after leaving the room.
Of course, that face was not real.
Neither were most of the faces belonging to the Prime Archive’s members.

They rarely wore obvious masks because obvious masks invited attention; instead, their special disguises imitated human skin closely enough that casual observers would believe they were simply looking at another ordinary person, and only a small number of regular customers had discovered that the faces greeting them inside the Prime Archive could change.
The woman seated behind the desk was Ada Dale, although the visitor knew neither that name nor what her true appearance looked like.

Beside the closed door stood another male member wearing equally simple clothing, his presence quiet enough that someone entering carelessly might forget he was there, while a darker corner beside one of the shelves concealed another figure whose outline blended almost completely with the shadows.
Ada looked toward the brown-robed visitor and spoke in an even voice.
"Welcome back, sir. Please take a seat."
The man paused only briefly before sitting opposite her.

He showed no surprise that she had recognized him despite the robe concealing his appearance, because this organization dealt in information for a living, and if they could not recognize regular clients through disguises, he would never have trusted them with matters this sensitive in the first place.
He had long suspected that the Prime Archive possessed some kind of identification skill or method, though he had never bothered asking exactly how it worked.
After settling into the chair, he went directly to the reason for his visit.
"I’m looking for an adventurer named Harlan Reed, an Early D-Rank man somewhere in his middle years."
Ada remained silent, waiting for him to continue.

"Several days ago, he was hired as part of an escort party traveling through the western road outside Arvelon. The entire group was later found dead, but Reed’s body wasn’t among them, and nobody has seen him since."
The man stopped there.

He did not explain why Harlan Reed mattered, nor did he mention that the escort had been transporting something valuable that belonged to the people behind him, because the Prime Archive had never demanded reasons when information alone was enough to complete a request.
Ada considered the details for several moments before answering.
"If you only require his current whereabouts, the price will be one hundred gold."
The brown-robed man showed no reaction to the amount.
He reached beneath his robe, removed a prepared pouch, and placed it on the table with a soft THUMP.
"Fifty."
Ada glanced at the pouch before returning her attention to him.
"The remaining half after confirmation?
"Same arrangement as before."
"Understood."
She raised one hand and gave a small motion toward the darker side of the room.
The figure hidden there immediately stepped forward.
The visitor’s gaze followed him, though no tension entered his posture, because he had seen the Prime Archive use hidden guards and assistants during his previous visits.

The man crossed toward one of the shelves lining the rear wall, where books, sealed ledgers, bundled papers, and scroll containers had been arranged according to a system known only to the organization’s members.
For the next several minutes, he checked one section after another, occasionally removing a ledger, scanning several entries, and returning it before moving farther along.
Nobody spoke while he searched.
The only sounds inside the room came from pages turning, the faint movement of footsteps outside, and the distant murmur of another conversation behind one of the neighboring walls.
Around five minutes later, the assistant finally pulled a narrow scroll from between two thicker records and brought it to Ada.
She opened it, read several lines, and then looked toward the visitor.
"Harlan Reed survived the attack."
The man beneath the brown hood remained still.
Ada continued.

"Two nights after the escort party was killed, someone matching his description purchased food and wound medicine from a traveling trader east of Willowbrook Village. Yesterday afternoon, one of our contacts confirmed that he was still there, staying inside an abandoned grain store near the northern edge of the village."
"Willowbrook Village," the man repeated, committing the name to memory.
"Approximately sixty kilometers southeast of Arvelon’s western trade road," Ada added. "Unless he moved sometime after yesterday evening, that should still be his location."
The visitor remained silent for a moment before reaching beneath his robe again and placing a second pouch beside the first.
Another soft *THUMP* sounded against the table.
"The remaining fifty."
Ada pulled both pouches toward her without counting them immediately.
"If the information proves outdated because he moved after our last confirmation, bring this transaction token on your next visit and we will check again without charging for the same search."
She slid a small plain token across the table.
The man picked it up and tucked it beneath his robe.
"That’s all I needed."
He rose from the chair, gave neither Ada nor the silent guards any unnecessary farewell, and left the room before descending through the same quiet building.
Nobody stopped him on the way out.

Within a short time, the brown-robed figure had returned to the underground street, where the city’s dim lamps, ceiling crystals, rough voices, and occasional clashes swallowed him back into the crowd until there was nothing separating him from the dozens of other cloaked figures moving beneath the night.
High above, on the third floor of the Prime Archive, someone stood beside a shuttered window and watched the familiar brown robe disappear between the buildings.
His appearance was completely ordinary, with nothing about his face or clothing suggesting that the entire organization below ultimately answered to him.
It was Zevan Crest.
Or, more precisely, one of Luke’s clones.
He watched until the customer vanished beyond the next street before calmly turning away from the window.

chapters.title: Chapter 343: "While the Main Body Enjoys His Honeymoon, I’m Working!"
paragraphs: "Sigh... while the main body is enjoying his honeymoon, I’m stuck here working myself to death."
Zevan leaned back against his chair and cursed Luke under his breath, which was rather ridiculous considering that he was technically cursing himself.

Originally, Luke had controlled his clones subconsciously at all times, continuously receiving their actions, thoughts, and surroundings through his mind, but after experimenting with Nyx’s doppelganger ability for some time, he discovered that constant awareness wasn’t actually necessary. Instead, he could allow the clones to operate entirely through the subconscious portion of his mind, and unless Luke deliberately focused on one of them, or the clone itself wanted to send something important back, the main body wouldn’t remain consciously aware of everything it was doing.

It was somewhat similar to how a person’s brain continuously controlled breathing, digestion, heartbeat, and numerous other bodily functions without forcing the person to consciously understand every process occurring inside their own body.
Because of that separation, Zevan could act, think, and experience things independently while still ultimately remaining Luke.
He tapped one finger against the armrest while recalling when everything had started.
"I arrived here with those two idiots on the 4th day of Fructus."
Naturally, the two idiots he was referring to were Luke’s other clones, who had traveled with him toward the Human Empire capital after leaving the main body behind.

They were currently in Arvelon City, the imperial capital of the Asterian Empire, and after arriving, the first several days had been spent simply understanding the city, because Arvelon was far too large and complicated for them to immediately establish their organizations without learning how its different districts operated.

One of the more important discoveries had been the existence of an entire Underground City beneath the capital, where much of Arvelon’s darker business took place beyond the sight of ordinary citizens, and after investigating the area, two of the clones had decided that it suited their organizations perfectly.
Zevan had established The Prime Archive, Luke’s information organization, while the second clone, who had chosen the name Warren Skell, established The Broken Halo, Luke’s assassination organization.

After Luke stopped consciously controlling them all the time, each clone had gradually begun developing a somewhat distinct persona of its own, which turned out to be another characteristic of Nyx’s doppelganger ability that Nyx himself probably would have explained if he weren’t currently sleeping.
"Let’s go meet those two."

Zevan pushed himself away from the chair and stood, straightening the simple black shirt covering his upper body, whose sleeves had been folded to his elbows, before adjusting his black trousers and leaving the third floor of the Prime Archive.

Like Luke’s other clones, Zevan currently wore a human-skin mask because none of them could casually walk around Arvelon while using Luke’s original face, especially when the Hero of Light was already becoming increasingly recognizable.
However, despite developing slightly different habits, there was one preference all three clones had inherited without any difference whatsoever.
They liked black.
Because of that, unless a particular situation demanded otherwise, most of their clothing somehow ended up being black or at least dark enough to resemble it.
"Good day, Boss."
"Boss."
Several members passing through the corridor greeted him as he descended, and Zevan acknowledged them with brief nods while continuing toward the entrance.

During the fifteen days in which Luke had been spending his time with Selene, the three clones had been anything but idle, and each organization had already gathered around one hundred ordinary members. Every one of those recruits had been an orphan whom the clones had carefully selected, and Luke’s blood magic had already been used to bind their loyalty, ensuring that even if circumstances changed in the future, betrayal would not become an immediate concern.
More surprisingly, however, the three clones had deliberately prevented their organizations from interacting with one another.

The Prime Archive’s members didn’t know that their actual master was merely one of Luke’s clones, nor did they know that another hundred people working under the same hidden master operated only a few blocks away inside The Broken Halo.
The same separation applied to the third organization as well.

Once Zevan stepped outside, the quieter atmosphere of the Prime Archive immediately gave way to the familiar disorder of the Underground City, where people moved through narrow streets beneath hanging lamps and dim crystal light while merchants whispered deals from shadowed storefronts, armed men pushed through crowds, and suspicious figures watched everyone who passed.
Zevan moved through the streets without slowing, ignoring several invitations, arguments, and attempts to draw him toward questionable businesses along the way.
Even when a nearly naked woman standing beside one of the narrow passages waved toward him with a practiced smile, he simply kept walking.
"Hey, handsome, why are you in such a hurry?"
Zevan didn’t even turn toward her.
"Tch, what a shameless method of gathering information.

Of course, in this place, a nearly naked woman standing along the road wasn’t necessarily selling her body, and that was exactly what made approaching anyone here troublesome, because many of the seemingly helpless women scattered around the Underground City were assassins, informants, thieves, or bait working for larger organizations.
And if someone wondered why they were standing outside instead of gathering information inside brothels, the answer was rather simple.
The brothels were already occupied by people belonging to stronger organizations.
"Competition even exists in a fantasy world."

Zevan’s mouth twitched as he remembered that, during the beginning of their operations, he had actually considered placing several female members inside brothels so they could gather information through music, dancing, and conversation rather than selling their bodies.

The idea had seemed practical at first, especially because the orphans they recruited were usually talented in one field or another, but the moment they tried approaching several establishments, the women were rejected almost immediately.
Arvelon’s brothels didn’t merely demand beauty.
They demanded exceptional beauty.
"Well, this is the Human Empire’s capital. What can I say?"

As that thought passed through his mind, Zevan couldn’t help remembering one particular night when he had thoroughly enjoyed the delicate hands of an Elven beauty working inside one of those establishments.
If Luke ever consciously received that memory, he would probably curse his own clone for taking advantage of his body to enjoy such things.

Worse still, if Luke’s wives somehow learned what one of his clones had been doing in the capital, the main body would probably be the one suffering the consequences despite not even being consciously involved.
"But what does that have to do with me?"
A shameless smile briefly appeared beneath Zevan’s disguise before he continued forward.

Zevan pushed himself away from the chair and stood, straightening the simple black shirt covering his upper body, whose sleeves had been folded to his elbows, before adjusting his black trousers and leaving the third floor of the Prime Archive.

Like Luke’s other clones, Zevan currently wore a human-skin mask because none of them could casually walk around Arvelon while using Luke’s original face, especially when the Hero of Light was already becoming increasingly recognizable.
However, despite developing slightly different habits, there was one preference all three clones had inherited without any difference whatsoever.
They liked black.
Because of that, unless a particular situation demanded otherwise, most of their clothing somehow ended up being black or at least dark enough to resemble it.
"Good day, Boss."
"Boss."
Several members passing through the corridor greeted him as he descended, and Zevan acknowledged them with brief nods while continuing toward the entrance.

During the fifteen days in which Luke had been spending his time with Selene, the three clones had been anything but idle, and each organization had already gathered around one hundred ordinary members.

Every one of those recruits had been an orphan whom the clones had carefully selected, and Luke’s blood magic had already been used to bind their loyalty, ensuring that even if circumstances changed in the future, betrayal would not become an immediate concern.
More surprisingly, however, the three clones had deliberately prevented their organizations from interacting with one another.

The Prime Archive’s members didn’t know that their actual master was merely one of Luke’s clones, nor did they know that another hundred people working under the same hidden master operated only a few blocks away inside The Broken Halo.
The same separation applied to the third organization as well.

Once Zevan stepped outside, the quieter atmosphere of the Prime Archive immediately gave way to the familiar disorder of the Underground City, where people moved through narrow streets beneath hanging lamps and dim crystal light while merchants whispered deals from shadowed storefronts, armed men pushed through crowds, and suspicious figures watched everyone who passed.
Zevan moved through the streets without slowing, ignoring several invitations, arguments, and attempts to draw him toward questionable businesses along the way.
Even when a nearly naked woman standing beside one of the narrow passages waved toward him with a practiced smile, he simply kept walking.
"Hey, handsome, why are you in such a hurry?"
Zevan didn’t even turn toward her.
"Tch, what a shameless method of gathering information.

Of course, in this place, a nearly naked woman standing along the road wasn’t necessarily selling her body, and that was exactly what made approaching anyone here troublesome, because many of the seemingly helpless women scattered around the Underground City were assassins, informants, thieves, or bait working for larger organizations.
And if someone wondered why they were standing outside instead of gathering information inside brothels, the answer was rather simple.
The brothels were already occupied by people belonging to stronger organizations.
"Competition even exists in a fantasy world."

Zevan’s mouth twitched as he remembered that, during the beginning of their operations, he had actually considered placing several female members inside brothels so they could gather information through music, dancing, and conversation rather than selling their bodies.

The idea had seemed practical at first, especially because the orphans they recruited were usually talented in one field or another, but the moment they tried approaching several establishments, the women were rejected almost immediately.
Arvelon’s brothels didn’t merely demand beauty.
They demanded exceptional beauty.
"Well, this is the Human Empire’s capital.
What can I say?"

As that thought passed through his mind, Zevan couldn’t help remembering one particular night when he had thoroughly enjoyed the delicate hands of an Elven beauty working inside one of those establishments.
If Luke ever consciously received that memory, he would probably curse his own clone for taking advantage of his body to enjoy such things.

Worse still, if Luke’s wives somehow learned what one of his clones had been doing in the capital, the main body would probably be the one suffering the consequences despite not even being consciously involved.
"But what does that have to do with me?"
A shameless smile briefly appeared beneath Zevan’s disguise before he continued forward.

chapters.title: Chapter 344: The Crownstar—Humanity’s Answer to Demigods!
paragraphs: After several more minutes of walking through the Underground City, he finally reached one of the passages connecting it to the surface and climbed upward until cool night air replaced the stale atmosphere below.
The moment he stepped outside, Zevan raised his head.
"Hmm... it’s already midnight."

The moon hung brightly in the night sky, although its light mattered surprisingly little inside Arvelon itself, because the capital possessed another source of illumination that easily overwhelmed it.
Before looking toward that, however, Zevan glanced toward the distant edge of the city, where an unbelievably high wall rose hundreds of meters into the air and stretched across the horizon.
"Even giants would struggle to cross that wall."
He clicked his tongue in amazement, because those walls were far more than oversized stone fortifications.

They had been constructed after the previous Human Emperor was slain by an Elven Demigod, and the materials, formations, and defensive enchantments built into them were powerful enough to withstand Demigod-level attacks.
Even that, however, wasn’t the most astonishing defense Arvelon possessed.
Zevan slowly turned toward the opposite side of the capital, where the Imperial Palace stood far in the distance, dominating the center of the city despite the kilometers separating them.
Above that palace floated what appeared to be a freaking star.

A blue star, hundreds of kilometers wide, remained suspended high above the Imperial Palace while controlled streams of radiant light continuously descended from it, spreading across Arvelon and illuminating the streets, towers, rooftops, walls, and districts even in the middle of the night.
"The Crownstar."
For once, genuine reverence entered Zevan’s voice.

The Crownstar was a Demigod-level artifact created under the current Human Emperor with the assistance of thousands of powerful mages, including S-Rank and SS-Rank practitioners, and its existence had fundamentally changed the position of humanity within Valtharion.

The Human Empire had not produced an actual Demigod, yet the Crownstar could both defend against one and unleash power capable of killing one, which meant humanity had effectively gained the same kind of deterrence even without possessing a Demigod of its own.
To Zevan, the concept was easy to understand.
It was no different from possessing a nuclear weapon in the modern world.
You didn’t necessarily need to fire it, because merely having something capable of guaranteeing unacceptable retaliation was enough to make most enemies reconsider attacking in the first place.

If another race launched a full-scale assault against humanity and forced the Asterian Empire to activate the Crownstar at full power, then the death of at least one Demigod could be guaranteed, and very few beings at that level would willingly volunteer themselves for such an outcome.
"And because of this, there hasn’t been another large-scale conflict between humanity and the other races."

Zevan remained impressed whenever he thought about it, because without the Crownstar, he could easily imagine how much pressure humanity might have faced from races possessing genuine Demigods, especially after remembering what had happened to the previous Human Emperor and the desperate measures he had taken in hopes of producing a Demigod for humanity.
"Whatever, that history has nothing to do with tonight."

He turned away from the distant Crownstar and continued toward the Common District, where most ordinary residents lived and where markets, taverns, workshops, inns, and many other smaller businesses remained active even this late into the night.

Unlike the Common District, many parts of Arvelon couldn’t simply be entered by anyone who wished to wander through them, because the imperial capital was divided according to function, authority, and social status.

The major sections included the **Imperial Crown District, Noble Crown District, War District, Arcane District, Grand Mercantile District, Adventurer District, Holy District, Academy District, Artisan District, Common Districts, Outer City, and the hidden Undercity**, with each section serving a different role within the enormous capital.
That division was another reason the clones had chosen the Common District and the Undercity as the foundation for their early operations.

The Common District connected directly to the Underground City, allowing people, information, and goods to move between the legal and illegal sides of Arvelon without requiring constant passage through heavily restricted areas, while the Underground City itself was surprisingly safe from complete destruction despite everything happening inside it.
Not because the imperial authorities were unaware of its existence.
Quite the opposite.

From what Zevan had learned, several noble families secretly benefited from the Underground City, and there were even persistent rumors that members of the Imperial Family held shares in certain businesses operating below the capital.
Whether those rumors were true or merely another layer of misinformation didn’t particularly interest him.
For Zevan, what mattered was establishing the organization, training loyal members, and building an information network strong enough to become useful to Luke in the future.

He eventually crossed one of the Common District’s busy marketplaces, where wagons continued rolling between rows of shops despite the late hour, adventurers gathered around food stalls after returning from quests, and travelers from numerous regions moved through the streets.

Humans formed the majority, but they were far from the only race present, because elves, demi-humans, beastkin, and several other races could be seen walking through the imperial capital without causing any particular disturbance.
"Finally, I’m here.
Zevan released a relieved breath upon reaching the tavern they had agreed to meet in, because he had half expected the other two clones to leave every arrangement to him again.
However, when he looked upward toward the fifth floor, he immediately spotted two familiar figures near one of the windows.
Warren Skell, the clone controlling The Broken Halo, was there.
Beside him sat Frederic Salter, the clone responsible for The Thirteenth Key, Luke’s merchant organization.
Both were already eating.
The moment they noticed Zevan below, the two casually raised their hands and waved toward him as though they hadn’t done anything wrong.
Zevan stared upward for a moment before annoyance spread across his disguised face.
"This bastard started eating without me again."
He entered the tavern immediately.

The ground floor was crowded with all kinds of customers, while waitresses moved rapidly between packed tables carrying plates, mugs, roasted meat, and bottles of rum as laughter, arguments, and overlapping conversations filled the room.
"Three more rums over here!"
"Coming!"
"Oi, that’s my plate!"
"Then guard your food better!"
Zevan ignored the noise and headed toward the stairs, climbing directly to the fifth floor, where Warren and Frederic had already booked a private room for the three of them.
After fifteen days of establishing their organizations independently, it was finally time for Luke’s three clones to sit together and decide what they were going to do next.

chapters.title: Chapter 345: Each Clone Possesses 99% of Luke’s Power!
paragraphs: After Zevan settled into his seat, the three finally began discussing what they had accomplished since arriving in Arvelon.

"The Prime Archive has already established a small network across the Common District and the Undercity, including street informants, tavern workers, caravan guards, scribes, and several independent brokers," Zevan began, leaning back against his chair as the faint noise from the tavern below reached the private room. "However, most of the information we’re receiving is still local, so the next step is planting people inside the Noble, Adventurer, Mercantile, Academy, and Holy Districts."
"That’s going to be difficult," Warren and Frederic replied almost simultaneously, causing both of them to glance toward one another before Warren continued.

"The Broken Halo has already received several assassination requests involving targets inside those districts, but I declined every one of them because, from what I’ve gathered, even the established assassins operating in Arvelon rarely dare to make a move there."

Frederic nodded in agreement before adding, "The Thirteenth Key has already completed a few small deliveries inside those districts, and I’ve personally seen some of their security arrangements. Guards are hidden almost everywhere, and in several places, I sensed people who were at least A-Rank."
Hearing that, Zevan and Warren both became quiet.

The Thirteenth Key had originally been created so Frederic could sell some of the valuable products generated by Luke’s system, but that plan had barely started because their main body was currently hoarding nearly every accumulated daily charge to improve the quality of whatever rewards he wanted for himself.

As a result, Frederic had been forced to rely on knowledge inherited from Luke’s previous world to establish his business, and one of the first products he introduced was a basic firearm that used black powder to propel its ammunition.
Even that had already begun creating problems.
The merchant groups operating in Arvelon weren’t fools, and several of them had quickly realized that a weapon like this could change certain parts of the market if production expanded.

"Even though firearms are practically useless against higher-ranked people, mortals and lower-ranked cultivators still find them extremely useful," Zevan said, giving a small nod as he remembered the reports passing through the Prime Archive. "Sales have already started increasing, and I’ve even received information that several nobles are trying to obtain the production method."
As he finished speaking, Zevan suddenly laughed.
"Hahaha! Those fools actually believed Frederic was working alone and sent D-Rank assassins after him."
Frederic’s mouth twitched when he heard that because, unfortunately, it was completely true.

If their main body hadn’t specifically instructed them to remain low-profile during the early stages, those assassins wouldn’t have survived long enough to realize their mistake, because each clone currently possessed roughly ninety-nine percent of Luke’s individual capability. They couldn’t reproduce the unpredictable miracles Luke sometimes created on the spot because that required the main consciousness actively controlling everything, but they could still use techniques Luke had already formed and mastered, giving each clone combat power somewhere within the Mid-to-High B-Rank range.

Warren casually lifted his wine glass before saying, "It’s fine for now. If they keep sending people, we can simply erase a few of their assassin bases and make the message clear, as long as none of those organizations are backed by the Imperials."
The moment he mentioned the Imperials, the expressions on all three clones immediately became unpleasant.
During their fourteen days in Arvelon, they had learned enough about the Human Imperial Family to understand that provoking them casually would be idiotic.

The Imperial bloodline itself was frighteningly strong, with even many of its younger members already standing above C-Rank, while the defenses surrounding the Imperial Palace were on an entirely different level. The restricted region around the palace stretched for nearly a hundred kilometers, and nearly every layer of it contained guards, formations, detection methods, or hidden protectors whose true strength the clones still couldn’t properly determine.
"Even after fourteen days, we still haven’t found anything useful regarding Seraphina," Frederic finally said, and the earlier humor inside the room disappeared.
All three released faint sighs.
Before sending them to Arvelon, Luke had given them another important task: discover what had truly happened to Aurielle’s mother, Seraphina, and determine where she had been imprisoned.

Luke had never directly pressed Aurielle for the details, yet every time her mother’s name appeared, he could see the sadness she tried to hide, and because of that, he had quietly decided to investigate the matter himself.

"All we’ve confirmed is that the official records label her as a traitor, while almost nobody outside the Imperial side seems to know anything beyond that," Zevan said, tapping one finger against the table. "Whatever happened was buried extremely well."

All three already suspected that the matter involved something deeper inside the Empire, but suspicion alone was useless when they currently lacked the power and access necessary to force their way into places controlled by the Imperial Family.
Luke understood that better than anyone, which was one of the reasons he had created these hidden organizations in the first place, particularly The Broken Halo.
If direct power couldn’t solve something, then there would eventually be situations where a quieter method was required.
Frederic suddenly turned toward Warren.
"So, how is the plan to kill those viscounts progressing?"

Warren calmly took another sip of wine while Zevan also shifted his attention toward him, because despite developing separate personalities, the three clones had inherited another trait from Luke that hadn’t weakened in the slightest.
They remembered grudges.
While Luke had been away from Blackstone, those ten viscounts had dared to bring their C-Rank forces into his territory, and none of the clones had forgotten it.

"Everything is already prepared," Warren answered after lowering his glass onto the table. "At the moment, none of the Broken Halo’s actual members are above Peak D-Rank, while the strongest forces belonging to those viscounts reach Mid C-Rank."

Zevan and Frederic nodded, because eliminating the viscounts wouldn’t simply mean dealing with the ten nobles themselves; their estates contained Early C-Rank combatants, guards, retainers, and numerous lower-ranked forces that could turn a direct assault into unnecessary trouble.
Warren, however, showed no concern.

"My people have already infiltrated portions of their forces, so I know their movements. Tomorrow, all ten viscounts are scheduled to attend a gathering hosted by a Count who serves under another Marquis."
The moment those words left his mouth, understanding appeared across the other two clones’ faces.
Warren continued without making them ask.
"So instead of wasting time destroying their armies one by one, the three of us will make the move personally and eliminate all ten Mid C-Rank viscounts during the same gathering."
Smiles gradually appeared across Zevan and Frederic’s faces.

If this had happened earlier, when Luke’s foundation was still only at the Bronze Knight level, silently killing ten Mid C-Rank nobles surrounded by guards would have been considerably more troublesome. Now, however, with their Silver-Rank foundation and combat strength reaching into High B-Rank through Luke’s established Titan techniques, none of them considered the viscounts themselves a serious threat.
Frederic leaned back slightly before saying, "Ten human nobles dying at the same gathering is going to create quite a bit of chaos throughout the region."
Zevan looked toward him for a moment before a grin appeared on his face.
"Haha! And what exactly does that have to do with us?"
Warren’s lips curled upward as well, and within moments, laughter filled the private room.
"Hahahaha!"
They truly didn’t care.

Even if sections of the Human Continent eventually descended into war, that alone wouldn’t make them lose sleep, because the people and things Luke considered his own mattered far more to them than some abstract stability belonging to nobles who had already chosen to become his enemies.
"Alright, then we’ll leave now," Frederic eventually said after their laughter subsided.

The three stood from their seats and left the private room together, descending through the tavern before casually walking out into the crowded street outside, where people were still moving between shops and drinking establishments despite the late hour.
However, only moments after they departed—
"AHHHH! MURDER!"
A woman’s shriek suddenly exploded from somewhere above, immediately drawing the attention of several customers and pedestrians near the tavern.
"What happened?!"
"Someone’s dead upstairs!"
A waitress who had gone into the private room to collect the plates had frozen near the doorway, her face pale as she stared toward the ceiling.

Pinned against the roof above her was a man completely dressed in black, his body held there by five small daggers driven through his clothing and flesh, while the only part of his face left uncovered was his pair of wide, lifeless eyes.
There were no signs that he had fought back.
Whatever had killed him had happened so quickly that he seemed to have died without even understanding what had occurred.
Beside the corpse, several words had been written across the ceiling in blood.
Petty tricks.
By the time frightened voices began spreading through the tavern, Zevan, Warren, and Frederic had already moved farther down the street.
Frederic glanced toward Zevan while continuing to walk.
"Which organization did that man belong to?"
Even though Warren had been the one who killed the assassin, Zevan was naturally the one who possessed the relevant information.
"The same organization that’s been targeting you."
Frederic gave a faint nod and immediately lost interest in the subject, because that group was hardly the only organization that currently wanted him dead.
Ever since the firearm business began expanding, several different groups had quietly placed bounties on his head.
A few breaths later, the three clones entered a particularly crowded section of the street, where merchants, adventurers, laborers, and late-night travelers continuously crossed one another’s paths.
Then, without attracting a single unusual glance from anyone nearby, all three disappeared among the moving crowd.
