Even if sections of the Human Continent eventually descended into war, that alone wouldn’t make them lose sleep, because the people and things Luke considered his own mattered far more to them than some abstract stability belonging to nobles who had already chosen to become his enemies.
"Alright, then we’ll leave now," Frederic eventually said after their laughter subsided.

The three stood from their seats and left the private room together, descending through the tavern before casually walking out into the crowded street outside, where people were still moving between shops and drinking establishments despite the late hour.
However, only moments after they departed—
"AHHHH!
MURDER!"
A woman’s shriek suddenly exploded from somewhere above, immediately drawing the attention of several customers and pedestrians near the tavern.
"What happened?!"
"Someone’s dead upstairs!"
A waitress who had gone into the private room to collect the plates had frozen near the doorway, her face pale as she stared toward the ceiling.

Pinned against the roof above her was a man completely dressed in black, his body held there by five small daggers driven through his clothing and flesh, while the only part of his face left uncovered was his pair of wide, lifeless eyes.
There were no signs that he had fought back.
Whatever had killed him had happened so quickly that he seemed to have died without even understanding what had occurred.
Beside the corpse, several words had been written across the ceiling in blood.
Petty tricks.
By the time frightened voices began spreading through the tavern, Zevan, Warren, and Frederic had already moved farther down the street.
Frederic glanced toward Zevan while continuing to walk.
"Which organization did that man belong to?"
Even though Warren had been the one who killed the assassin, Zevan was naturally the one who possessed the relevant information.
"The same organization that’s been targeting you."
Frederic gave a faint nod and immediately lost interest in the subject, because that group was hardly the only organization that currently wanted him dead.
Ever since the firearm business began expanding, several different groups had quietly placed bounties on his head.
A few breaths later, the three clones entered a particularly crowded section of the street, where merchants, adventurers, laborers, and late-night travelers continuously crossed one another’s paths.
Then, without attracting a single unusual glance from anyone nearby, all three disappeared among the moving crowd.

chapters.title: Chapter 346: She had finally come to claim what belonged to her: Her Husband.
paragraphs: 20th day of Fructus, Year 50,001.
"Haa... the weather is really nice today."

Luke—or more precisely, the clone he had left behind in the Blackstone Highlands—leaned comfortably against a chair beside the mages' residence, enjoying what had become a rare day without any urgent work demanding his attention.

A calm breeze drifted across the nearby lake, carrying cool air over the grassy shore while faint ripples spread across the clear surface, and Luke had dressed accordingly, wearing an open shirt with nothing underneath and a pair of shorts while relaxing beneath the warm light.
Not far away, Aurielle was swimming through the lake.
More importantly, she was wearing a purple bikini.

Luke had been the one to introduce the idea to her, explaining that people from his previous world commonly wore this kind of clothing while swimming, and with the magical clothes he had previously given her, changing the outfit into something similar had hardly taken any effort.
Luke lowered his sunglasses slightly while watching her move through the water.
"My Aurielle is definitely the best."
His gaze followed his wife with open appreciation as she swam farther across the lake, though before he could continue enjoying the peaceful scenery, a familiar voice suddenly came from behind.
"Master!"
Luke had already heard that voice enough times to know exactly what would happen next.
THUD!

Aurora threw herself at him from behind and wrapped both arms tightly around his body, turning what should have been an ordinary hug into something closer to a body slam, while the chair beneath them immediately cracked before collapsing under the impact.

Luke barely reacted to the destroyed chair and instinctively raised one hand, preparing to rub her head as he usually did whenever Aurora clung to him, but this time something felt noticeably different.
'Hmm? Why does her hug feel softer than usual?'
Curious, Luke removed the sunglasses from his face and turned slightly, only to find Aurora's smiling face already so close to his that she could have kissed him simply by leaning forward a little.

He ignored that part because Aurora had always liked pressing herself against him as though she wanted to completely melt into his embrace, and instead slowly lowered his gaze from her face toward her neck.
'Okay... nothing strange so far.'
His gaze moved slightly lower.
Luke swallowed.
'Damn it, is she trying to kill me openly?!'

Because, down there he could see Aurora's cleavage clearly and Aurora was wearing a white bikini, and with almost her entire upper body pressed directly against his chest, Luke had a very clear view that he absolutely hadn't been prepared for.
'Where did she even learn about this outfit? I'm sure I only told Aurielle.'
Before he could think any further, another softer voice came from beside them.
"Master..."
Luke turned toward the source and immediately froze again.

Vaelira stood a short distance away wearing a blue bikini, one hand holding her opposite elbow while her posture remained unusually stiff with embarrassment. Even with the blue mask still covering part of her face, her nervousness was obvious, because every time her gaze met Luke's, she quickly lowered it again as though regretting the decision to appear before him like this.
'Damn... even Vaelira is wearing one.
The blue bikini suited her far too well, and combined with her already striking figure, Luke had to admit that the usually composed woman looked dangerously attractive at that moment.

Earlier, he had given all of them magical clothing because they enjoyed the convenient ability to change outfits whenever needed, but he certainly hadn't expected them to copy Aurielle's newly introduced swimming attire this quickly.
Then another voice came from the opposite side.
"Master, how do I look?"
Luke turned again and nearly cursed aloud.

Theia had also appeared nearby, this time wearing a green bikini that contrasted sharply with her long purple hair and green eyes. Unlike Vaelira, she wasn't openly hiding her body or lowering her gaze, yet the faint stiffness in her posture and the almost unnoticeable trembling of her fingers made it clear that she was nowhere near as calm as she was pretending to be.
'This damn main body left me behind to deal with all of this.'

For a brief moment, the clone seriously considered directly connecting with Luke's main consciousness and dumping the entire situation onto him, because dealing with one beautiful woman in a bikini was manageable, while suddenly being surrounded by four of them felt far beyond what his poor subconscious portion of Luke's brain had been prepared to handle.
Unfortunately, before he could make that decision, a sweet voice carrying an unmistakably cold edge drifted over from the lake.
"Darling~ As a Lord, shouldn't you maintain a little more distance from your subjects?"
Luke immediately looked toward Aurielle with an aggrieved expression.
Aurielle, however, wasn't looking at him.

Her attention was fixed entirely on Aurora, who was still happily wrapped around Luke while pressing herself against his chest without even realizing why Aurielle's expression had become increasingly dangerous.
'He certainly looks like he's enjoying himself.'
Aurielle clenched her teeth slightly while moving closer to the shore.

When Luke first told her about bikinis, she had secretly thought that wearing something like this might help capture even more of his attention, and she had looked forward to spending a peaceful day swimming with him while enjoying some time alone.
Instead, the three women who had barely left Luke alone since his return had somehow copied the exact idea and followed them here as well.
'Why can't I spend even one peaceful day alone with him?'
Aurielle cursed her luck inwardly.

After spending so much time together, she had grown considerably closer to Aurora, Vaelira, and Theia, and she no longer disliked their presence the way she might have earlier, but whenever Luke became involved, that possessive feeling still surfaced before she could stop it.
Some part of her wanted him entirely to herself, without Aurora hanging from his neck, without the others surrounding him, and sometimes even without his other wives appearing between them.
As for why that feeling had been growing stronger recently, even Aurielle herself couldn't properly explain it.
Luke, meanwhile, looked from Aurielle to Aurora, then toward Vaelira and Theia, and immediately reached the only sensible conclusion available.
Escape.
"All of you, I suddenly remembered something important that I need to take care of, so I'll be leaving first."
Aurora blinked in confusion, but before she could tighten her embrace again, Luke slipped out of her arms and moved several steps away.

Her hugs might have looked harmless, but Aurora had never properly understood how much strength she used when clinging to him, and if Luke's current body hadn't already reached the Silver-Rank foundation, an ordinary man probably would have had several bones crushed long ago.
Silver-black energy immediately gathered around Luke as Valzareth materialized over his body, and before any of the four women could stop him, space distorted around his figure.
WHOOSH!
Luke disappeared.
The four women remained near the lake, staring at the empty place where he had been sitting only moments earlier.
Far away from them, Luke reappeared and released a relieved breath, believing he had successfully escaped the growing disaster.
Unfortunately, his enhanced senses were still far too good.
Aurora's confused voice carried faintly across the distance.
"Ahh... why didn't Master let me hug him longer? Even though that poking thing down there was a little annoying."
Luke's entire body stiffened.
Back beside the lake, silence descended.
Aurielle slowly turned toward Aurora.
Theia also looked at her.
Vaelira remained frozen where she stood, clearly wishing she could somehow disappear before the situation became worse.
Aurora merely looked between them with the same innocent expression as before, completely unaware that Aurielle's and Theia's faces had darkened considerably after hearing her words.
Far away—
"It's over!"
Luke grabbed his head in despair.
None of this was his fault.

Aurora had suddenly appeared in a bikini and pressed her entire body against him, so naturally his body had reacted slightly on its own, and there wasn't exactly much he could have done about that while she refused to stop hugging him.
"I need to disappear for a few days."
The decision came almost instantly.

Without wasting any more time, Luke activated the connection to the Time Chamber and vanished from inside it, deciding that escaping Blackstone entirely was currently much safer than returning anywhere near that lake.
Besides, the actual Luke was already on his way back and had crossed roughly half the remaining distance.
'The main body's almost here anyway, so this can become his headache.'
With that extremely irresponsible thought, the clone escaped the calamity he had personally created.
Unfortunately for the approaching main body, the bikini incident was far from the only problem waiting for him in Blackstone.
High above the territory, an uninvited visitor floated silently in the sky while looking down at the buildings, roads, and people spread throughout the Blackstone Highlands.
Two black dragon horns curved upward from her head, while brilliant golden draconic eyes calmly examined the territory beneath her before a faint smile appeared on her face.
"So... this is where the cutie has been living?"
The woman continued floating above Blackstone, completely unaware that the Luke currently returning home had no idea she was already waiting for him.
After all, she had finally come to claim what belonged to her.
Her husband.

chapters.title: Chapter 347: Selene Refuses to Let Luke Leave?!
paragraphs: Meanwhile, Luke was flying through the sky in his winged Titan form, his destination being none other than the Blackstone Highlands, his own territory, while the powerful beats of his enormous wings carried him steadily across the vast distance.

"Sigh, escaping from Selene wasn't easy." Luke breathed out in relief as the wind rushed past him, because even after spending fifteen continuous days together, Selene had still been unwilling to separate from him and had repeatedly tried to convince him to accompany her back to Empyrean Academy.

"Even though I want to spend more time with her, this isn't the time for that." He clicked his tongue in annoyance, although he knew there was nothing he could do about it right now, since both his personal strength and the development of his territory required his attention.

After all, ever since arriving in this world, Luke had never forgotten about the demons rampaging across it, and if the situation eventually became worse, relying entirely on other kingdoms or organizations was never going to be enough.
He needed his own army, and more importantly, he wanted that army to consist of elites capable of standing against powerful enemies without collapsing the moment he wasn't around.

That was also one of the reasons why Luke had never complained whenever the system gave him summon-type units, since every powerful summon increased the overall strength of Blackstone, with Aurora, Vaelira, Theia, and the other elite units already proving just how valuable such rewards could become.
"Even though all of them somehow end up being women who want my love, thanks to some horny system."
Luke clicked his tongue again, expecting the system to immediately appear and defend its dignity like it usually did, yet several seconds passed without so much as a single response.
"Whatever."

Ignoring the suspicious silence, Luke recalled Selene's expression when she had finally left for Empyrean Academy, and rather than sadness, what he remembered most clearly was the unwillingness written across her face, as though she would have happily dragged him along if he had given her even the slightest opportunity.

"Soon," Luke muttered as his hand slowly tightened into a fist, because sooner or later, he intended to bring all of his wives together so he could spend time with every one of them without constantly traveling from one place to another.
Of course, whether they could actually remain together without eventually trying to kill each other was an entirely different problem, and one Luke preferred not to think about too deeply right now.
Instead, he shifted his attention toward something much more practical and began calculating his accumulated Daily Return Charges and available Monthly Claims.
Current System Status — 20th Day of Fructus, Year 50,001
Daily Return Charges
Aurielle Valmont: 1 Charge — 1,000× Return
Selene Nightveil: 15 Charges — 15,000× Return
Wife Monthly Claims
Aurielle Valmont: 1 Monthly Claim Available
Selene Nightveil: 1 Monthly Claim Available
Total Wife Monthly Claims: 2
Lover Monthly Claim
Theia Yvette: 1 Monthly Claim Available
Total Monthly Claims Available: 3
— 2 Wife Monthly Claims
— 1 Lover Monthly Claim

"Sigh, sadly, the system won't generate Daily Return Charges while my clones stay with my wives." Recalling that restriction still made Luke feel somewhat regretful, because otherwise he could have simply left one clone with each of them and accumulated charges without ever worrying about being physically present himself.

Still, the situation wasn't entirely bad, because Aurielle's Monthly Claim had generated even though his original body hadn't been staying with her, which confirmed that Monthly Claims were independent of the restriction placed upon Daily Return Charges.
"At least I don't have to personally stay with every wife after reaching their second milestone just to receive the Monthly Claims."
That alone made things considerably easier for him, especially when the number of people and territories demanding his attention continued to increase.

With that thought settled, Luke spread his wings wider before driving them downward with greater force, causing the air beneath them to surge as his speed increased and the distant landscape began passing beneath him even faster.
He wanted to reach Blackstone as soon as possible.

Around the same time, one of Luke's clones was walking through the increasingly crowded streets of Blackstone, his face fully concealed beneath ordinary clothing so that none of the passing citizens, merchants, or adventurers could recognize their lord casually moving among them.

The road itself was far busier than it had been several weeks earlier, with loaded wagons rolling between shops, merchants calling toward potential customers from newly constructed buildings, and groups of workers moving materials toward the expanding sections of the territory.
While passing through one particularly busy stretch of road, Luke's clone heard two men talking nearby.
"Hey, did you hear about those ten viscounts? Every one of them was supposedly a Mid-C Rank, yet they disappeared while traveling to attend a Marquis's party."
The second man immediately lowered his voice, although his curiosity clearly outweighed whatever caution he possessed.
"Yeah, I heard about it. Apparently, they couldn't even find a bloodstain, and there weren't any guards around the damaged carriage either. The viscounts simply disappeared."
Hearing those words, a faint smile appeared beneath the cloth covering Luke's face, because he could already make a fairly good guess about who had been responsible.
'Looks like one of the other clones already dealt with them.'

Although Luke's clones could remain at practically unlimited distances from the original body now, the clones themselves couldn't freely exchange information with one another across such distances, while the original body remained the central point capable of retrieving and focusing on the information gathered by them.
'At least I don't have to worry about those guys pestering my territory anymore.'

With another potential problem removed, Luke continued along the road, yet his attention soon shifted away from the surrounding conversations and toward Blackstone itself, and seeing how much the territory had changed during these twenty days brought a genuine sense of pride.

The original developed area of Blackstone had covered only around one kilometer, but it had now expanded to nearly ten kilometers, with most of the newly claimed and developed land extending toward the Stormhowl Mountains, where construction crews and newly settled residents continued pushing the territory outward.

More importantly, this expansion had happened without Luke needing to invade another human noble's land, which meant Blackstone had been able to grow rapidly without immediately becoming tangled in another round of political disputes.
"Plus, the border issue is finally resolved."

The remaining demi-human tribes near Blackstone's border had submitted and become part of the Blackstone Highlands, removing one of the territory's long-standing concerns while also allowing the forces stationed there to finally return.
Among those returning forces were the Berserker Greatswordsmen, along with Taron, the original Silver Knight who had spent so much time protecting the distant border.

Although Blackstone now possessed several individuals far stronger than Taron, Luke had no intention of mistreating or sidelining him simply because the territory had grown stronger, especially when Taron had protected Blackstone and supported Aurielle during the period when Luke himself had been unable to remain there.
For that reason, Luke had left Taron as one of the primary commanders responsible for the army, while the issue of his cultivation speed was something Luke was already considering separately.
"Sigh, the Mana Well inside the Time Chamber is starting to lose its effectiveness for Silver Knights and anyone above them."

chapters.title: Chapter 348: “Aurielle, Where Is Luke?”
paragraphs: That problem had become increasingly obvious as Blackstone's stronger fighters continued advancing, since resources that had once produced rapid improvement at the lower realms could no longer provide the same results once someone stepped into Silver and especially Golden.

Luke therefore needed to find other methods, whether through future system rewards, stronger cultivation resources, or simply using the rapidly improving economy of Blackstone to purchase whatever the territory required.
Fortunately, the economic side was no longer as miserable as it had once been.

With more merchants arriving, the population increasing, trade routes becoming busier, and Blackstone itself producing more goods, the territory's wealth had risen sharply and was gradually approaching the million gold coins Luke had possessed near the beginning.
Remembering that brought another matter to mind, and Luke's clone quietly reviewed the progress made by Blackstone's fighters during the latest period of training.
Blackstone Highlands — Current Power Progress
Knights
Aurora — Mid-Golden Knight → Approaching Late-Golden Knight
Vaelira — Mid-Golden Knight → Late-Golden Knight
Aurielle — Early Golden Knight → Mid-Golden Knight
Peter Bassus — Early Golden Knight → Approaching Mid-Golden Knight
10 Blackstone Legion Knights — 6th Stage Silver → 8th Stage Silver
Osric Thornfield — 6th Stage Silver → 8th Stage Silver
Taron — Silver Knight → Silver Knight
10 Berserker Greatswordsmen — Early Silver → Early Silver
120 Territory Guards / Archers — Peak Bronze → Early Silver Knight
6,030 Soldiers — Early Bronze → Mid-Bronze Knight
10,100 Soldiers — Peak Iron → Mid-Bronze Knight
20,000 New Recruits — Body Temper → Peak Iron Knight
Mages
Elena Whitmore — Circle Mage → Early Rune Mage
(5th Mage Realm, equivalent to Golden Knight / C-Rank)
9 Elemental Mages — Circle Mage → Peak Multi-Circle Mage
(4th Mage Realm / D-Rank)
Lucy Dawnvale — Apprentice Mage → Peak Multi-Circle Mage
Theia Yvette — Arcane Core Mage → Arcane Core Mage, fully recovered
Current Major Army Groups
Early Silver Knights — 120
Mid-Bronze Knights — 16,130
Peak Iron Knights — 20,000
Windmarch Reach forces are not included in this progress report.

"Well, it's still good that they managed to rank up this much." Luke's clone gave a small nod as he recalled the amount of resources that had gone into achieving such progress, especially the Aether Crystals produced during this period, nearly all of which had been consumed to push so many soldiers forward at once.

Even with those resources, several soldiers had still failed to reach the next realm, although Luke wasn't particularly disappointed, since advancing an army of this size was never going to happen perfectly in a single training period.

As for the forces stationed in Windmarch Reach, their situation was different, because they were still responsible for guarding the conquered territory while continuously expanding Blackstone's influence there, leaving them with far less time and resources for cultivation, which had caused their realms to remain mostly stagnant for now.
"I'll do something about that later."

While thinking about future cultivation resources, Luke remembered another matter he had handled during this period, which was helping Lucy's family by giving them enough gold to stabilize their situation and clearing the debts that had been hanging over them.
That had naturally brought Lucy even closer to him and Blackstone, although despite all of her recent progress, the mysterious physique within her still hadn't awakened.

Luke was considering that problem as he passed beside a narrow alley between two newly constructed buildings, when without the slightest warning, an overwhelming pressure descended across the entire Blackstone Highlands.
HUMMMMMMM!

Luke's clone stopped immediately as the air around him seemed to grow several times heavier, while throughout the surrounding street, conversations, footsteps, and the rattling of merchant carts abruptly collapsed into confusion.
"What?! What happened?!"

People barely had time to shout before the pressure intensified, forcing ordinary adventurers, guards, merchants, and citizens toward the ground, while many mortals lost consciousness almost instantly and collapsed where they stood.

Anyone below D-Rank found it nearly impossible to remain standing, and across Blackstone, every powerful individual who could still resist the pressure immediately became alert, from the managers of the major guild branches to the higher-ranked beings residing within the territory.
Luke's clone remained standing beneath the crushing pressure, although his expression became serious as he raised his head and tried to determine where it was coming from.
Before anyone could locate the source, however, a cold female voice descended from somewhere high above the city.
"Aurielle, where is Luke?"

Despite the pressure holding many people against the ground, almost everyone who remained conscious instinctively turned their gaze upward, and the moment they saw the figure floating above Blackstone, shock spread across the streets.

A woman hovered calmly in the sky, her long crimson hair moving behind her with the wind, while two black dragon horns curved upward from her head and brilliant golden draconic eyes looked down upon the territory beneath her.
"That's a dragon!"

The frightened shout immediately spread through the surrounding crowd, because even though the woman hadn't transformed into her true draconic form, the horns, golden eyes, and oppressive draconic pressure made her identity impossible to mistake.

Before the alliance between the races, most ordinary humans would never have known enough about dragons to recognize one in humanoid form, but after the alliance had been established and information regarding the Dragon Race had spread throughout the continent, their most distinctive traits had become widely known.
More importantly, there was no mistaking the pressure surrounding her.
It was unmistakably draconic.

Inside the Time Chamber, Aurielle and several others had still been training when hurried footsteps suddenly approached from the distance, followed by Noah rushing toward her with obvious panic on his face.
"My Lady! A-A dragon has appeared in the territory!"
Aurielle lowered the sword in her hand, but before she could respond, Noah hurriedly added the part that immediately changed her expression.
"It's a dragon woman, and she's asking for Lord Luke!"
The training area fell silent for a moment as Aurielle's gaze sharpened, and after only a brief pause, one particular name escaped her lips.
"Rhaenyra Crimsonscale..."
There was no uncertainty in her voice, only an unmistakable coldness as she slowly tightened her grip around the sword.
"Why is she here?"
The answer seemed obvious enough, and that realization only worsened Aurielle's mood.
"For Luke? Heh... she doesn't even love Luke, nor does she have any real feelings for him."
Her voice remained quiet, but Noah clearly had no intention of remaining anywhere nearby while his lady was speaking in that tone.
Aurielle noticed his nervousness and waved one hand toward him.
"Go. I'll handle this."
"Yes, My Lady."

Noah nodded quickly before turning around and leaving, although the fear on his face didn't disappear, because dragons had remained little more than mythical creatures to most humans for generations, living almost entirely within their own continent before the Demon War forced the races into an alliance.

Before that alliance, ordinary people from other races could spend their entire lives without ever seeing a dragon, yet once the war began, the Dragon Race had become one of the leading forces attacking the demons, and the results had quickly turned into stories repeated across the continents.

There were tales of individual dragons burning through entire demonic armies, and although demons had continued attacking the territories of other races afterward, almost none willingly brought the war directly into dragon lands again.
Aurielle watched Noah disappear before calmly raising one hand.
"Eclipse Queen Regalia."

chapters.title: Chapter 349: Not Even a Goddess Can Take Luke From Aurielle!
paragraphs: Darkness immediately gathered around her body as black-violet armor formed piece by piece, covering her from shoulders to feet while silver-edged plates locked into place and violet runes moved faintly across their surface.

The crown-shaped headpiece settled above her head as the lower armored layers spread around her waist like a royal battle skirt, while a dark cloak formed behind her and shifted gently beneath the surrounding currents of energy.
Once the armor had completely manifested, Aurielle summoned the purple blade inherited from her mother and wrapped her fingers tightly around its hilt.
“Luke is mine, and no one is taking him away from me, not even a goddess herself.”
The instant those words left her mouth, something within Aurielle reacted.
For the briefest moment, one of her eyes became filled with complete darkness while the other shone with brilliant light, and at the same time, a faint Twilight mark appeared between her eyebrows.
It lasted for less than a heartbeat.

The mark had barely formed before an unseen force erased it completely, suppressing whatever power had attempted to emerge as though Valtharion itself refused to allow it to manifest freely within the world.

Had the System been present to witness it, it probably would have complained once again about Valtharion’s pettiness toward powers originating beyond its control, because among everything Luke had encountered so far, Valtharion seemed especially wary of foreign power.
Aurielle didn’t waste time questioning what had happened, because her attention was already fixed on the woman waiting outside.

Darkness gathered behind her back before spreading outward into the black-violet form of the Regalia’s Eclipse Wings, and with a powerful flap, Aurielle rose from the ground before flying toward the Time Chamber’s exit.
Elsewhere inside the chamber, Theia, Aurora, and Vaelira had also heard Noah’s warning, and although each reacted differently, the same thought passed through their minds almost simultaneously.
Someone had entered their master’s territory with hostile intent while openly searching for him.
None of them intended to ignore that.
Aurora immediately prepared herself for battle, Vaelira took up her bow, while Theia rose and gathered her recovered mana around herself before following the others toward the exit.

The warning spread quickly throughout the Time Chamber after that, passing from one training ground to another until Luke’s soldiers and summons understood that an unknown dragon had appeared above Blackstone while demanding to see their lord.
Armor was fastened, weapons were taken from their racks, and formations began assembling without anyone needing to repeat the order twice.
Soon, one unit after another began marching toward the exit.

What happened afterward would eventually spread far beyond Blackstone, because this became the day outsiders finally realized just how much military strength the Hero of Light had gathered within barely two months.
More than a hundred Silver Knights and thousands upon thousands of Bronze Knights were about to appear before the public at once.
Outside, Blackstone had fallen into near-total silence.

Those capable of remaining conscious continued staring toward the dragon woman floating above the territory, while those strong enough to stand kept their weapons close without daring to make the first move.
Everyone was waiting for Lord Luke to appear and deal with the situation, because one thought had already begun spreading through the frightened crowd.
If this dragon became angry enough to reveal her true form and attack the city, the damage to Blackstone could become catastrophic.
Surprisingly, almost no one recognized the woman as one of Luke’s wives.

Rhaenyra Crimsonscale rarely displayed herself publicly outside the Dragon Continent, and while some people had heard that the Hero of Light had married a Dragon Princess, very few had ever seen her face closely enough to connect the woman floating above them with that title.
Before Luke could appear, however, another sound began spreading through the territory.
THUMP! THUMP! THUMP!
The synchronized footsteps grew steadily louder as people turned toward the direction of the Lord’s Estate, and soon their already frightened expressions began changing into disbelief.

Rows of armored soldiers were emerging in disciplined formation, their weapons already drawn as one group after another filled the road, while the sound of metal boots striking the ground rolled through the surrounding streets.
The pressure from the dragon still hung over Blackstone, yet none of the approaching soldiers stopped.

Silver Knights marched among the forward formations, while behind them came line after line of Bronze Knights whose numbers continued growing until the road itself seemed filled with Blackstone’s forces.

The surrounding adventurers and merchants stared in disbelief, while several guild members who had believed they possessed a reasonable understanding of Blackstone’s military strength suddenly realized how incomplete their information had been.
One adventurer finally broke the stunned silence.
“What the fuck?! Since when did Blackstone have this many soldiers?”
No one answered him, because most of the people nearby were wondering the exact same thing.

The number of Silver and Bronze Knights marching out from Luke’s territory no longer resembled the military strength expected from an ordinary Barony, and as formation after formation continued appearing, more than one experienced observer began comparing what they were seeing to the forces normally controlled by a Count.

Before the onlookers could recover from the sight of Blackstone’s hidden army, another movement from the direction of the Lord’s Estate immediately drew their attention, because five figures emerged from behind the marching soldiers, and aside from Luke himself, they had already become some of the most recognizable people within the entire territory.

Aurielle appeared first, rising above the formations with the black-violet Eclipse Wings spreading from behind her armor, while beside her came Elena, whose large white angelic wings were fully manifested as she flew through the air with a faint golden radiance surrounding her feathers.

The third figure was Theia, the B-Rank powerhouse whose existence had already become known among Blackstone’s higher-ranking residents, although unlike Aurielle and Elena, there were no wings behind her back as she slowly rose into the air.
Instead, faint Arcane energy gathered beneath and around her body, allowing her to remain suspended as though the air itself were holding her up.

She was using an Arcane-Grade flight spell, one of the many utility spells available to sufficiently advanced mages, and because there were no visible wings or obvious physical movements involved, her flight looked closer to effortless floating.
Behind the three flying women came Aurora and Vaelira, both walking forward among the armored soldiers with unusually cold expressions as they looked toward the dragon floating above Blackstone.

That alone surprised several people watching from the nearby streets, because while Vaelira’s quiet and reserved nature made such an expression unsurprising, Aurora was almost always seen smiling brightly whenever she moved through Blackstone.
Seeing that familiar smile completely absent caused more than one person to realize just how seriously Luke’s people were treating the current situation.
However, the moment Blackstone’s forces fully emerged from the estate grounds, Rhaenyra’s draconic pressure descended upon them as well.
HUMMMMMMM!

The air seemed to thicken around the formations as the invisible weight pressed down upon every soldier, causing those below D-Rank to freeze where they stood while many struggled even to properly breathe, and the D-Rank fighters themselves were forced to circulate their strength just to remain upright.
Only those at C-Rank and above could continue moving with relative freedom, although even they could clearly feel the oppressive presence surrounding the dragon woman above them.
Several soldiers clenched their weapons harder while others instinctively lowered their stances, yet none broke formation despite the pressure weighing against their bodies.

chapters.title: Chapter 350: Luke Corrupted Aurielle’s Language?!
paragraphs: Aurielle paid almost no attention to the situation behind her.

With another flap of her Eclipse Wings, she accelerated directly toward Rhaenyra, while Elena and Theia followed through the air and Aurora and Vaelira positioned themselves beneath and slightly behind her, leaving the five women facing the Dragon Princess together.
Meanwhile, the person responsible for this entire situation was doing something considerably less impressive.
Luke’s clone was hiding behind the corner of a building several streets away, carefully leaning his head past the stone wall while watching everything unfolding above.
More strangely, he wasn’t peeking alone.

If the System possessed a visible spirit body that ordinary people could actually see, they would have witnessed an extremely questionable scene of one grown man and one small spirit-like existence leaning around the same corner while secretly watching the confrontation.
Luke’s clone suddenly paused.
‘System?’
He slowly turned his head toward the familiar presence beside him before staring with obvious confusion.
“Wait, why are you here? Weren’t you with the main body?”

The question was reasonable, because Luke’s clones couldn’t actually use the System themselves, while only the original Luke possessed proper access to it, which meant the System normally spent nearly all of its time accompanying the main body.
Seeing it voluntarily appear beside a clone was definitely new.
The System remained suspiciously silent.
Luke’s clone stared at it for another moment before his expression gradually changed with realization.
“Let me guess.”
He leaned slightly closer while keeping his voice low enough that no one nearby could hear them.
“The main body is flying back alone right now, which means there isn’t a single woman, princess, queen, lover, or wife anywhere near him.”
“But here, there are two wives, a lover, and several other women standing around while they’re about to start fighting over him.”
The System still didn’t answer.
Luke’s clone pointed an accusing finger toward it.
“So you abandoned the main body and came here because you wanted to watch the fun.”
He paused before adding with complete certainty, “Am I right, you horny System?”

Luke’s accusation was uncomfortably close to the truth, but the System had long since achieved something resembling a PhD in shamelessness, so expecting it to admit anything was clearly asking too much.
[The System chooses its right to remain silent. ( ̄ー ̄)]
Luke’s clone stared at the message for several seconds, temporarily unable to think of anything capable of matching that level of shamelessness.
Before he could respond, however, the System spoke again as though the previous accusation had never happened.
[Luke, why are you hiding here?]
[Your wife traveled all this way just to meet you, so shouldn’t you go out there and welcome her properly? After all, she probably came because she missed you!]
A small pause followed.
[Maybe...]
“Maybe?”
Luke’s mouth twitched as he looked back toward the sky.
“She definitely didn’t come here because she missed me.”
The System remained quiet while Luke continued with obvious suspicion.
“Did you forget the sixth chap—Ahem! I mean, the second day after I arrived here, when she subdued me without any effort and carried me away like a sack of potatoes?”
[Luke, that happened in the past, and besides, look above.]
[Even Aurielle is welcoming Rhaenyra with a lovely smile.]
Luke hesitated before cautiously leaning farther around the corner and looking toward the sky.
Above Blackstone, Aurielle had already flown close enough to stop directly across from Rhaenyra, although there wasn’t even the faintest trace of the “lovely smile” the System had just described.
Her expression was completely cold.
Then Aurielle spoke.
“Fuck off, Rhaenyra! You are not welcome here!”
For several heartbeats, an unbelievable silence covered the surrounding streets.

Even many of the people still being suppressed by Rhaenyra’s draconic pressure forgot their discomfort for a moment as they stared upward, because none of them had expected the usually dignified former princess and current Baroness of Blackstone to greet a Dragon Princess with those words.
Luke’s clone slowly pulled his head back behind the wall.
The System remained silent for another second before immediately turning its anger toward him.
[YOU taught her that language!]
[I told you to make a healthy yandere, not a bitch!]
Luke opened his mouth, but nothing useful came out.

He couldn’t exactly defend himself either, because he knew perfectly well that the main body had become considerably rougher and less restrained around Aurielle after their relationship deepened, although even he hadn’t expected the consequences to appear in quite this form.
With a resigned expression, Luke looked toward the nearby road and quietly muttered, “Should I run away before this poor clone gets sacrificed for something the main body did?”
Before he could take even one step, however, the System released a suspiciously pitying sigh.
[Sigh, Luke, it’s already too late.]
[You should probably forget about this clone.]
Luke froze.
“What do you mean by that?”
At the same moment, high above Blackstone, Rhaenyra’s mouth twitched after hearing Aurielle’s greeting, because even she hadn’t expected those words to come from the former Human Princess.
‘What happened to her?’
As she hadn’t behaved quite like this during their earlier meetings.
Rhaenyra considered it briefly before simply dismissing the matter.
‘Whatever. I only need to take him and leave.’
She suppressed the irritation building inside her, because losing her temper against the people below would be pointless when most of them were far too weak to be considered meaningful opponents.
To Rhaenyra, becoming genuinely angry at them would be no different from stopping to fight ants simply because they happened to cross her path.
Instead of replying to Aurielle immediately, she shifted her golden draconic gaze downward toward the city.
Almost at the same moment, Aurielle did the same.
Luke’s clone, still hidden behind the building, suddenly heard the System continue its earlier explanation.
[Because your wives can sense the Golden Chains connected to you.]
[And since this clone is currently close enough to them, Aurielle and Rhaenyra can already tell where you are.]
Luke became completely silent.
Then he slowly leaned away from the wall.
“Wait...”
Before he could finish, the uncomfortable sensation of being watched suddenly crawled across his back.
Two gazes had landed directly upon his hiding place.
Luke’s clone stiffened before slowly looking upward, where Aurielle was staring toward the building with an expression that told him very clearly that hiding had already become pointless.
Rhaenyra was looking in the same direction.
For one brief moment, Luke still hoped the wall might somehow help.
Then Rhaenyra’s golden draconic eyes suddenly brightened.
A faint golden radiance passed through her pupils as her gaze seemed to pierce straight through the building, and the instant Luke noticed that change, a terrible premonition rose in his heart.
He remembered something he had once heard about the Dragon Race.
‘Dragon Eyes...’
Among the many rumors surrounding dragons, there was one particular saying that had remained in his memory.
Dragon Eyes could peer through things that even Sage Eyes failed to perceive.
Luke’s clone slowly swallowed.
The System released another pitying sigh beside him.
[Sigh, it seems your main body is going to face the wrath of your fiery dragon wife very soon.]
“Aurielle, why is Luke’s clone here?!”

Meanwhile, the person responsible for this entire situation was doing something considerably less impressive.
Luke’s clone was hiding behind the corner of a building several streets away, carefully leaning his head past the stone wall while watching everything unfolding above.
More strangely, he wasn’t peeking alone.

If the System possessed a visible spirit body that ordinary people could actually see, they would have witnessed an extremely questionable scene of one grown man and one small spirit-like existence leaning around the same corner while secretly watching the confrontation.
Luke’s clone suddenly paused.
‘System?’
He slowly turned his head toward the familiar presence beside him before staring with obvious confusion.
“Wait, why are you here?
Weren’t you with the main body?”

The question was reasonable, because Luke’s clones couldn’t actually use the System themselves, while only the original Luke possessed proper access to it, which meant the System normally spent nearly all of its time accompanying the main body.
Seeing it voluntarily appear beside a clone was definitely new.
The System remained suspiciously silent.
Luke’s clone stared at it for another moment before his expression gradually changed with realization.
“Let me guess.”
He leaned slightly closer while keeping his voice low enough that no one nearby could hear them.
“The main body is flying back alone right now, which means there isn’t a single woman, princess, queen, lover, or wife anywhere near him.”
“But here, there are two wives, a lover, and several other women standing around while they’re about to start fighting over him.”
The System still didn’t answer.
Luke’s clone pointed an accusing finger toward it.
“So you abandoned the main body and came here because you wanted to watch the fun.”
He paused before adding with complete certainty, “Am I right, you horny System?”

Luke’s accusation was uncomfortably close to the truth, but the System had long since achieved something resembling a PhD in shamelessness, so expecting it to admit anything was clearly asking too much.
[The System chooses its right to remain silent. ( ̄ー ̄)]
Luke’s clone stared at the message for several seconds, temporarily unable to think of anything capable of matching that level of shamelessness.

“Maybe?”

I mean, the second day after I arrived here, when she subdued me without any effort and carried me away like a sack of potatoes?”

You are not welcome here!”
